new_roles.title: Senior Director of Quality, Compliance and Risk
new_roles.description:
**New England Village**

**Position:** Senior Director of Quality, Compliance and Risk

**Location:** Pembroke, MA 02359 (on-site)

**Salary:** $105,000-$120,000 annually

**Position Summary**

New England Village is seeking an experienced Senior Director of Quality, Compliance & Risk to provide organization-wide leadership for quality management, regulatory compliance, risk management, accreditation readiness, policy governance, and continuous improvement.

This is a senior leadership role for a professional with substantial prior experience in quality management and regulatory compliance within a complex, highly regulated environment. The successful candidate will bring demonstrated experience leading quality and/or compliance functions and building systems that translate regulatory requirements, organizational findings, data, and risk into measurable and sustainable improvement.

The Senior Director works across programs and support departments to promote consistent standards, effective monitoring, clear accountability, regulatory readiness, and continuous improvement. Department leaders remain responsible for the quality, compliance, and performance of their respective areas, while the Senior Director provides the organizational framework, oversight, consultation, analysis, and escalation necessary to support enterprise accountability.

The Senior Director serves as New England Village's designated Compliance Officer, directly supervises the Director of Program Improvements & Supports and the Director of Program Implementation & Practice, and serves as a member of the Senior Leadership Team.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Lead and continuously strengthen the organization's quality management framework, including the Quality Management Plan, performance indicators, monitoring systems, trend analysis, corrective action, and continuous improvement.
* Serve as the organization's Compliance Officer and lead the continued development, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of a formal enterprise compliance program.
* Maintain organizational readiness for licensing, accreditation, regulatory reviews, audits, surveys, investigations, inspections, and other external reviews.
* Establish and oversee effective approaches to internal quality and compliance review, risk assessment, root-cause analysis, corrective action, monitoring, and verification that improvements are sustained.
* Develop and maintain an organizational approach to identifying, assessing, mitigating, monitoring, and escalating significant regulatory, service, health and safety, privacy, financial, operational, and organizational risks.
* Analyze incidents, complaints, investigations, audit findings, corrective actions, regulatory findings, performance measures, and other data to identify patterns, systemic concerns, recurring issues, and emerging risks
* Lead and support effective policy and procedure governance, ensuring regulatory and organizational requirements are translated into practical and sustainable operations.
* Ensure significant findings result in meaningful corrective and improvement actions, with assigned accountability, measurable outcomes, follow-up, and evidence of effectiveness.
* Provide leadership and professional development to functions responsible for quality assessment, compliance monitoring, program improvement, implementation support, training, and practice fidelity.
* Work collaboratively with program and support leaders while maintaining the independence and objectivity necessary to identify concerns, challenge practices, and escalate significant or unresolved risk.
* Monitor changes in applicable regulatory and funding requirements and coordinate appropriate changes to policies, procedures, systems, training, monitoring, and organizational practices.
* Provide clear analysis, reporting, and recommendations regarding significant quality, compliance, regulatory, and risk matters to senior and executive leadership and designated Board committees.

**Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in human services, healthcare administration, quality management, compliance, public administration, or a related field required; master's degree preferred.
* Minimum of seven years of progressively responsible experience in human services, healthcare, behavioral health, Medicaid-funded services, or a comparable highly regulated environment, including at least five years with significant responsibility for quality management, regulatory compliance, risk management, accreditation, or related organizational assurance functions.
* At least three years of progressive leadership experience, preferably including supervision of managers, senior professionals, or multidisciplinary functions.
* Knowledge of Massachusetts DDS and MassHealth requirements, with direct experience in IDD or comparable Massachusetts human services strongly preferred.
* Demonstrated experience leading a quality and/or compliance function, with responsibility for activities such as regulatory monitoring, internal review or audit, corrective action, quality improvement, investigations, risk assessment, or accreditation/licensing readiness.
* Demonstrated experience developing and operating formal quality or compliance systems, including monitoring plans, audit/review processes, corrective-action systems, quality measures, risk tracking, policies and procedures, and reporting to senior leadership.
* Demonstrated experience preparing an organization for licensing, accreditation, regulatory audits, surveys, investigations, or external reviews, including responding to findings and monitoring corrective actions through resolution.
* Demonstrated ability to analyze quality, compliance, incident, and operational data; identify systemic or recurring issues; conduct or guide root-cause analysis; and translate findings into measurable improvement.

new_roles.title: VP, Manufacturing - Fresh Bakery
new_roles.description:
**Since 1869, we've connected people through food they love. We’re proud to be stewards of amazing brands that people trust. Our portfolio includes the iconic Campbell’s brand, as well as Cape Cod, Chunky, Goldfish, Kettle Brand, Lance, Late July, Pacific Foods, Pepperidge Farm, Prego, Pace, Rao’s Homemade, Snack Factory, Snyder’s of Hanover. Swanson, and V8.**

**Here, you will make a difference every day. You will be supported to build a rewarding career with opportunities to grow, innovate and inspire. Make history with us.**

**Why Campbell’s…**

* Benefits begin on day one and include medical, dental, short and long-term disability, AD&D, and life insurance (for individual, families, and domestic partners).
* Employees are eligible for our matching 401(k) plan and can enroll on the first day of employment with immediate vesting.
* Campbell’s offers unlimited sick time along with paid time off and holiday pay.
* If in WHQ – free access to the fitness center. Access to on-site day care (operated by Bright Horizons) and company store.
* Giving back to the communities where our employees work and live is very important to Campbell’s. Our “Campbell’s Cares” program matches employee donations and/or volunteer activity up to $1,500 annually.
* Campbell’s has a variety of Employee Resource Groups (ERGs) to support employees.

**Job Description**

The Vice President, Manufacturing – Fresh Bakery provides strategic and operational leadership for Campbell’s Fresh Bakery manufacturing network, including bakery operations in Bloomfield, Connecticut; Downers Grove, Illinois; Lakeland, Florida; and Denver, Pennsylvania. This leader establishes the manufacturing strategy, operating priorities, performance expectations, and transformation agenda for the network, ensuring consistent execution across safety, quality, service, cost, reliability, productivity, and people.

Leading through the Plant Managers, the VP creates alignment across sites while maintaining clear site-level accountability for day-to-day operations and results. The role builds manufacturing capability and organizational talent across the network, identifies and addresses systemic performance opportunities, and drives continuous improvement and transformation to strengthen the long-term competitiveness of the Fresh Bakery business.

This leader partners across Supply Chain and the broader organization to align manufacturing strategy, capabilities, capacity, capital priorities, and resources with business needs. The incumbent must be an enterprise-minded business partner who creates direction, enables effective decisions, builds talent and culture, drives disciplined execution, and owns results across the network.

**Essential Job Duties**

**Manufacturing Strategy & Network Leadership:** Define and lead the multi-year manufacturing strategy for the Fresh Bakery network. Translate business and Supply Chain priorities into clear site objectives, integrated roadmaps, operating plans, and performance expectations. Maintain clarity between network-level strategic direction and Plant Manager ownership of daily site operations.

**Safety, Quality & Operating Integrity:** Set expectations and governance for employee safety, food safety, product quality, environmental responsibility, and regulatory compliance across all bakery sites. Ensure effective management systems, standards, controls, and escalation routines are in place, while holding Plant Managers accountable for site execution and results.

**Network Performance Management & Accountability:** Establish the operating cadence and performance-management system for safety, quality, service, cost, labor, yield, waste, reliability, customer service, and employee engagement. Review performance across sites, identify systemic gaps and best practices, define corrective actions, and ensure clear ownership and follow-through.

**Manufacturing Transformation & Operational Excellence:** Lead the transformation agenda for Fresh Bakery manufacturing, creating consistent operating systems, standards, and management routines across the network. Build a culture of continuous improvement and zero loss, and use Lean Manufacturing, Total Productive Maintenance, equipment reliability, and problem-solving disciplines to deliver sustainable improvements.

**Cost, Productivity & Business Performance:** Deliver network productivity, cost, waste, and efficiency commitments through disciplined planning and execution. Connect operational performance to financial outcomes, evaluate trade-offs, and mobilize cross-site resources to address significant performance gaps or opportunities.

**Capacity, Capability & Capital Strategy:** Shape network capacity, capability, technology, and capital priorities based on demand, growth, service, risk, and long-term business needs. Sponsor major capital and capability initiatives, ensure disciplined prioritization and governance, and partner with Engineering and other functions to achieve intended business outcomes.

**Talent, Leadership & Culture%:** Build a strong and diverse manufacturing leadership pipeline across the Fresh Bakery network. Coach and develop Plant Managers and senior site leaders; strengthen succession, bench strength, workforce planning, engagement, and retention; and create a high-performing culture grounded in accountability, collaboration, inclusion, and continuous improvement.

**Cross-Functional & Enterprise Partnership:** Partner with Planning, Procurement, Engineering, Quality, Logistics, Research & Development, Commercial, Finance, People & Culture, and other stakeholders to align priorities, solve network constraints, support innovation and commercialization, manage risk, and deliver enterprise outcomes. Serve as the senior manufacturing voice for the Fresh Bakery business.

**Required Education & Skills**

· Bachelor's degree strongly preferred or an Associate's degree with significant experience.

· Fresh Bakery manufacturing experience strongly preferred

· 15+ years of progressive manufacturing/operations experience

· Prior experience as a Plant Manager, General Manager, Director of Site Operations, or comparable senior manufacturing leader

· Significant people leadership experience, including leadership of senior operational leaders

· Demonstrated manufacturing leadership experience

· Multi-site leadership experience, likely something I'd make required or strongly preferred

**Preferred Experienc** e

· Multi-site manufacturing leadership experience, including leadership through Plant Managers or comparable senior site leaders.

· Experience in food manufacturing or consumer packaged goods (CPG) within a complex, high-volume manufacturing network.

· Demonstrated experience leading large-scale manufacturing transformation and operational excellence, with a track record of driving sustainable improvements in safety, quality, service, cost, reliability, and productivity.

· Experience applying Lean Manufacturing, Total Productive Maintenance (TPM), reliability, Six Sigma, or other continuous improvement methodologies at scale.

· Experience developing manufacturing network strategy, including capacity, asset utilization, capital investment, and long-term capability planning.

· Demonstrated experience developing senior manufacturing leaders and building succession and bench strength across multiple operations.

· Experience managing significant operating budgets, productivity commitments, capital investments, and/or P&L responsibility.

· Strong business acumen and demonstrated ability to work across Planning, Engineering, Quality, Logistics, Procurement, Finance, Commercial, R&D, and People & Culture to deliver business outcomes.

· Advanced degree in Business, Engineering, Operations, Supply Chain, or a related field preferred.

**Physical Requirements**

This role requires regular work in manufacturing environments and a visible presence across bakery facilities, including walking, standing, climbing stairs, and accessing production, warehouse, and office areas. The incumbent must be able to wear required personal protective equipment and work a flexible schedule as business needs require.

**Travel**

This role requires **at least 75% travel** , primarily to Campbell’s Fresh Bakery manufacturing sites and Headquarters. Regular and sustained on-site presence is expected to provide visible leadership, build strong partnerships with Plant Managers and site leadership teams, understand operating conditions firsthand, and support execution of manufacturing priorities and transformation initiatives

 

**Compensation and Benefits:**

The target base salary range for this full-time, salaried position is between

$221,500-$304,600

Individual base pay depends on work location and additional factors such as experience, job-related skills, and relevant education or training. Total pay may include other forms of compensation. In addition, we offer competitive health, dental, 401k and wellness benefits beginning on the first day of employment. Please ask your Talent Acquisition Partner for more information about our total rewards package.

**The Company is committed to providing equal opportunity for employees and qualified applicants in all aspects of the employment relationship, including consideration for employment, without regard to race, color, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, citizenship, marital status, protected veteran status, disability, age, religion, or any other classification protected by law.**

new_roles.title: Senior Director, Operations
new_roles.description:
We’re looking for people who put their innovation to work to advance our success – and their own. Join an organization that ensures a more secure world through connecting and protecting our customers with inventive electrical solutions.

The Senior Director, Operations is a strategic operations leadership role responsible for scaling a $1.5B+ manufacturing campus and multi-site footprint through digital transformation, operational excellence, and high-impact leadership to enable accelerated growth and customer value. While this role carries responsibility for long-term operational strategy, digital transformation, capacity planning, and Smart Factory initiatives, the immediate mandate is centered on stabilizing and transforming one of nVent's most important manufacturing operations globally. The Anoka campus represents approximately $1.5 billion in annual revenue and employs roughly 1,700 people today, with expected growth toward 2,000 employees in the coming years. It is the largest manufacturing operation in the United States and the second-largest globally within nVent's manufacturing network.

 

Reporting directly to the Vice President, Integrated Supply Chain of the Systems Protection Segment, this role will have significant visibility across the organization and will play a critical role in shaping the future operating model of one of nVent's most strategically important manufacturing assets. Success in this role will create meaningful opportunities for broader enterprise leadership responsibility within nVent's global Integrated Supply Chain organization.

 

Key Responsibilities:

* Champion a high-performance continuous improvement culture by embedding Lean and problem-solving disciplines across all levels of the organization; empower employees to identify waste, implement solutions, and deliver sustainable gains while formally recognizing exceptional performance and contributions.
* Lead large-scale, multi-site operational transformation across a large scaled flagship campus and additional high-growth plants, ensuring alignment of capacity, capability, and talent strategies to support accelerated business growth and evolving customer demand.
* Drive Smart Factory / Digital Manufacturing advancement by scaling production capability through strategic investments in automation, advanced tooling, equipment, and data-driven systems (Industry 4.0), while balancing legacy operations with next-generation technologies to optimize throughput, quality, and cost.
* Own end-to-end operational performance across Operations, Procurement, Manufacturing Engineering, Quality, Environmental Health & Safety (EHS), Facilities, Material Handling, and Business Support functions, ensuring disciplined execution against safety, quality, delivery, cost, and cash flow objectives
* Develop and execute integrated strategic business plans that translate enterprise objectives into site-level actions, including long-range capacity planning, capital deployment (CapEx), workforce strategy, and footprint optimization across multiple locations.
* Serve as a key leader and cross-functional partner, collaborating with senior leadership, supply chain, engineering, and commercial teams to align short- and long-term operational strategies, remove constraints, and ensure successful new product introductions and business expansion.
* Lead, coach, and inspire a large, diverse organization by building strong leadership benches, strengthening succession pipelines, and fostering accountability, engagement, and inclusion across all functions and sites.
* Leverage data and operational analytics to drive decision-making, identifying bottlenecks, improving asset utilization (OEE), optimizing material flow, and prioritizing high-impact investments that enable scalability and profitability.
* Establish robust communication channels and employee engagement mechanisms to proactively monitor organizational health, gather feedback, and address concerns in partnership with Human Resources—ensuring a strong, transparent, and trust-based culture across all locations.
* Ensure world-class safety, compliance, and sustainability performance, reinforcing a zero-harm culture while maintaining adherence to environmental regulations, responsible sourcing practices, and corporate governance standards.
* Establish and sustain a rigorous management operating system across the campus, including daily management, tiered accountability processes, visual management, structured problem solving, and disciplined escalation practices that enable rapid identification and resolution of operational issues.
* Drive stabilization and performance improvement initiatives across critical manufacturing lines, ensuring achievement of safety, quality, delivery, and productivity commitments while restoring operational predictability and customer confidence.
* Lead the continued development of a high-performance culture rooted in accountability, transparency, problem solving, and employee engagement, creating an environment where issues are surfaced early, addressed rapidly, and solved at their root cause.
* Evaluate and optimize material flow, production layout, workforce deployment, and capacity utilization across the campus, balancing immediate operational needs with long-term scalability requirements.
Partner closely with Quality, Engineering, Supply Chain, Lean, Human Resources, and Finance leaders to strengthen organizational capability, improve execution, and ensure alignment around operational priorities and business objectives. 

 

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS & ABILITIES:

* The ideal candidate will bring a BA or BS degree in Business, Engineering or similar field; MBA or other graduate degree is preferred.
* Deep understanding of lean manufacturing, Six Sigma, and continuous improvement methodologies (TPM, Kaizen) within high-volume environments.
* Strong command of Smart Factory technologies, including IoT integration, predictive maintenance, automated material handling, and data-driven shop floor management.
* Comprehensive knowledge of EHS (Environmental, Health, and Safety) compliance, supply chain logistics, strategic procurement, and capital expenditure (CapEx) management.
* Expertise in long-range capacity planning, workforce strategy, and balancing the operational requirements of legacy product lines with the agility needed for new product introductions (NPI).
* Proficiency in P&L management, budget forecasting, and aligning plant-level performance metrics with enterprise-wide financial objectives.
* Ability to translate corporate strategy into actionable site-level plans and orchestrate cross-functional teams toward common goals.
* Demonstrated success in leading large-scale cultural and technical shifts, including the transition to digital manufacturing environments while maintaining stable output.
* Skill in leveraging operational analytics to identify bottlenecks, optimize production capability, and justify capital investments.
* Exceptional ability to foster open, transparent communication across all levels—from the shop floor to the executive boardroom—and effectively partner with Human Resources on organizational health.
* Proven ability to build, mentor, and inspire high-performing teams, fostering an environment of psychological safety and professional growth.
* Ability to navigate complex matrix organizations and collaborate effectively with stakeholders in Sales, Engineering, Finance, and HR to execute short- and long-term plans.
* Capacity to remain decisive and calm under pressure, managing the competing demands of high-growth production spikes, technical troubleshooting, and daily operational hurdles.•Ability to balance immediate, reactive operational needs with long-term, proactive improvements in infrastructure, tooling, and site facilities.
* Aptitude for cultivating a high-engagement, inclusive workplace that promotes active employee participation in problem-solving and recognizes performance excellence.

**WE HAVE:**

* A dynamic global reach with diverse operations around the world that will stretch your abilities, provide plentiful career opportunities, and allow you to make an impact every day

 + nVent is a leading global provider of electrical connection and protection solutions. We believe our inventive electrical solutions enable safer systems and ensure a more secure world. We design, manufacture, market, install and service high performance products and solutions that connect and protect some of the world's most sensitive equipment, buildings and critical processes. We offer a comprehensive range of systems protection and electrical connections solutions across industry-leading brands that are recognized globally for quality, reliability and innovation.
 + Our principal office is in London and our management office in the United States is in Minneapolis. Our robust portfolio of leading electrical product brands dates back more than 100 years and includes nVent CADDY, ERICO, HOFFMAN, ILSCO, SCHROFF and TRACHTE. Learn more at www.nvent.com .

* Commitment to strengthen communities where our employees live and work

 + We encourage and support the philanthropic activities of our employees worldwide
 + Through our nVent in Action matching program, we provide funds to nonprofit and educational organizations where our employees volunteer or donate money

* Core values that shape our culture and drive us to deliver the best for our employees and our customers. We’re known for being:

 + Innovative & adaptable
 + Dedicated to absolute integrity
 + Focused on the customer first
 + Respectful and team oriented
 + Optimistic and energizing
 + Accountable for performance

* Benefits to support the lives of our employees

**Pay Transparency** 
 
nVent’s pay scale is based on the expected range of base pay for this job and the employee’s work location. Employee pay within this range will be based on a combination of factors including knowledge, skills, abilities, experience, education, and performance. Where federal, state, or local minimum wage requirements exist, employee pay will comply.
 
 
**Compensation Range:**

$204,400.00 - $304,000.00

Depending on the position offered, employee may be eligible for other forms of compensation, such as annual incentives.

**Benefit Overview**

At nVent, we value our people and their health and well-being. We provide a broad benefits package with meaningful programs for eligible full-time employees that includes:

* Medical, dental, and vision plans along with flexible spending accounts, short-term and long-term disability benefits, critical illness, accident insurance and life insurance.
* A 401(k) retirement plan and an employee stock purchase plan — both include a company match.
* Other supplemental benefits may include tuition reimbursement, caregiver, personal and parental leave, back-up care services, paid time off including volunteer time, a well-being program, and/or legal & identity theft protection.

At nVent, we connect and protect our customers with inventive electrical solutions. People are our most valuable asset. Inclusion and diversity means that we celebrate and encourage each other’s authenticity because we understand that uniqueness sparks growth.

For more than 65 years, we've turned big ideas into solutions that help protect homes, strengthen businesses and build a more resilient, efficient, sustainable energy future.

Ready to Power a Smarter World with us?

**Sr Director, Operations Engineering**
=======================================

The Sr Director, Operations Engineering is responsible for leading the enterprise Operations Engineering function with a focus on New Product Launches, Operations Integrations, Product Moves, and Operations Standards. This role ensures that new products, newly integrated operations, and transferred products are launched and sustained in manufacturing safely, on time, at quality, and at target cost. Through the development and deployment of enterprise standards, best practices, and the Generac Fulfillment System (GFS), the Director drives consistent, world-class execution across the Order-to-Cash process (Plan, Source, Make, Deliver & Service). The role partners closely with Engineering, Advanced Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Quality, Finance, HR, and Business Unit leadership, and supports Generac's global manufacturing portfolio.

**Major Responsibilities**
--------------------------

### **New Product Launches (NPI)**

* Lead and coordinate the successful launch of New Product Introductions (NPI) within operations, from early design involvement through production ramp and sustained performance.
* Ensure manufacturing readiness for new products, including process design, PFMEA, line layout, tooling, fixtures, work instructions, and capacity planning.
* Partner with Product Engineering to drive design for manufacturability and assembly so new products launch with optimal cost, quality, and delivery.
* Establish launch gates, readiness criteria, and success metrics, and hold cross-functional teams accountable to them.
* Lead and support the introduction of new and revised processes and technologies that support cost reduction and competitive advantage.

### **Operations Integrations**

* Lead the operational integration of new sites, acquisitions, and expanded capacity into the Generac manufacturing network, aligning processes, systems, and performance expectations.
* Lead and contribute to facility transformation, including layout, mixed-model lines, value stream design, and deployment of the Generac Fulfillment System (GFS).
* Assess integrated facilities, infrastructure systems, and technology against best-in-class capability and develop roadmaps to close gaps.
* Coordinate cross-functional collaboration with HR, Finance, Engineering, Supply Chain, Quality, and senior leadership to ensure integrations meet business objectives.
* Incorporate workplace optimization, space planning, and long-term facility planning into integration plans.

### **Product Moves & Transfers**

* Lead the planning and execution of product moves and technology transfers between facilities and with external supply chain partners, ensuring continuity of supply, quality, and cost.
* Own and continuously improve the product transfer procedure, and support the Operations Product Transfer Steering Committee to ensure alignment and adherence to the procedure.
* Develop transfer plans that include capacity validation, equipment and tooling relocation, process validation, training, and inventory bridge strategies.
* Partner with Business Unit and Manufacturing Strategy leaders to support footprint, rebalancing, and new capacity decisions with sound operations engineering analysis.

### **Operations Standards**

* Develop with corporate Advanced Manufacturing, deploy, and sustain enterprise operations engineering standards, policies, procedures, and process documentation that drive consistent execution across all facilities.
* Drive significant contributions to the implementation of the Generac Fulfillment System (GFS) across the Order-to-Cash process.
* Develop and implement operating methodologies designed to maximize floor space utilization, asset uptime and utilization, eliminate waste, and reduce operating cost.
* Champion lean principles and continuous improvement, and ensure the ongoing success of process improvement initiatives.
* Establish and monitor KPIs to evaluate productivity, engineering output, launch performance, and facility efficiency, using data to drive improvement.
* Ensure compliance with safety, quality, and environmental standards, and incorporate sustainability and energy efficiency initiatives.

### **Project Management & Financial Stewardship**

* Drive and project manage major cost, quality, and delivery initiatives, with a strong focus on breakthrough process and technology improvements.
* Facilitate project flow through regular engagement with engineering, manufacturing, and other cross-functional teams, managing shifting priorities and deadlines in a fast-paced environment.
* Oversee capital projects related to launches, integrations, and product moves, and provide budgetary figures for future fiscal year planning.
* Manage the operations engineering budget and support reduction of the operating cost of each facility consistent with company objectives.

### **Leadership & Talent Development**

* Lead the Operations Engineering team, including project planning, technical guidance, and resource allocation across sites and initiatives.
* Select, coach, and develop a high-performing team of engineers and project managers, setting objectives that align with company strategy.
* Manage organizational talent through performance management, succession planning, and development, ensuring feedback is consistently delivered and performance is systematically improved.
* Provide guidance to cross-functional teams and leadership on key decisions related to investment in core manufacturing technologies, processes, and systems.

**Minimum Job Requirements**
----------------------------

* **Education:** Bachelor's Degree in Engineering (Mechanical, Electrical, or Industrial) or Industrial Technology.
* **Work Experience:** 10+ years of related experience in Operations Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, and Production, including leading new product launches and product transfers.
* **Leadership Experience:** 5+ years of increasing responsibility for project and/or people management involving a broad range of operational technologies and processes.

**Knowledge / Skills / Abilities**
----------------------------------

* Strong knowledge of New Product Development, PFMEA, and operations engineering principles.
* Knowledge of lean principles, continuous improvement, and end-to-end supply chain principles.
* Experience operating in both high-mix, low-volume and high-volume, low-mix production environments.
* Ability to assess and manage end-to-end processes and to manage strategic and tactical issues by being hands-on.
* Ability to develop and deploy standards and best practices across multiple sites.
* Ability to attract, develop, and manage an impactful team.
* Demonstrated skills in problem solving, conflict resolution, and cross-functional collaboration.
* Excellent organizational, written, and oral communication skills, including the ability to influence senior leadership.
* Proven ability to prioritize multiple projects with shifting priorities and moving deadlines.
* Proficiency in a CAD platform (AutoCAD, SolidWorks, and/or ProE), MS Office, and ERP platforms.

**Preferred Job Requirements**
------------------------------

* Master's Degree in Mechanical, Electrical, or Industrial Engineering.
* Project Management certification (e.g., PMP).
* Experience deploying processes and standards at an enterprise level, both internally and with external supply chain partners.
* Experience leading operations integrations, facility transformations, and multi-site product transfers.
* Experience working in an international company and in matrix organizations, with multi-site support experience.
* Previous experience using SAP or an equivalent ERP.
* Experience with facilities engineering and with using and/or implementing CMMS systems.
* Large-scale project management experience.

new_roles.title: Director, Merchandising Operations
new_roles.description:
Parachute Health is transforming post-acute care as the leading digital ordering platform for medical equipment and supplies. We connect major health systems, health plans, and suppliers to help patients get the life-saving products they need at home. Since launching, we've connected 300,000+ clinicians and 3,000+ supplier locations across all 50 states and helped 15M+ patients. What started as a DME ePrescribing tool has become the order management platform of choice for home medical equipment.

Join our team and make a difference in patient care.

### **About the Role**

Parachute Health is building the definitive platform for ordering home medical equipment and supplies, helping clinicians and suppliers ensure that millions of patients each year receive the critical equipment and supplies they need. Our Merchandising Operations team (AKA "Merch") comprises Category Managers and Category Analysts who have three primary jobs: 1) build and maintain our catalog, 2) build and maintain our coverage criteria rules engine, and 3) partner with R&D to improve the tools and workflows behind both. Merch sits at the intersection of e-commerce, compliance, operations, and R&D, and its work is central to Parachute's core functionality. Clinicians use our catalog to find and order the right equipment for their patients, and suppliers rely on it to fulfill those orders. Our coverage criteria help users determine whether an item should be covered by the patient's insurance.

The Merch team's work is nuanced and detail-dense: we maintain information on tens of thousands of products so our software, and the people who use it, can rely on it. The 18-person team splits its time between project work, like building and redesigning product categories and turning payer rules into qualification questions, and ticket-based work, resolving complex requests escalated by our support and partner teams. Our work requires efficient operational processes and excellent documentation.

As Director of Merchandising Operations, you will own the team's operating framework: how work is planned, prioritized, and delivered, and how the team partners with other teams across Parachute. You'll coach and develop a mix of managers and individual contributors, lead the team's largest cross-functional projects, and serve as a close thought partner to the SVP of Merchandising.

The role is primarily internal (roughly 90%), with occasional customer communication, especially on escalations, that calls for a steady, polished hand.

### **What You'll Do**

* Be the operational leader for a highly motivated, highly capable team of managers and individual contributors: keep work running smoothly, protect morale, and learn and add to a team culture that is already strong.
* Drive key projects: stay close to the work and personally drive the team's largest, most complex projects, including timelines, dependencies, and cross-team communication.
* Know every team process end to end. Lead the creation, maintenance, and centralization of SOPs and shared resources; drive consistent practices, training, quality assurance, and continuous improvement across category teams.
* Collaborate with partner teams (e.g., Supplier Implementation, Product, Customer Success) so handoffs and shared processes run smoothly.
* Be a Merch advocate: make the team's work understandable and visible across the company.
* Run bandwidth and capacity planning; flag risks early and rebalance coverage.
* Define and report on team metrics (ticket throughput, SLAs, SKU work, rollout milestones).
* Own escalations as needed, partnering effectively with people at all levels across the organization.
* Support recruiting as needed, own onboarding for new merchants, and maintain continuity coverage for every category.

### **Requirements**

* 7+ years in operations, program delivery, or management or technology consulting (e.g., a Big Four or top-tier firm), with 3+ years managing and growing managers.
* Track record of delivering complex, cross-functional projects using a clear, repeatable methodology.
* Data-driven: comfortable with capacity models, dashboards and prioritization trade-offs.
* Willingness to travel roughly once a quarter.

### **More About You**

* Passionate about improving patient outcomes in the healthcare space.
* Gets things done: drives work to completion and builds processes that stick.
* Thrives in complex, nuanced domains; quickly learns intricate systems (e.g., insurance coverage rules, product data) well enough to make sound calls.
* Clear, concise communicator who pushes back constructively and drives decisions.
* Sound compliance judgment: in a highly regulated industry, you know which issues to resolve and which to escalate.
* Track record of growing into increasing scope and responsibility.
* Nice to have: catalog, product data or e-commerce experience; healthcare, DME/HME or payer experience.

### **Benefits**

* Medical, Dental, and Vision Coverage: Comprehensive plans with options for low-to-no-cost premiums
* Employer HSA Contribution: Company-funded contributions to your Health Savings Account
* 401(k) Retirement Plan
* Equity Incentive Plan
* Annual Company-Wide Bonus: Opportunity for up to 15% bonus based on company performance
* Remote-First Culture: We are remote-first with a dedicated NYC office and reimbursement options for co-working spaces
* Flexible Vacation Policy
* Summer Fridays: 5 additional Fridays off during the summer (separate from PTO)
* Home Office and Wellness Stipend
* Monthly Internet Stipend
* Annual Learning and Development Stipend

### **Base Salary Range (based on level and experience)**

$145,000-$180,000

new_roles.description:
United States - Remote

JOB ID: R-259392 LOCATION: United States - Remote WORK LOCATION TYPE: Remote DATE POSTED: Nov. 02, 2026 CATEGORY: Clinical SALARY RANGE: -

**Join Amgen’s Mission of Serving Patients**
--------------------------------------------

At Amgen, if you feel like you’re part of something bigger, it’s because you are. Our shared mission—to serve patients living with serious illnesses—drives all that we do.

Since 1980, we’ve helped pioneer the world of biotech in our fight against the world’s toughest diseases. Amgen is advancing a broad and deep pipeline and portfolio of medicines to treat heart disease, obesity and obesity-related conditions, rare diseases, inflammatory conditions and cancer. As a member of the Amgen team, you’ll help make a lasting impact on the lives of patients as we research, manufacture, and deliver innovative medicines to help people live longer, fuller happier lives.

Our award-winning culture is collaborative, innovative, and science based. If you have a passion for challenges and the opportunities that lay within them, you’ll thrive as part of the Amgen team. Join us and transform the lives of patients while transforming your career.

 
 
 

**Local Study Operations Manager (LSOM), Director**
---------------------------------------------------

**What you will do**
--------------------

Let’s do this. Let’s change the world. In this vital role you will provide strategic and operational leadership for the country LSOM organization and is accountable for the quality, timeliness, cost, and compliant execution of the country clinical study portfolio. The role achieves results through LSOM Senior Managers and their FTE and FSP teams, translating global clinical development strategy into country operating priorities. The role directs portfolio delivery, resource and capacity strategy, financial planning, quality and risk management, vendor performance, and inspection readiness from feasibility through study close-out. As a member of the country leadership team, this role influences study placement and portfolio decisions, leads the resolution of significant operational issues, develops organizational capability and succession plans, and represents LSOM operations in country, regional, and global governance forums.

 
 

**Accountabilities**

* Lead the successful delivery of the country study portfolio through the LSOM management organization, ensuring alignment with global clinical development priorities.

* Provides strategic direction and leadership to LSOM country organization across the full study lifecycle, including feasibility, study execution, and study close-out.

* Establishes portfolio-level oversight of delivery, quality, risk, timelines, and performance, directing timely escalation and resolution of critical issues for LSOM management organization.

* Manage LSOM and LSOM vendor performance to guarantee high-quality study execution, serving as the primary escalation point for local study challenges, driving solutions, and ensuring portfolio targets are met within the country.

* Build leadership capability within the LSOM organization through targeted coaching, development, and succession planning, preparing LSOMs to lead increasingly complex trials and programs.

* Establishes strong operating partnerships with Clinical Research Associate (CRA) organization to support study start-up, monitoring, issue resolution, and compliant trial execution across the country portfolio.

* Cultivate a high-performing, accountable, and inclusive organization focused on operational excellence and continuous improvement.

* Champion strong integration between study strategy and local execution teams to translate portfolio priorities into effective country-level delivery.

* Strengthen cross-functional alignment and accountability across country teams to accelerate execution and deliver portfolio commitments.

* Influences study-placement and portfolio investment decisions by providing strategic insight into country's capabilities, operational readiness, performance, and growth potential.

* Anticipates portfolio-level delivery risks, quality trends, and evolving resource requirements, directing mitigation strategies and systemic improvements across country operations.

* Sponsor initiatives that advance operational efficiency, digital innovation, organizational capability, and the adoption of leading practices.

* Direct resource strategy, capacity planning, and workload allocation across FSP and FTE LSOM teams to optimize execution and align resources with global priorities.

* Ensure compliance with applicable regulatory, GCP, ICH, and organizational standards across the country's study portfolio.

Partner with the Regional Head/Country Head and senior cross-functional stakeholders to align priorities, establish accountability for trial deliverables, and resolve significant escalations. 



**Responsibilities**

* Serve as the functional leader for LSOM Senior Managers and the broader LSOM team, including both FSP and FTE, to optimize trial execution and align with global priorities. including strategy and execution, managing risks and escalations

* Partners closely with CRAs, CSPO, Quality, and FSP partners.

* Leads the coordination among country functional teams to ensure successful delivery of the country portfolio.

* Ensure inspection readiness and provide hands-on support during inspections, including responsibility for storyboards.

* Sponsors continuous operational improvement initiatives and encourage sharing of best practices.

* Ensure compliance with relevant regulatory and quality standards.

* Collaborate with the Regional Head/Country Head to engage cross-functional stakeholders, align on trial deliverables, and manage escalations as needed.

**Capability Building and People Leadership**

* Lead, coach, and develop LSOM Sr Managers, including performance management, succession planning, and leadership bench development.

* Build the organizational capabilities, resourcing needed to meet the current and future regional portfolio requirements.

* Foster a high-performing, inclusive, accountable, and patient-focused culture across geographically distributed teams.

* Lead organizational changes and enable adoption of new operating models, technologies

**Authority**

* Accountable for country level oversight and delivery of clinical trials.

* Manage the performance of LSOM Senior Managers and their teams

* Holds line management authority for regional and country operations leaders, including performance management, talent development, succession planning, and capability building.

* Sets regional delivery goals, operating expectations, and performance standards across study start-up, site engagement, monitoring, execution, and closeout.

* Capability build, talent and performance management, and acting as a liaison for cultural differences within region.

**Outputs**

* Manage LSOM resources in accordance with the global study strategy.

* Oversee resource allocation and workload balance across LSOMs.

* Handle FSP supplier resource coordination and monitor performance through quality oversight metrics.

**Role Overview:**

We are seeking a high-caliber, transformative **Director of Operations** to lead, scale, and optimize our operations. new_roles.title: Field Operations Director
new_roles.description:
### **The Position**

From the beginning, Genentech has been a team of highly dedicated, passionate individuals. We are a place where people are united around a single purpose and an ambitious vision. Together, we aspire to deliver ever better health outcomes for patients while lowering overall healthcare costs. Our goal is to compel the customer to act on behalf of their patients while showing great commitment to the rare disease community, whose support is key. Utilizing innovative methods to identify patients who may benefit from treatment, we must take a highly strategic approach to patient access while assisting patients and their caregivers to navigate the healthcare system.

POSITION SUMMARY

The Field Operations Director serves as the trusted operations partner to an assigned Regional VP or National Team VP and their leadership team, helping translate business priorities into clear plans, coordinated execution, and effective connection to the broader CE Operations and enterprise support network. The Director owns the operating rhythm and priority agenda for the assigned leadership team and provides a single point of connectivity between Field Leadership and the broader operational ecosystem.

SCOPE & KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Strategic Partnership with Field Leadership

* Serve as the primary Operations partner to an assigned Regional VP or National Team VP and their leadership team.
* Develop a deep understanding of the team's business priorities, customers, opportunities, challenges, and performance.
* Translate enterprise and CE priorities into clear implications and action plans for the assigned Region or National Team.
* Provide strategic and operational counsel to leadership and proactively identify issues requiring attention, decisions, or escalation.
* Help leadership prioritize competing needs and maintain focus on the highest-impact business opportunities.

Operating Rhythm & Business Planning

* Own the operating rhythm and priority agenda for the assigned leadership team.
* Lead development and coordination of annual, quarterly, and other operating plans.
* Translate priorities into clear roadmaps with owners, milestones, dependencies, and measures of progress.
* Coordinate leadership agendas, decision materials, action tracking, and follow-through.
* Support Regional or National Team input into ABP, resource planning, RBO, and other CE and enterprise planning processes.

Operational Integration & Execution

* Serve as a front door for operational requests from the assigned leadership team and route needs to the appropriate CE Operations or enterprise partner.
* Connect Field Leadership and HEDs to the broader support network without requiring them to independently navigate multiple teams.
* Coordinate across Enterprise Operations, RBO, Squad Field Partners, ABP, DDA, L&SD, and other functions to enable execution.
* Anticipate execution barriers, dependencies, and operational risks and mobilize partners to resolve them.
* Ensure appropriate communication and coordination between enterprise initiatives and Regional/National execution.

Insights & Decision Support

* Synthesize field insights, performance signals, customer information, and emerging business needs into clear leadership implications.
* Develop business reviews and decision materials that enable productive leadership conversations.
* Identify patterns and recurring needs that may have implications beyond the assigned Region or National Team.
* Surface cross-field opportunities, risks, and common needs to the Head of CE Field Operations so they can be addressed across the organization where appropriate.
* Provide recommendations related to priorities, resources, capacity, and operational tradeoffs.

Resource & Capacity Planning

* Maintain an integrated understanding of the assigned team's resource and capacity requirements.
* Support Regional or National Team roster, resource, and capacity planning.
* Identify capacity constraints and emerging needs and develop recommendations in partnership with Field Leadership.
* Connect local resource needs to broader CE and enterprise planning processes.

KEY DELIVERABLES

* Annual and quarterly operating plans
* Regional or National Team priority roadmap
* Leadership agendas, decision materials, and action logs
* Business reviews and synthesized field insights
* RBO, ABP, and enterprise planning inputs
* Resource, roster, and capacity plans
* Consolidated requests, risks, and capacity recommendations
* Clear escalation of cross-field opportunities and common operational needs

MINDSET & CAPABILITIES

* Trusted partner who builds credibility with senior Field Leaders
* Strategic thinker with strong operational discipline
* Able to translate ambiguity and complexity into clear plans and actions
* Strong business acumen and understanding of field execution
* Highly effective at influencing without formal authority
* Skilled at connecting people, priorities, and resources across organizational boundaries
* Strong analytical and synthesis capabilities
* Proactive and anticipatory rather than reactive
* Comfortable navigating a complex, matrixed environment
* Strong judgment and ability to distinguish between issues that should be solved locally and those requiring enterprise solutions
* Demonstrated ability to manage multiple priorities while maintaining focus on business impact
* Growth mindset and commitment to continuous improvement

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

* Bachelor's degree required
* Significant pharmaceutical, biotechnology, consulting, commercial, field operations, strategic, and/or analytical experience (8+ years preferred)
* Demonstrated experience partnering with senior business or field leaders
* Experience translating strategy into operational plans and driving execution
* Strong project/program management and cross-functional leadership capabilities
* Demonstrated ability to operate effectively within a complex matrixed organization
* Strong communication, executive presentation, analytical, and problem-solving skills
* Ability and willingness to travel as required for internal and external business meetings

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

* Graduate-level degree (e.g., MBA or advanced life sciences degree)
* Prior Field, Field Operations, Commercial Operations, or business planning experience
* Experience with resource planning, business planning, account planning, or field effectiveness
* Experience supporting Regional or National field leadership teams

Location: This is a Field-based role and relocation benefits are not available.

The expected salary range for this position based on the primary location of CA is $147,900 - $274,700 USD Annual. Actual pay will be determined based on experience, qualifications, geographic location, and other job-related factors permitted by law. A discretionary annual bonus may be available based on individual and Company performance. This position also qualifies for the benefits detailed at the link provided below.

new_roles.description:
**Job Description**

**This role is fully remote and must be located within the 50 U.S. states. Standard working hours are in Eastern Timezone. Semi-annual travel may be required to a Devoted office for on-site work.**

**A bit about this role:**

At Devoted, our mission is to dramatically improve the health and well-being of our members by treating each of them like family. Devoted is growing at an incredible pace, and we are thrilled to welcome and serve every new member who joins us. This growth demands that our Utilization Management (UM) operation must scale and evolve without ever losing sight of the people at the center of every authorization.

We believe UM done right means decisions that are correct, fair, and fast, delivered through a frictionless process and with heart. Behind every request is a member waiting on care and a provider working to deliver it. UM is hard, but the challenge doesn’t exempt us from our mission.

We are seeking a curious, operationally minded leader to serve as Director, Utilization Management Operations. Reporting to the Vice President of Health Services, you will lead the teams behind our administrative work: a large onshore and offshore team of UM Administrative Coordinators who manage intake, outreach, notifications, and follow-up. You will also hold dotted-line accountability for monitoring and ensuring the success of our Part B medical authorization turnaround times (TAT).

This role is for someone who is energized by a complex process: someone who wants to unravel it, reimagine it, and lead the build of something simpler, faster, and more consistent. You will have significant influence over the roadmap for Orinoco, our internal technology platform, and an integrated AI engine to put to work. This role will help pave the way towards realizing the next generation of our UM program, driving improvements in effectiveness, efficiency, and experience for our members and provider partners.

**Your Responsibilities and Impact will include**:

* **SLA & Timeliness Ownership:** Own SLA performance for the administrative steps that support authorization review across UM, delivering consistent, predictable performance at a meaningfully lower cost. Hold dotted-line accountability for Part B medical authorization turnaround times (TAT), partnering with the clinical leaders of that team to monitor performance, surface risks early, and remove administrative barriers to on-time decisions.
* **Process Reimagination:** Map our administrative processes end to end, including auth intake, requests for additional clinical information, facility census checks, member and provider notifications, and member follow-up, and lead their redesign for speed, consistency, and simplicity.

Thousands of patients move through our platform every day, and each is a real person waiting for an answer to a healthcare concern. We exist to get them that answer faster.

We manage the medical imaging pathway end-to-end. Providers order through a single point of entry, and from there, we run the entire medical diagnostic pathway. Managing the full pathway, rather than brokering pieces of it, is what lets us deliver imaging faster, at higher quality, and at a lower cost than the fragmented status quo.

We're looking for a **Director of Integration & Operational Excellence** at an exciting time. We've raised over $200m in funding to date, reached profitability, and are growing 100% year on year.

Millions of people wait too long for a diagnosis. Come help us fix that.

**WHAT YOU WILL ACHIEVE IN THIS ROLE**
--------------------------------------

You'll report to our Chief Operating Officer and Co-Founder and work closely with the CEO, Corporate Development, our CFO and leaders across Operations, Commercial, Product, Technology, People and Clinical. Your mandate is to make acquisitions work in practice and build the operating capability that allows Scan.com to integrate businesses repeatedly as we grow.

You'll join before upcoming acquisitions close, learn how Scan.com operates, and help prepare both our business and acquired teams for integration. You'll own the integrated plan, budget, dependencies, and delivery cadence from operational diligence through Day 1, the first 100 days, and the handover to business-as-usual owners. Functional leaders retain accountability for decisions in their areas; you'll hold the overall plan together, drive execution, and bring unresolved trade-offs to the COO.

Success means retained customers and referral relationships, uninterrupted patient service, reliable billing and collections, and measurable improvements in operating performance.

* **Lead integration planning before close.** Work with Corporate Development and Finance to test the operating assumptions behind each acquisition, identify integration costs and working-capital needs, and turn diligence findings into a practical delivery plan.
* **Build the integration playbook.** Establish Day 1 readiness criteria, 100-day plans, workstream owners, decision rights, budgets, and escalation routes. Adapt the approach to founder-owned businesses, carve-outs, referral networks and imaging centers.
* **Prepare** **Scan.com** **to receive acquired businesses.** Identify capacity constraints in scheduling, billing, customer support, technology and management. Resolve gaps before moving additional volume onto our platform.
* **Own execution across workstreams.** Lead the integration cadence across Finance, Operations, Commercial, People, Product, Technology and Clinical, working with Legal and Compliance on the approvals needed in their areas. Sequence concurrent integrations around available capacity.
* **Protect the business through change.** Build relationships with acquired founders and teams, identify key people and customer relationships to retain, and coordinate clear communications and responsibilities.
* **Make systems and process changes work operationally.** Partner with technical and operational owners on referral routing, scheduling, imaging systems, reporting and billing migrations. Agree testing, reconciliation, cutover criteria and contingency plans before switching.
* **Deliver the financial case.** Establish baselines with Finance and track revenue retention, collections, operating costs, and realized synergies. Separate one-time integration costs from recurring benefits and avoid counting growth or savings already included in the plan.
* **Improve operating performance across** **Scan.com****.** Lead focused projects on center and mobile-unit economics, staffing, vendor costs, workflows and capacity. Build the business case, implement the changes, and demonstrate the result in operating metrics and the P&L.
* **Build a practical operating cadence.** Maintain a reliable view of owners, milestones, budgets, risks, and decisions. Use automation and AI to reduce reporting work and give leadership concise updates on what needs attention.
* **Make improvements stick.** Document repeatable processes, train the teams who will run them, and hand over completed workstreams with clear ownership and measures of success.

**Example projects**

* Prepare a founder-owned imaging business for Day 1, retaining key relationships while aligning financial reporting and collections.
* Build a carve-out plan that identifies essential staff, systems and shared services, with costed transitional arrangements and clear exit dates.
* Validate referral-level unit economics and center capacity before moving new patient volume onto Scan.com's network.
* Reconcile an acquired company's billing and receivables data, establish collection baselines and resolve issues before a systems migration.

**YOUR FIRST 90 DAYS**
----------------------

Your ramp begins inside Scan.com, before an acquisition closes. The timing of live integrations will depend on the deal pipeline; preparation and operating improvement start immediately.

* **Days 1–30: learn the business at ground level.** Spend time with scheduling, center operations, Commercial, Finance, and revenue-cycle teams. Follow cases from referral through scan, report, billing, and payment. Review prior integrations, map the core systems and handoffs, and establish baseline service and financial metrics.
* **Days 31–60: build readiness.** Assess upcoming acquisitions alongside the deal team. Identify receiving-team capacity constraints, retention risks, and operational dependencies. Produce costed Day 1 and 100-day plans with named owners, and deliver an initial improvement to an existing Scan.com workflow.
* **Days 61–90: test and lead delivery.** Rehearse critical workflows and agree readiness criteria with functional owners. Launch the integration reporting cadence and lead the first implementation workstreams as transactions permit. Give leadership a clear view of what is ready, what needs fixing, and what should be sequenced later.

**How we'll measure success**

* Customer, referral volume, and key-employee retention.
* Patient access, scheduling performance and report turnaround through transitions.
* Billing accuracy, cash collections and receivables performance.
* Realized margin improvement and synergies, validated with Finance and measured against integration costs.
* Delivery against agreed budgets and milestones, followed by a successful handover to operational owners.

**WHAT YOU MIGHT BRING TO THE TABLE**
-------------------------------------

You don't need to meet every criterion. We are looking for someone who has personally led acquisitions through operational integration and can show what changed after close.

* **A record of delivering integrations.** You've led multiple post-acquisition integrations or substantial workstreams with direct accountability for outcomes. You can explain what went wrong, how you responded, and what the financial and operational results were.
* **Healthcare operating experience.** You've worked in a multisite healthcare, diagnostic imaging, healthcare-services, or similarly complex operating business. Experience in a PE-backed platform, founder-owned acquisition, or carve-out is particularly relevant.
* **Operational and financial depth.** You've owned a P&L, an operating function, or an integration programme with measurable financial responsibility. You can connect staffing, capacity, pricing, service quality, and collections to profitability and cash flow.
* **Understanding of the revenue cycle.** You understand how provider contracts, credentialing, billing workflows, denials, and receivables affect delivery and cash. Imaging-specific experience is valuable.
* **Experience implementing change.** You've worked with technical and operational teams on systems migrations, process standardization, or service transitions, including testing and reconciliation.
* **Credibility with acquired teams.** You can earn the trust of founders and frontline staff, retain what makes a business successful and make difficult changes clearly and respectfully.
* **Strong financial and analytical judgment.** You can build and challenge unit economics, integration budgets and business cases, distinguish recurring benefits from one-off effects, and investigate the detail behind a misleading headline metric.
* **Leadership across functions.** You establish clear accountability, resolve competing priorities and escalate decisions early. You are comfortable holding senior stakeholders to commitments.
* **A hands-on approach.** You're willing to spend time in centers and alongside operating teams, investigate individual cases and improve processes before they are fully documented. The role involves travel to Scan.com operations and acquired businesses.
* **Practical use of AI and automation.** You improve how work gets done while keeping appropriate human review over sensitive data, financial decisions, and operational changes.

Experience in consulting, transaction services, or strategic finance can be valuable when combined with direct responsibility for implementation and results after close.

**AI REQUIREMENTS**
-------------------

At Scan.com, AI isn't a side project; it's how we work. We expect everyone to use AI to think faster, remove drudgery, and multiply their output. What we care about is judgment: knowing when AI makes you sharper, when it doesn't, and how to use it responsibly around patient data. We'll assess this in the way that matters for this role, using the tier below. You don't need to be an engineer. You need to reach for the best tool and get more done as a result.

* Tier 1 — For this role, the expectation is that you are an AI-Native. You build with AI directly, shipping, automating, or prototyping real work with LLMs and agents, and have clear judgment on where humans must stay in the loop.

 + You build with AI, not just alongside it. You've shipped, automated, or prototyped something real using LLMs, agents, or AI tooling.
 + You can explain a workflow you redesigned so a machine does the boring 80%.
 + You have a view on where agentic systems help and where a human must stay in the loop, especially in regulated, PHI-adjacent work.
 + **Assessment:** a practical exercise where you use AI tools live or in a take-home.

**A VIEW ON OUR CULTURE**
-------------------------

We're building something that matters. Every scan we speed up is a real person waiting on an answer, and that urgency runs through everything we do. We move fast, we own outcomes, and take pride in our output. If you like ambiguity, working with ambitious people, and want your work to visibly move the needle, you'll feel at home here.

**HOW WE WILL INTERVIEW YOU**
-----------------------------

We keep our interview process short and sweet. Here are the stages you can expect, but we might switch up the order depending on team availability:

* 30-minute introductory phone call with a member of our Talent Team.
* A 45-minute discussion with the COO covering integrations you've led, the operating decisions you owned, and the results you delivered.
* A practical integration case and 'Scan Standard' interview. You'll assess a fictional acquisition, identify the key risks and build a prioritized Day 1 and 100-day plan. We'll discuss how you would protect service and collections, measure success, and use AI tools in your work.
* Meet the founders and/or other team members. Again, the length varies depending on how many people are involved and whether in person or via video call.
* Offer!

**WHAT WE OFFER**
-----------------

We go beyond the basics with our benefits package. We believe great work starts with supporting our people. Here's what you can expect from us:

* Salary range of **$150,000 - $175,000**
* Equity
* Flexible remote or hybrid work options
* Dedicated personal development budget
* Medical, vision, and dental coverage
* 28+ days of paid time off across PTO and wellbeing days, so you can show up at your best
* Paid parental leave
* 401k retirement plan
* All the equipment you need to do your best work
* Inclusive, people-first policies designed by our team, for our team

**DIVERSITY AT** **SCAN.COM**
-----------------------------

Scan.com is committed to eliminating discrimination and encouraging diversity within our team. We strive to provide equality and fairness for all job applicants and employees and never discriminate on the basis of gender, marital status, age, race, ethnicity, religion, or physical differences.

We are opposed to all forms of unlawful treatment and discrimination.

Our ambition is for our team to be representative of society's diversity, and for every employee to feel respected and able to bring their best selves to work.

If you need an accommodation to apply or interview, contact us at people@scan.com.

We look forward to receiving your application!

new_roles.title: Sr. Director, Launch Excellence & Operations
new_roles.description:
***Join Immatics and shape the future of cancer immunotherapy; one patient at a time!***

Immatics is committed to making a meaningful impact on the lives of patients with cancer. We are the global leader in precision targeting of **PRAME**, a target expressed in more than 50 cancers. Our cutting-edge science and robust clinical pipeline form the broadest **PRAME** franchise with the most **PRAME** indications and modalities, spanning TCR T-cell therapies and TCR bispecifics.

**Why Join Us?**

* **Innovative Environment:** Help to pioneer advancements in cancer immunotherapy.
* **Collaborative Culture:** Be part of a diverse team dedicated to your professional growth.
* **Global Impact:** Contribute to therapies that make a lasting impact on patients globally.

**Role Overview**

The Senior Director, Launch Excellence & Operations serves as a strategic partner and deputy to the VP, Launch Excellence, Strategy & Operations, helping shape and execute Immatics' commercial launch strategy. This highly visible role sits at the center of launch planning, governance, and operational readiness, ensuring cross-functional alignment and execution as the organization prepares for commercialization.

The successful candidate will lead integrated launch planning, support the Launch Readiness Review (LRR) process, and establish the operating rhythms, governance, and performance management frameworks necessary to drive launch success. This individual will operate seamlessly between strategy and execution, translating insights into action, guiding critical business decisions, and creating clarity in a dynamic and evolving environment.

**Reports to:** Vice President, Launch Excellence, Strategy & Operations

**Location:** US, Fully Remote

**Salary Range:** $250,000 - $290,000

**Basic Qualifications:**

* Bachelor’s degree in life sciences, business, engineering, or a related field with 15+ years of relevant experience OR
* MBA / advanced degree (MBA, PhD, MD, or equivalent) with 12+ years of relevant experience A combination of top-tier strategy consulting experience and in-house biopharmaceutical commercial strategy, commercial operations, or launch leadership experience.

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* 5+ years in oncology; direct experience with TCR, CAR-T, or TIL cell therapies, including a first wave of commercial launch strongly preferred
* Demonstrated ownership of commercial launch strategy or launch readiness — including launch planning, cross-functional governance, milestone and risk management, and readiness tracking through to launch.
* Knowledge of personalized manufacturing and vein-to-vein logistics, including manufacturing slot allocation and patient journey management.
* Understanding of the melanoma treatment landscape, therapeutic decision-making, and patient access barriers.
* Working knowledge of the cell therapy operational value chain — treatment center authorization, apheresis scheduling, chain of identity / chain of custody, and product delivery.
* Experience standing up launch governance, a launch readiness review process, or a commercial PMO from scratch.
* Familiarity with digital launch excellence tools and analytics.
* Experience scoping and managing external consultants, agencies, and analytics vendors.
* Proven ability to drive strategic decision-making across functions without direct authority: framing the decision, assembling the analysis, aligning stakeholders, and driving the issue to closure.
* Exceptional executive communication, influencing, and synthesis skills; able to distill complex, ambiguous cross-functional situations into a clear recommendation
* Strong strategic planning and operational execution skills.

**In this role you will:**

**Launch Strategy & Commercial Planning**

* Partner with the VP to develop and execute an integrated launch strategy, roadmap, and commercial playbook.
* Lead strategic evaluations and business cases for critical commercial decisions, capabilities, and growth opportunities.
* Continuously refine launch strategy based on market, competitive, regulatory, and operational insights.
* Develop executive recommendations and materials for senior leadership and key governance forums.

**Launch Governance & Cross-Functional Integration**

* Drive cross-functional alignment, decision-making, and accountability through the Launch Readiness Review (LRR) process.
* Co-own launch readiness planning, including critical milestones, dependencies, risks, and mitigation strategies.
* Establish and maintain operating rhythms, governance processes, and communication forums that support launch execution.
* Facilitate resolution of complex cross-functional issues and ensure timely escalation of key decisions.

**Operational Readiness & Cell Therapy Operations Performance**

* Build and monitor performance frameworks across the end-to-end cell therapy patient journey.
* Partner with operational teams to identify and address patient funnel attrition, process bottlenecks, and execution risks.
* Provide commercial leadership for systems, analytics, and reporting capabilities that enable launch readiness and operational excellence.
* Develop scalable processes and performance metrics to support successful commercialization.

**Travel Requirements:**

* Up to 20% travel to support cross-functional team meetings, treatment center engagement, advisory boards, congresses, and launch activities, including periodic travel to Immatics US in Stafford, TX

Qualified candidates will participate in a structured interview process, which includes:

* An initial recruiter phone screen (conducted via video)
* Interviews with the hiring leader and other key stakeholders (via video)
* A final-stage interview

**What do we offer?**

At Immatics, we believe in investing in our team’s health, safety and well-being. Here’s what you can expect if you join Immatics

**Comprehensive Benefits**:

* Competitive rates for Health, Dental, and Vision Insurance
* 4 weeks of vacation, granted up front each year and prorated for first and last year of employment.
* 12 company paid holidays
* 7 days of sick time
* 100% employer-paid life insurance up to at 1x annual salary, up to one hundred thousand dollars
* 100% employer-paid short- and long-Term disability coverage
* 401(k) with immediate eligibility and company match. The company will match 100% of your contributions up to 3% of your base salary for the first two years of employment, 4% for years 2-3 of employment, and up to 5% of your salary from the fourth year onward of continued employment.
* Partially paid parental leave for eligible employees.
* Additional voluntary employee-paid benefits and services, including accident, hospital indemnity, and critical illness insurance, as well as identity theft protection and pet insurance.

**Equal Employment Opportunity**

We are an equal opportunity employer and are committed to building a diverse and inclusive workplace. We consider all qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, ancestry, age, marital status, disability, genetic information, veteran status, or any other status protected by applicable law.

**Reasonable Accommodations**

We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations to individuals with disabilities and to applicants with sincerely held religious beliefs, practices, or observances. If you require assistance or accommodation during the application or interview process, please contact us at RecruitingUS@immatics.com.

**Work Authorization**

Applicants must be authorized to work in the United States without the need for current or future sponsorship.

**Pre-Employment Requirements**

Employment is contingent upon successful completion of a background check, reference checks and pre-employment drug screening, where permitted by applicable law. For certain roles, additional screenings such as a credit check or motor vehicle record review may be required, where job-related and consistent with business necessity.

**Notice to Staffing Agencies and Third-Party Recruiters**

Immatics US partners with a select group of approved staffing agencies. Candidate submissions are accepted only from agencies that have a current written agreement with Immatics US and signed and formally engaged by our Talent Acquisition team for an active search. Unsolicited resumes or candidate information, including submissions made directly to hiring managers, will not be considered and are not eligible for placement fees.
