existing_roles.description:
**Reports to:** Executive Director

 

**Job Summary:**

The Director of Quality and Compliance for the PACE (Program of All-Inclusive Care for the Elderly) Program will oversee and manage all aspects of quality assurance, compliance, and regulatory adherence for the PACE program. This role ensures that the program operates in full compliance with federal, state, and local regulations, as well as upholds the highest standards of care for the elderly participants. The Director will lead efforts to continuously improve program quality, enhance participant satisfaction, and drive performance excellence across the organization.

 

**Key Responsibilities:**

1. Regulatory Compliance Management:

* Ensure adherence to all PACE-related federal, state, and local regulations, including CMS (Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services) and state-specific requirements.

* Monitor and interpret updates to regulatory policies, and adjust organizational practices as necessary to remain compliant.

* Act as the primary liaison between the organization and regulatory agencies, ensuring timely reporting and response to audits, surveys, and inspections.

2. Quality Assurance and Improvement:

* In collaboration with the Medical Director develop, implement, and evaluate quality improvement initiatives to ensure high standards of care, safety, and service delivery for participants.

* Collaborate with clinical and operational teams to analyze performance metrics and identify opportunities for continuous improvement.

* Oversee the development and execution of corrective action plans (CAPs) for any areas of deficiency, ensuring timely resolution.

3. Risk Management and Reporting:

* Lead risk assessment processes to identify potential compliance and quality issues, minimizing risk to the organization and participants.

* Develop and implement risk mitigation strategies, including monitoring trends, identifying patterns, and taking proactive actions.

* Ensure the organization is prepared for external audits and inspections, managing all compliance-related documentation and reporting.

4. Staff Training and Development:

* Develop and conduct ongoing training programs for staff on compliance, quality standards, and regulatory requirements.

* Foster a culture of compliance and continuous improvement across the organization by leading educational initiatives and creating awareness.

* Provide guidance and support to staff on regulatory changes, quality standards, and best practices.

5. Participant Care and Satisfaction:

* Advocate for participants’ safety and satisfaction, ensuring that their rights and well-being are protected in all aspects of the program.

* Work closely with interdisciplinary teams to ensure person-centered care is at the core of all service delivery and interventions.

* Monitor and evaluate participant feedback, addressing any concerns or complaints in a timely and professional manner.

6. Leadership and Strategic Planning:

* Serve as a key member of the senior leadership team, contributing to the strategic direction of the PACE program.

* Collaborate with leadership to set annual goals for quality and compliance performance and develop strategies to achieve these objectives.

* Ensure alignment of quality and compliance initiatives with organizational goals and values.

7. Data Collection and Analysis:

* Oversee the collection, analysis, and reporting of quality and compliance data to track program performance and outcomes.

* Utilize data to drive decision-making and identify areas for operational improvements and resource allocation.

* Prepare reports and presentations for senior leadership and external stakeholders regarding compliance, quality, and performance metrics.

8. Technology and EMR

* Serving as the primary point of contact for EMR-related issues, providing guidance and troubleshooting support to team members.

* Leading training sessions and providing ongoing support for staff to ensure efficient use of the EMR system.

* Collaborating with IT and management teams to implement updates and resolve system issues.

* Continuously staying updated on new features and best practices for the EMR system to ensure the organization is utilizing the platform to its full potential.

**Qualifications:**

* Bachelor’s degree in healthcare administration, nursing, public health, or a related field (Master’s degree preferred).

* Minimum of 4 years of experience in quality management, compliance, or regulatory affairs in a healthcare setting, with at least 2 years in a leadership role.

* Knowledge and experience with PACE program operations and regulations (CMS and state-level).

* Strong understanding of healthcare regulations, accreditation standards, and compliance protocols.

* Proven track record in leading quality improvement initiatives and risk management programs.

* Exceptional leadership, communication, and interpersonal skills.

* Ability to work collaboratively across departments and with interdisciplinary teams.

* Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to drive results.

* Certification in Healthcare Quality (CHCQM, CPHQ) or other relevant certifications preferred.

**Physical Demands:**

* Ability to work in an office environment and attend in-person meetings.

* Occasional travel to program sites or regulatory meetings may be required.

**Work Environment:**

* A collaborative, team-oriented atmosphere within a dynamic, fast-paced healthcare environment.

* Commitment to participant-centered care and service excellence.

existing_roles.title: Global Director of Quality
existing_roles.description:
**Lead Globally. Drive Innovation. Make an Impact.**

**Join Amphenol Alden and Make a Difference in Patient Care Worldwide!**

At **Amphenol Alden Products (AAP)**, what we do matters. Our medical cable assemblies and interconnect solutions support the advanced technologies healthcare professionals rely on every day. Behind every product is a patient, a family, and an opportunity to make a difference in someone's life.

With roots as a family business more than 90 years ago, Amphenol Alden combines a proud history and entrepreneurial spirit with the resources and opportunities of a global corporation. We are a growing organization that values innovation, teamwork, accountability, and the contributions of our employees.

We believe our people are the foundation of our success. That's why we offer competitive compensation, an outstanding benefits package, work/life balance, and opportunities for professional growth and development.

**The Opportunity**

We are seeking an experienced and strategic **Global Director of Quality** to lead and advance quality operations across four manufacturing facilities in the United States, Mexico, India, and China.

Reporting to AAP’s General Manager and serving as a member of the Leadership Team, this individual will establish and drive the global quality strategy, strengthen Quality Management Systems (QMS), and promote a culture of quality excellence and continuous improvement throughout the organization.

This is an opportunity to make a significant impact by developing high-performing global Quality teams, driving operational improvements, strengthening customer and supplier partnerships, and ensuring consistent quality standards across all manufacturing locations.

**Principal Duties and Responsibilities**

* **Global Quality Strategy:** Develop and execute global quality strategies, objectives, and initiatives that support business goals, product quality, regulatory compliance, and operational excellence.
* **Quality Management Systems:** Lead the development, implementation, standardization, and continuous improvement of Quality Management Systems across all facilities, ensuring compliance with ISO 9001, ISO 13485, applicable FDA requirements, customer specifications, and other relevant regulatory standards.
* **Executive Leadership:** Participate as a member of the Executive Leadership Team in establishing business strategies, operational objectives, and organizational improvement initiatives.
* **Quality Performance:** Establish and monitor global quality metrics, including customer complaints, internal and supplier defects, Cost of Poor Quality (COPQ), corrective actions, and audit performance. Drive measurable improvements in quality and process capability.
* **Continuous Improvement:** Champion Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, and data-driven problem-solving methodologies to reduce defects, minimize waste, improve process consistency, and enhance overall operational performance.
* **Engineering and Operations Partnership:** Collaborate with Engineering and Operations to ensure effective quality planning, design and process FMEAs, risk assessments, process validation, and verification throughout the product lifecycle.
* **New Product Introduction:** Provide quality leadership for New Product Introduction (NPI) and manufacturing transfers, ensuring process capability, quality requirements, and customer expectations are met before production release.
* **Supplier Quality:** Partner with Global Supply Chain to develop and maintain a high-performing supplier base through supplier qualification, audits, performance monitoring, development, and corrective action programs.
* **Customer Quality:** Provide strategic leadership for customer quality initiatives, serving as the senior escalation point for significant quality concerns, customer audits, and corrective action resolution.
* **Audits and Regulatory Compliance:** Oversee internal and external quality audits, regulatory inspections, and management reviews, ensuring findings are addressed promptly and compliance is sustained.
* **Corrective and Preventive Action:** Strengthen global CAPA processes through effective root cause analysis, risk mitigation, and prevention of recurring quality issues.
* **Global Team Leadership:** Lead, mentor, and develop the global Quality organization, establishing clear expectations, accountability, talent development plans, and succession strategies.
* **Global Standardization:** Promote consistency and the sharing of best practices across manufacturing facilities in the United States, Mexico, India, and China.
* **Executive Reporting:** Provide regular updates to executive leadership on global quality performance, emerging risks, customer satisfaction, and progress toward strategic quality objectives.

**Related Experience and Education**

* Bachelor's degree in Quality, Engineering, or a related technical or scientific discipline; Master's degree preferred.
* 10+ years of previous related experience and at least 5 years of experience managing individuals.
* Strong knowledge of ISO 13485, ISO 9001, FDA Quality System requirements, and applicable regulatory standards.
* Demonstrated experience leading Quality Management Systems and continuous improvement initiatives across multiple manufacturing locations.
* Strong working knowledge of Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, CAPA, root cause analysis, risk management, and quality improvement methodologies.
* Proven ability to influence cross-functional teams, develop talent, and drive results in a global organization.

**Why Join Amphenol Alden?**

We believe great people deserve a great place to work. We offer a competitive compensation and benefits package designed to support your professional success, financial future, and overall well-being.

* Competitive salary and bonus opportunity.
* Hybrid work schedule.
* Excellent 401(k) retirement savings plan to help you plan for the future.
* Comprehensive benefits, including medical, dental, vision, life insurance, short- and long-term disability, Health Savings Account (HSA), and Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA).
* Employee discounts and company-sponsored activities.
* Opportunities for professional growth and career development.
* The opportunity to lead a global organization and make a meaningful contribution to products that support patient care worldwide.

**Ready to Lead What's Next?**

If you are a strategic quality leader who thrives on building strong teams, solving complex challenges, and driving results across global operations, we'd love to hear from you!

**Join Amphenol Alden and help shape the future of our global operations while making a difference in patient care around the world.**

*Amphenol Alden Products is an Equal Opportunity Employer.*

*Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States without current or future employer sponsorship.*

existing_roles.title: Head of Quality
existing_roles.description:
**About Tutor**

We believe robots should be the next chapter in making physical labor safer and more affordable. But, nearly nine out of ten American factories and warehouses don’t have a single robot. Tutor Intelligence is changing that.

We build robots that go straight into real factories and warehouses, to do real work, with real impact. Our robot Cassie does back-breaking work, moving boxes, pallets, and bulk goods for family-owned manufacturers to some of the largest brands in the world. Our robot Sonny does handwork, using two arms to achieve human-like dexterity in picking and packing. Every robot learns on the job, and each one we deploy makes the next one more capable, more affordable, and faster to put to work.

Founded at MIT and headquartered in Watertown, MA, we do it all in-house: the robotics hardware, the machine learning, and the field deployment and service. We’re a team of researchers, engineers, technicians, operators, and sellers who love building things and solving hard problems.

Our mission is grand: robots everywhere, for the common good, raising the standard of living across North America, and then the world.

**Why Tutor?**

Whether you’re designing robots, closing deals, running deployments, or creating the processes that help us scale, your work doesn’t sit on a shelf. It shows up on real production floors, making physical work safer and more affordable.

Our team of 160+ is driven by curiosity and a genuine love of building. Everyone here takes real ownership, learns fast, and holds a high bar while having each other’s backs. If you love hard problems and creating things that didn’t exist before, you’ll fit right in.

**The Role**

Tutor is hiring a Head of Quality to lead quality as a function, alongside the Head of Manufacturing. You own the quality system, supplier quality across our supply base, product safety certifications, and the quality targets the company holds itself to. The quality engineers and the quality manager report to you, and you grow the team from there. You report to the CTO. As our operations organization grows, you and the Head of Manufacturing will report to the leader of that organization.

This is a building role. The first pieces, incoming inspection, supplier controls and failure analysis, are being put in place by the team you will lead. Your job is to turn them into a system that holds as production grows, a supplier base we can trust, and a quality record that customers and certifying bodies can verify. You have the authority to hold any shipment that is not right.

### **Requirements**

* You have led a quality function at a company that builds complex electromechanical hardware in volume
* You have built or rebuilt a quality system and taken it through ISO 9001 or an equivalent certification
* You have run supplier quality across a supply base, including suppliers overseas
* You have taken a product through product safety certification
* You have built and led a team of quality engineers and managers
* You make decisions from data, and you can hold a shipment when the data says so

### **Nice to haves**

* Robotics, automation, vehicles, or capital equipment
* Reliability engineering methods: life testing, failure rate analysis, design reviews
* Building quality data and tooling that other teams use
* Experience with manufacturing execution systems

### **Benefits**

* **Fully employer-covered health insurance**, so you’re protected without the premium.
* **A managed 401(k)** to help you plan for the future.
* **Generous time off:** unlimited PTO and all federal holidays off for full-time salaried employees, and 16+ days of accrued paid time off plus 1.5x pay on federal holidays for hourly employees.
* **Regular in-office meals** and team social events throughout the year.

**Compensation**

The base salary range for this role is $220,000 to $280,000, depending on experience.

As Tutor grows, so will our benefits. We’re continuing to invest in ways to support our team at work and beyond.

*Tutor Intelligence is an equal opportunity employer and welcomes applicants from all backgrounds.*

existing_roles.description:
**Company Overview**

Contentnea Health is a Community Health Center providing comprehensive medical, dental and behavioral health services for members of our communities in Greene, Pitt and Pamlico counties in eastern North Carolina.

**Job Summary**

Provides strategic leadership, oversight, and coordination of all organizational quality initiatives, including designing, implementing and evaluating quality programs to ensure delivery of safe, patient-centered, equitable, and efficient care, leads data-driven improvement efforts, and supports regulatory reporting and compliance with standards.

**Responsibilities and Duties**

* Oversees the Quality Improvement (QI) department activities.
 + Leads the development, implementation, and evaluation of the organization’s Quality Improvement Program.
 + Identifies opportunities to support QI efforts through evaluation, testing, and/or integration for electronic health record (EHR) functionality and other Heath Information and Technology (HIT) systems.
 + Summarizes and shares clinical quality data with the Board, key leadership, and staff to inform decision-making and priorities for improvement.
 + Champions the adoption of standardized best practices and lessons learned across disciplines and departments at the care team level and at the organizational level using communication tools, published workflows, staff meetings, events and trainings.
 + Facilitates QI Committee meetings and ensures documentation, follow-up, and progress tracking.
 + Establishes annual QI goals, work plans, and performance benchmarks aligned with strategic priorities.
 + Develops dashboards and data tools to share performance results with leadership and staff.
* Collaborates with and guides clinical care team members to establish QI processes through the organization.
 + Leads or participates in work teams related to QI and functions as a coach to support care team in building, fostering patient-centeredness and healthy patient outcomes.
 + Researches external organizations and participates in training opportunities, and works with partners, consultants and experts to guide QI efforts.
 + Assesses the need for and facilitates education, training, and technical assistance for staff to ensure compliance with QI efforts.
 + Uses existing data systems to identify areas in need of quality improvement across the organization.
* Oversees organizational data submission and sharing to external entities in collaboration with other departments as needed.
 + Follows regulation on data collection and reporting structure as defined by the Health Resources and Services Administration (HRSA) and health plan incentives.
 + Approaches changes to the EHR or other IT systems with consideration to data governance.
 + Monitors Federal Tort Claims Act (FTCA) requirements and the health center’s compliance.
 + Leads the annual FTCA deeming and redeeming application process and ensures all required evidence and documentation are completed and submitted accurately.
 + Ensures accurate and timely reporting of UDS clinical measures and other federal/state quality requirements.
 + Participates in HRSA review and response with organization leaders.
 + Acts as administrator for electronic Value-Based Care (VBC) and Quality Incentive Plans (QIP) platforms.
 + Partners with key leadership to determine participation priorities.
 + Oversees QI and clinical participation in contracted VBC and QIPs.
 + Monitors performance with VBC and incentive plans; shares performance data with key leadership.
* Ensures ongoing alignment with Patient-Centered Medical Home (PCMH) standards, manages The National Committee for Quality Assurance (NCQA) reporting and serves as PCMH project manager.
 + Leads annual submission of PCMH report to maintain recognition for each recognized site and maintains documentation and policies needed for audits, accreditation, and regulatory compliance.
 + Ensures all new hires are trained in PCMH processes, policies, and workflows, including care coordination, team-based care, access, patient experience and satisfaction.
 + Maintains current knowledge of NCQA/PCMH standards and serves as the subject matter expert. Analyzes and reviews processes, policies, and systems on an ongoing basis to ensure they are aligned with current and updated PCMH standards.
 + Uses data to drive continuous improvement in clinical quality, patient experience and cost/utilization outcomes.
 + Reports PCMH performance to leadership to inform resource allocation and prioritize performance improvement activities.
 + Coordinates PCMH improvement activities with staff and leadership.
* Provides overall management and direction to departmental staff.
 + Oversees the development and maintenance of the departmental budget; monitors ongoing budgetary compliance and addresses problems as needed.
 + Delegates departmental duties and responsibilities; participates in high priority special projects and activities.
 + Represents the department at all senior management meetings.
 + Prepares departmental company policies and procedures and conveys all senior management communications and directives.
 + Monitors departmental performance using company performance standards and addresses issues as needed.
 + Directs departmental performance and provides specific instructions on completion of tasks/responsibilities.
 + Prepares and conducts performance appraisals for immediate staff.
 + Conducts hiring, disciplinary, and termination procedures.

**Qualifications and Skills**

Bachelor Degree in Nursing. Current licensure as a Registered Nurse in good standing with the NC Board of Nursing. Possesses advanced understanding of quality improvement theory and quality methodology, evidence-based practice, state and national priorities for patient safety and population health as determined by HRSA, DHHS, and other entities, and regulatory, recognition and compliance standards, such as FTCA, PCMH, and HRSA. The ideal candidate will have progressive experience in leading quality improvement activities and in leading staff.

Description:

Exalt Health, an acute rehabilitation hospital, provides an intensive rehabilitation program, and admitted patients must be able to tolerate three hours of intense rehabilitation services per day. Focused on caring for patients with complex rehabilitative needs such as stroke, spinal cord injury, brain injury, head trauma, medically debilitation conditions, neurological disorders, cardio-pulmonary amputations, orthopedic injuries, and multiple major traumas.

**Position Summary**

The Quality Director is responsible for spearheading the development, implementation, and continuous improvement of a comprehensive quality and patient safety program throughout our inpatient rehabilitation hospital network. In this role, you will drive a culture of excellence, ensuring our delivery of the highest standards of patient care across all our facilities in Texas. This position demands strong leadership, data analysis skills, exceptional attention to detail, and an unwavering commitment to patient-centered care.

**Essential Duties and Responsibilities**

* Strategic Planning: Design and implement a system-wide quality management framework, aligning with organizational goals and regulatory requirements.
* Performance Monitoring: Oversee the collection, analysis, and reporting of key quality metrics and patient outcome data. Identify trends, pinpoint areas for improvement, and develop targeted interventions.
* Continuous Improvement: Lead initiatives to enhance clinical quality, patient safety, and process efficiency across all rehabilitation facilities. Implement evidence-based best practices and drive innovation in quality improvement endeavors.
* Regulatory Compliance: Ensure adherence to all state, federal, and accreditation standards (e.g., The Joint Commission) related to quality management and patient safety.
* Education and Training: Develop and deliver educational programs to cultivate a quality-focused culture among staff at all levels.
* Collaboration: Partner with clinical leaders, department heads, and frontline staff to foster a collaborative environment focused on continuous improvement and patient satisfaction.
* Risk Management: Proactively identify and mitigate potential risks to patient safety and guide the organization in proactive risk management practices.
* Board Reporting: Prepare regular reports for the Executive Leadership team and Board of Directors, showcasing quality performance metrics, initiatives, and strategic recommendations.

Requirements:

**Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities**

Licenses or Certifications

* Certified Professional in Healthcare Quality (CPHQ) or other relevant quality certifications highly desired.
* Current, unencumbered clinical licenses in the state where the hospital is operating required.

Education, Training, and Experience

* Education in a healthcare-related field or a clinical degree preferred.
* Minimum of 7-10 years of progressive leadership experience in healthcare quality management, with a proven track record in an inpatient hospital setting.

Skills and Abilities, Proficiency and Productivity Standards

* Deep knowledge of quality improvement methodologies (e.g., Lean, Six Sigma, PDSA).
* Expertise in healthcare regulatory standards, accreditation requirements, and best practices.
* Proficiency in healthcare data management and statistical analysis tools.
* Organizes and prioritizes tasks and projects, accurately completing job responsibilities within the specified time constraints.
* Excellent attention to detail and accuracy.
* Analytical and problem-solving abilities.
* Ability to work under deadlines and handle multiple tasks.
* Speaks and communicates English effectively in verbal and written format; writes legibly.
* Reading and comprehension at the level necessary to perform job duties appropriately.
* Works cooperatively with co-workers and other hospital employees
* Functions proficiently in a Microsoft Windows environment (Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint)

The company is an equal opportunity employer, drug-free workplace, and complies with ADA regulations as applicable.

existing_roles.title: Quality Assurance Director
existing_roles.description:
Arrowhead Winch engineers and manufactures industrial winch, hoist and drive systems under the BRADEN, CARCO and Gearmatic brand names in Broken Arrow and Okmulgee, Oklahoma. We are seeking a talented **Quality Assurance Director** to join our team in **Broken Arrow, Oklahoma.** Please note: This is a **100% on site** office-based position supporting both the Okmulgee and Broken Arrow, Oklahoma manufacturing plants. Benefits include 401K with matching up to 5%, plus profit sharing plan; medical, dental and vision plans; flexible spending and health savings accounts; paid short- and long-term disability program; paid life insurance; and paid holidays, sick and vacation time. Our work environments are clean, climate controlled and safe. Arrowhead Winch does require applicants to complete a background check, drug test, and pre-employment physical as a condition of employment. Our goal is for all employees to work safely without injury while maintaining the highest safety standards in compliance with company policies.

**Quality Assurance Director** **Position Overview:**

The Quality Assurance Director leads the Quality Department and builds a world-class, prevention-focused quality culture across the Broken Arrow and Okmulgee plants. Partnering with Operations, Engineering, Purchasing, and frontline teams, this leader promotes quality at the source, shared accountability, and measurable customer satisfaction. The role oversees the ISO 9001 Quality Management System (QMS), customer and supplier quality, corrective action, measurement systems, traceability, warranty analysis, and new-product readiness.

**Quality Assurance Director** **Essential Functions/Responsibilities:**

* Build a quality-at-the-source culture through visible shop-floor leadership, employee engagement, supervisor coaching, recognition, and shared accountability.
* Set quality strategy and annual goals aligned with business priorities, customer requirements, and measurable results.
* Lead and standardize quality procedures, controls, audits, and ISO 9001 management reviews across both plants; ensure actions are completed and effective.
* Partner with Operations to strengthen standard work, in-process checks, visual controls, and mistake-proofing to prevent defects and improve first-pass yield.
* Establish clear expectations for employees to identify, contain, and escalate suspect product; support prompt action on quality concerns.
* Define quality standards and process controls for machining, welding, painting, assembly, and final testing.
* Track and review leading and lagging quality measures, including first-pass yield, customer escapes, scrap, rework, warranty cost, supplier rejects, cost of poor quality, and corrective-action effectiveness; assign owners for improvements.
* Monitor customer scorecards and ensure customer-specific specifications, certifications, inspection records, and corrective-action requirements are met at both plants.
* Communicate quality issues, containment plans, corrective actions, and verified closure promptly and accurately to customers.
* Develop employee quality awareness and problem-solving skills; maintain inspector training, qualification, and competency requirements.
* Lead Quality Department staffing, coaching, performance management, succession planning, and professional development.
* Oversee calibration, measurement system suitability, and gage repeatability and reproducibility (Gage R&R) studies.
* Lead cross-functional root-cause analysis and corrective action using structured methods such as 8D or 5 Whys; verify actions prevent recurrence.
* Use risk-based and layered process audits to confirm compliance with critical controls and sustain improvements.
* Manage nonconforming material, including identification, containment, segregation, documented disposition, controlled deviations, and release authorization.
* Control process changes through risk assessment, approval, validation, documentation, and communication.
* Partner with Purchasing to improve supplier quality through scorecards, reject trends, audits or visits, and targeted corrective actions.
* Lead returned-product, warranty, and field-failure investigations; coordinate containment, customer feedback, and prevention of repeat issues.
* Partner with Design Engineering to improve manufacturability and eliminate design-related quality risks.
* Support new products, engineering changes, and process transfers through risk-based quality planning, PFMEAs, control plans, inspections, and process validation.
* Set end-of-line testing requirements and records; ensure failed tests are investigated and authorized before retest or product release.
* Maintain part, component, production, and test traceability appropriate to product and customer requirements.
* Manage the quality budget and prioritize sustainable improvements that reduce the cost of poor quality without compromising conformance.
* Manage customer specific process approvals, create qualification plans, and maintain required test results and certifications. Establish required internal processes that must be maintained to hold the customer certifications.

**Quality Assurance Director** **Qualifications:**

* Bachelor’s degree in engineering, quality, manufacturing, or a related field.
* Seven to ten years of quality leadership in ISO 9001 manufacturing, including machining and assembly, multi-site supervision, and team development.
* Proven success building a quality-first culture, coaching frontline teams, and reducing recurring defects through prevention and accountability.
* Ability to interpret part and assembly drawings; working knowledge of metrology and geometric dimensioning and tolerancing (GD&T).
* Practical experience with Lean/Six Sigma, structured root-cause analysis, and corrective-action effectiveness verification.
* Experience with statistical process control (SPC), Gage R&R, process capability, PFMEA, and control plans, including methods suited to low-volume, high-mix production.
* Strong analytical, technical, leadership, communication, and conflict-resolution skills; ability to influence cross-functional teams and work effectively with customers.
* Strong documentation and organizational skills; proficiency in Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint, and Word.

**Quality Assurance Director** **Preferred Qualifications:**

* Lean or Six Sigma certification (Green Belt or Black Belt preferred).
* ISO 9001 Lead Auditor training or certification.
* Experience using short-run SPC, layered process audits, and mistake-proofing in low-volume, high-mix manufacturing.
* Welding inspection knowledge; AWS Certified Welding Inspector (CWI) a plus.
* Knowledge of paint and coatings inspection.
* Knowledge and Experience using AI Tools such as Claude, ChatGPT, and Microsoft Copilot

**Physical Demands and Work Environment:**

* Sit, stand, and walk for extended periods, including in a manufacturing shop.
* Use a computer and review technical documents for extended periods.
* Have adequate vision to inspect parts and review documents.
* Hear and speak clearly for effective communication.
* Occasionally lift up to 50 lbs. with assistance and bend, squat, or stoop.
* Work around electrical and heavy equipment; handle and inspect parts.
* Wear required personal protective equipment (PPE) in applicable areas.
* Travel regularly between the Broken Arrow and Okmulgee plants.

Arrowhead provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, military and/or veteran status, disability, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws in accordance with Section 503 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973, as amended, and the Vietnam Era Veterans Readjustment Assistance Act of 1974, which require affirmative action to ensure equal opportunity in all aspects of employment. If accommodation required, contact HR at 918-259-3259.

existing_roles.title: Director of Trade Compliance & Quality
existing_roles.description:
Description:

The Director of Trade Compliance & Quality leads Zhone’s global trade compliance program and supports the development and implementation of the company’s Quality Management System.

The primary responsibility of this position is Trade Compliance. The successful candidate must have extensive, hands-on experience managing U.S. and international import/export compliance in a global business environment, including export controls, customs, product classification, sanctions and restricted-party screening, licensing, regulatory documentation, and international shipping requirements.

The role provides subject-matter expertise and practical guidance to Engineering, Supply Chain, Operations, Logistics, Sales, Finance, Legal, and other stakeholders to help ensure Zhone products and transactions comply with applicable trade laws and regulatory requirements.

As a secondary but strategically important responsibility, the Director leads Zhone’s Quality Management System initiatives, with the objective of achieving and subsequently maintaining ISO 9001 and TL 9000 certification.

The position requires a practical, hands-on leader capable of developing policies and procedures, resolving complex compliance matters, preparing the organization for audits and certifications, and working effectively with suppliers, contract manufacturers, customers, regulatory authorities, freight forwarders, customs brokers, and certification bodies.

**Key Responsibilities**

Trade Compliance - Primary Responsibility

* Lead and continuously improve Zhone’s global import and export compliance program.
* Interpret and apply applicable U.S. and international trade laws and regulations, including the Export Administration Regulations (EAR), ITAR where applicable, U.S. Customs requirements, sanctions requirements, and FCC-related regulatory considerations.
* Manage classification of products, components, software, and technology using Export Control Classification Numbers (ECCNs) and Harmonized Tariff Schedule (HTS) classifications.
* Determine export authorization and licensing requirements and manage applicable export licenses and import permits.
* Manage denied-party, restricted-party, sanctions, embargo, and country-of-destination compliance.
* Review transactions involving controlled or potentially restricted technologies, customers, countries, suppliers, end users, and end uses.
* Provide guidance on the handling and transfer of export-controlled technical information and technology.
* Establish and maintain trade compliance policies, procedures, work instructions, records, and internal controls.
* Ensure accurate customs, import/export, and international shipping documentation.
* Support proper determination and documentation of country of origin, customs valuation, tariff classification, and applicable trade requirements.
* Support compliance associated with global sourcing, contract manufacturing, product transfers, and changes in manufacturing location.
* Monitor regulatory developments, assess business impact, and implement required process and documentation changes.
* Conduct or coordinate periodic trade compliance audits and risk assessments.
* Develop and deliver role-appropriate trade compliance training.
* Maintain documentation needed for internal audits, external audits, disclosures, and regulatory inquiries.
* Investigate and resolve complex or escalated trade compliance matters.
* Coordinate with customs brokers, freight forwarders, suppliers, customers, regulatory authorities, and external trade counsel, as appropriate.
* Partner with Engineering to obtain the technical information necessary for defensible product classifications and regulatory assessments.
* Provide practical compliance guidance that supports business execution while maintaining appropriate regulatory controls.

Quality Management - Secondary Responsibility

* Lead Zhone’s initiative to achieve and maintain ISO 9001 and TL 9000 certification.
* Develop, implement, and maintain an effective company-wide Quality Management System (QMS).
* Conduct gap assessments against ISO 9001 and TL 9000 requirements and establish a prioritized certification-readiness roadmap.
* Develop and maintain quality policies, procedures, work instructions, records, and document-control requirements.
* Establish and coordinate the internal quality audit program and QMS management reviews.
* Manage or oversee nonconformities, Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA), root-cause analysis, and verification of corrective-action effectiveness.
* Establish and monitor quality performance indicators and applicable TL 9000 measurements.
* Coordinate quality requirements with Zhone’s ODM, EMS, component, and other manufacturing partners.
* Support supplier qualification, supplier performance monitoring, supplier corrective actions, and quality audits, as appropriate.
* Coordinate with Engineering, Operations, Supply Chain, and Customer Support on product and process quality matters.
* Lead preparation for certification and surveillance audits and serve as a primary interface with certification bodies.
* Ensure audit findings and nonconformities are appropriately investigated, documented, corrected, and closed.
* Drive continuous improvement using quality data, customer feedback, product returns, manufacturing issues, field performance, and supplier performance.

Requirements:

Education

* Bachelor’s degree in business, Supply Chain, International Trade, Engineering, Quality, or a related discipline preferred.
* An equivalent combination of relevant education and substantial trade compliance experience may be considered.

Trade Compliance

* 8+ years of progressive, hands-on trade compliance experience, preferably within telecommunications, networking equipment, electronics, technology, or another international hardware business.
* Extensive working knowledge of the U.S. Export Administration Regulations (EAR).
* Demonstrated experience performing or managing ECCN classifications.
* Strong experience with HTS classification and U.S. Customs requirements.
* Experience determining export licensing and authorization requirements.
* Demonstrated experience with sanctions, embargo, end-use/end-user, and restricted-party compliance.
* Experience managing international import/export documentation and regulatory records.
* Experience working with freight forwarders, customs brokers, suppliers, and contract manufacturers.
* Strong analytical, investigative, and problem-solving skills, with demonstrated ability to assess regulatory and operational risk and resolve complex trade compliance matters.
* Experience developing or maintaining trade compliance policies, procedures, internal controls, training, and audit programs, and translating regulations into practical business processes and documented decisions.
* Ability to interpret technical product information and collaborate with Engineering on regulatory classifications.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain complex regulations in clear business terms and influence and collaborate across Engineering, Supply Chain, Operations, Logistics, Sales, Finance, Legal, and executive management.
* Ability to work effectively with customers, suppliers, manufacturing partners, auditors, and regulatory authorities.
* High attention to detail and ability to maintain accurate, audit-ready compliance and quality records and supporting documentation.
* Strong Microsoft Excel and data-analysis capabilities; experience with ERP systems and trade-compliance or classification tools is preferred.

Quality

* Practical experience working within an ISO 9001 Quality Management System.
* Familiarity with QMS documentation, internal audits, management reviews, certification readiness, Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA), root-cause analysis, and continuous improvement.
* Experience supporting or leading an ISO certification or surveillance audit is strongly preferred.
* Previous TL 9000 experience is highly desirable.
* Experience with quality management in telecommunications, electronics manufacturing, ODM/EMS, or another technology-hardware environment is preferred.
* Familiarity with 5 Whys, 8D, Fishbone/Ishikawa analysis, Pareto analysis, and FMEA is desirable.

**Recommended Professional Certifications**

Trade Compliance - Certifications Strongly Preferred

* Certified Export Specialist (CES), NCBFAA Educational Institute.
* Certified Customs Specialist (CCS), NCBFAA Educational Institute.
* U.S. Customs Broker License, highly desirable.
* Additional recognized training or credentials covering EAR/export controls, sanctions, customs, and international trade compliance.

Quality - Certifications Preferred

* ISO 9001 Lead Auditor or Lead Implementer training.
* TL 9000 training.
* ASQ Certified Quality Auditor (CQA).
* ASQ Certified Manager of Quality/Organizational Excellence (CMQ/OE).
* ASQ Certified Quality Engineer (CQE).

existing_roles.description:
**Lassonde Pappas & Co.** is a US Leader in beverage manufacturing dedicated to our team members, customers and consumers satisfaction. We remain committed to our small-town roots and rural values. **Hardworking** and **caring** are qualities that make our teams special. Since 1942, we’ve been producing delicious products for our customers across the country!

To provide the best for our customers, we focus on building the best team by creating and advancing an inclusive environment amongst our diverse workforces. If you’re passionate about customer satisfaction, reliable, and committed to being and doing better, join us!

**We value each of our employees’ total wellbeing. To support employees in all stages of their wellness journey, we have a robust benefits program including medical, dental, and vision coverage options, growth and development potential, along with 401-K, Life & Disability Insurance, PTO, Tuition Reimbursement, Health Fairs, Gym Membership Discounts, and so much more!**

*Pay Range for this position is: $155,000-$200,000 plus annual bonus, depending on experience and geographical location.*

**POSITION SUMMARY** 
The Environmental Health and Safety Director leads the development, implementation, and performance of health, safety, and environmental programs and policies at Lassonde Pappas & Co. Inc. facilities, to maintain compliance with applicable national and local regulations and to ensure a safe, healthy working environment for all employees. This role reports to the VP of Manufacturing for the US and is based out of our Cherry Hill, New Jersey location.

**Primary Responsibilities include*****:***

* Oversee and ensure the organization’s compliance with local, state, and federal environment, health, and safety regulations including (but not limited to) fire safety and OSHA regulations, and keep up with any changes to laws and regulations that impact the organization
* Work closely with the organization’s legal department to ensure that the company is in compliance with these regulations
* Direct audits and work with each plant and its departments to ensure that all company guidelines are being followed
* Manage the safety budget at the manufacturing sites to ensure that appropriate personal protective and safety equipment is available as needed to prevent injuries and provide for a safe and healthy work environment
* Develop, implement, and evaluate programs, policies, and procedures related to health, safety, and environmental issues in the workplace, and ensure that environmental policy and procedure manuals are available and updated at all times to reduce the risk of injury or illness in the workplace
* Prepare, schedule, and execute training to cover emergency procedures, workplace safety, and other relevant topics
* Lead the planning, execution, monitoring and continuous improvement of environmental health and safety programs
* Conduct risk assessments of work sites to identify potential hazards and formulate plans to mitigate them
* Coordinate with insurance carriers to ensure that appropriate coverage is in place to cover any potential risks
* Review the employee accident reports and medical claims to evaluate the need for potential changes to current policies or procedures
* Consult with engineers to ensure that building designs are safe and compliant with current regulations
* Performs other related duties as required and assigned

**SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES**

* Maintain staff by training employees; maintaining a safe, secure, and legal work environment; developing personal growth opportunities.
* Set objectives, monitor performance, and develop individual training plans to support professional development

* Communicate job expectations; planning, monitoring, and assessing job results; coaching, and counseling employees; developing, coordinating, and enforcing systems, procedures, and productivity standards.
* Establish strategic goals; identifying and evaluating trends; choosing a course of action; defining objectives; evaluating outcomes.
* Set strategic direction and coordinate the work of others to achieve objectives.

**EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE**

**Minimum Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Environmental Safety, Occupational Safety and Health, or related field required; Masters degree desirable.

* Minimum 8 years working experience in Supply Chain environment in Food and Beverage or other perishable goods
* 5+ years of safety and environmental experience in a manufacturing environment. Experience with a union manufacturing environment is a plus.
* Excellent negotiation skills and the ability to influence others while maintaining professionalism
* Proficient in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook (knowledge in Excel should extend past spreadsheet manipulation and should include creation of formulas)
* Excellent verbal and written communication skills
* Detailed oriented and can multi-task
* Excellent time management skills

**Additional Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience in the food/beverage industry
* Experience in Manufacturing or production environment
* Experience with risk management and project management
* Must pay high attention to detail and have strong interpersonal, communication, and observation skills
* Experience in report writing
* Proven organizational skills
* Ability to direct, coach, and train others
* Consultative, influential, strategic thinking and problem-solving skills

**PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS & WORKING CONDITIONS**

This position requires sufficient physical ability to work in a typical office setting; driving a motor vehicle and occasionally working in the field/production setting.

**FREQUENT:** sitting, upward and downward flexion of neck; fine finger dexterity and light to moderate finger pressure to include extended periods of keyboard and mouse use, side-to-side turning of neck, walking, standing, bending and stooping, pushing/pulling, twisting at waist, moderate wrist torque to twist equipment knobs and dials.

**OCCASIONAL:** squatting, kneeling, reach above and at shoulder height, moderate grasp to manipulate reference books and manuals; lifting objects weighing 20 – 35 lbs. from below waist to above shoulders and transporting distances up to 50 feet.

**VISION:** Ability to see in the normal visual range with or without correction.

**HEARING:** Ability to hear in the normal audio range with or without correction.

Other duties as assigned are part of every job description. existing_roles.title: Director of Planning and Production Coordination
existing_roles.description:
**POSITION:** Director of Planning and Production Coordination

**SHIFT:** Monday - Friday, 8:00 am - 5:00 pm + Additional hours based on business demand

**SALARY:** $139,362 - $155,161.50 + (DOE) + Full Benefits Package

**LOCATION: On-site in office in Fargo, ND**

### **SUMMARY OF RESPONSIBILITIES**

The Director of Planning and Production Coordination leads enterprise planning and production coordination across CSP, Tank and Structural product lines. The role establishes consistent planning standards, aligns demand with capacity, ensures production readiness, balances workloads across sites and supports reliable customer commitments. The role owns the planning system and coordination processes.

### **ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS**

* Embrace and demonstrate the qualities of the TrueNorth Steel Game Changer definition.
* Comply with all safety, quality, environmental and workplace requirements.
* Lead, coach, and develop the CSP, Tank and Structural Planning Leaders and the Production Coordinator Supervisor, establishing clear expectations, accountability, and succession coverage.
* Establish and continuously improve an integrated planning and production-coordination system with common standards, planning horizons, terminology, decision rights, data requirements, and escalation paths.
* Align customer demand, forecasts, backlog, inventory, labor, equipment, material availability, and site capability into executable production plans.
* Confirm customer commit-date feasibility using verified readiness, material, capacity, outside-processing, site, and delivery information.
* Provide an enterprise view of capacity and constraints, leading approved workload-balancing actions such as site transfers, priority changes, outsourcing, overtime, and staffing adjustments.
* Define and enforce production-readiness requirements for drawings, bills of material, routing, material, CNC and nesting information, quality requirements, outside services, job packets, shipping information, and approvals.
* Lead regular site, product-line, and enterprise planning reviews that surface demand, capacity, backlog, readiness, schedule performance, risks, and decisions requiring action.
* Partner with Manufacturing, Sales, Project Management, Estimating, Drafting, Engineering, Purchasing, Inventory Control, Quality, Shipping, Logistics, Finance, and other functions to resolve planning constraints.
* Govern planning and production coordination data and transactions in SyteLine, Tekla and other approved systems, including capacity assumptions, work-center data, production status, and readiness information.
* Define performance measures and dashboards for schedule, backlog, capacity, readiness, equipment use, changes, and failure-related costs. Use data to improve delivery, throughput, material utilization, and profitability.
* Establish repeatable standard work, documentation, training, cross-training, and backup coverage to reduce dependence on individual knowledge.
* Serve as the escalation point for significant cross-site, cross-product, and cross-functional planning issues. Elevate unresolved matters with facts, alternatives, risks, and recommendations.
* Support annual business, capacity, capital, workforce, and budget planning, along with strategic manufacturing initiatives.
* Provide the VP of Manufacturing with regular updates on planning risks, delivery, capacity, material, organizational needs, trends, and recommended actions.
* Travel to manufacturing sites is required to understand processes, build relationships, support teams, and ensure consistent implementation of planning and production-coordination standards.
* Prompt and dependable attendance.
* Other duties as assigned.

### **KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND QUALITIES**

* Strong knowledge of manufacturing planning, scheduling, capacity management, production coordination, inventory, and shop-floor execution.
* Ability to lead leaders and standardize planning processes across multiple manufacturing sites or business units.
* Working knowledge of ERP-supported planning, bills of material, routing, work centers, job release, inventory, and production transactions.
* Strong analytical judgment and ability to balance customer commitments, manufacturing capability, cost, and business risk.
* Effective communication, facilitation, change leadership and cross-functional influence skills.
* High integrity, accountability, attention to detail, sound judgment, and bias toward action.
* Commitment to safety, quality, customer service, teamwork, and continuous improvement.

### **EDUCATION AND WORK EXPERIENCE**

* Bachelor’s degree in Operations Management, Supply Chain Management, Engineering, Manufacturing, Business Administration, Construction Management or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant work experience.
* Minimum of ten years of progressive responsible experience in manufacturing operations, planning, scheduling, supply chain, project coordination, or a related field preferred, including five years of leadership experience.
* Experience leading multi-site planning or operational processes, ERP-supported planning and cross-functional improvement preferred.
* Experience in steel fabrication, metal manufacturing, project-based manufacturing, or a related industrial environment preferred.

* Establish goals to provide continual improvement in operational productivity and quality.

existing_roles.description:
**Job Description Summary**
===========================

GE Aerospace is seeking a Director – Digital Operations, Manufacturing Execution to lead ongoing digital operations across our Manufacturing Execution ecosystem. This role is responsible for platform stewardship, operational support, service continuity, and steady-state ownership of critical manufacturing applications that enable factory performance across the enterprise.
 
 
The Director will provide cross-functional leadership across support, product, and architecture to ensure reliable, scalable, and well-governed operations for platforms including PlantApps, PFMD, Bluestreak, and the broader future digital manufacturing ecosystem. This leader will own the operating model for sustaining and improving these platforms over time, with accountability for uptime, service performance, support responsiveness, operational stability, platform health, and issue resolution.
 
 
This is a high-impact leadership role for someone who can operate effectively across a complex enterprise, align multiple stakeholders, and build a durable future-state operating model for manufacturing digital operations. 
 
\*Eastern Time Zone Preferred for US Based Candidates\*

**Job Description**
===================

**Roles and Responsibilities**:

In this role, you will:

* Lead the digital operations function for Manufacturing Execution, with accountability for ongoing support, operational continuity, service performance, and platform stewardship.
* Provide continuous, steady-state ownership across a portfolio of manufacturing digital platforms, including PlantApps, PFMD, Bluestreak, and related applications in the future digital manufacturing ecosystem.
* Lead cross-functional teams spanning operations, support, product, and architecture to ensure stable and effective operation of business-critical manufacturing platforms.
* Establish and manage the support model, operating model, service governance, and platform ownership structure required to sustain and improve MES-related platforms.
* Drive uptime, operational stability, support responsiveness, platform health, and issue resolution across the ecosystem.
* Partner with operations teams, product owners, architects, support teams, and site users to ensure services are reliable, well-governed, and aligned to business needs.
* Govern service delivery through clear KPIs, operating cadences, escalation paths, and performance reporting.
* Lead root cause analysis, corrective actions, and continuous improvement efforts to reduce repeat issues and strengthen operational reliability.
* Ensure operational readiness and service continuity for releases, upgrades, migrations, implementations, and platform transitions.
* Prioritize investment and attention across support needs, service risks, platform health, and business-critical operational demands.
* Drive adherence to compliance, controls, and cybersecurity requirements while simplifying and strengthening operational processes.
* Build and lead a culture grounded in FLIGHT DECK, with strong focus on respect for people, continuous improvement, customer value, and accountability.
* Shape and optimize a durable future-state operating model for enterprise manufacturing digital operations.

**Minimum Qualifications**:

 

* Bachelor’s degree from accredited university or college with minimum of 8 years of professional experience OR Associates degree with minimum of 11 years of professional experience OR High School Diploma with minimum of 13 years of professional experience
* Minimum 5 years of professional experience in Digital Operations.
* Note: Military experience is equivalent to professional experience
* Eligibility Requirement:
* Legal authorization to work in the U.S. or UK is required. We will not sponsor individuals for employment visas, now or in the future, for this job.

**Desired Characteristics:**

**Technical and Business Expertise:**

* Strong experience leading digital operations, service delivery, application support, or platform operations in a complex enterprise environment
* Experience with Manufacturing Execution Systems (MES), manufacturing applications, or other business-critical digital platforms
* Demonstrated success operating and improving platforms with accountability for service continuity, uptime, support responsiveness, and operational stability
* Experience working across multiple platforms and stakeholder groups to create effective operating models and governance structures
* Strong understanding of service management, incident/problem management, release readiness, operational controls, and platform lifecycle support
* Ability to make tradeoffs across platform health, support demand, business priorities, and technical constraints
* Familiarity with digital manufacturing environments and the role of technology in supporting safety, quality, delivery, and cost

**Leadership:**

* Demonstrated success leading enterprise or multi-platform operational ownership with broad cross-functional leadership
* Experience leading support, product, architecture, and engineering in a matrixed global organization
* Ability to create clarity in complex environments and align teams around a common operating model
* Strong judgment in prioritization, escalation management, governance, and service ownership decisions
* Experience coaching, developing, and optimizing teams in support of long-term organizational capability

**Personal Attributes:**

* Excellent communication skills with the ability to engage senior leaders and technical teams with confidence and clarity
* Strategic thinker with the ability to translate vision into a durable operating model and concrete action plans
* Strong analytical, organizational, and execution skills
* Comfortable working through ambiguity, scale, and organizational complexity
* Customer-focused and operationally disciplined, with a strong bias for action and continuous improvement

**Additional Information for candidates in US:**

The base pay range for this position is $152,000-$202,000 USD. The specific pay offered may be influenced by a variety of factors, including the candidate’s experience, education, and skill set. This position is also eligible for an annual discretionary bonus based on a percentage of your base salary/ commission based on the plan. This posting is expected to close on November 10th, 2026.

GE Aerospace offers comprehensive benefits and programs to support your health and, along with programs like HealthAhead, your physical, emotional, financial and social wellbeing. Healthcare benefits include medical, dental, vision, and prescription drug coverage; access to a Health Coach from GE Aerospace; and the Employee Assistance Program, which provides 24/7 confidential assessment, counseling and referral services. Retirement benefits include the GE Aerospace Retirement Savings Plan, a 401(k) savings plan with company matching contributions and company retirement contributions, as well as access to Fidelity resources and planning consultants. Other benefits include tuition assistance, adoption assistance, paid parental leave, disability insurance, life insurance, and paid time-off for vacation or illness.

GE Aerospace (General Electric Company or the Company) and its affiliates each sponsor certain employee benefit plans or programs (i.e., is a “Sponsor”). Each Sponsor reserves the right to terminate, amend, suspend, replace or modify its benefit plans and programs at any time and for any reason, in its sole discretion. No individual has a vested right to any benefit under a Sponsor’s welfare benefit plan or program. This document does not create a contract of employment with any individual.

**For Candidates in the UK:**

At GE Aerospace we understand the importance of Total Reward. Our flexible benefits plan, called FlexChoice, gives you freedom, choice and flexibility in the way you receive your benefits, as well as giving you the opportunity to make savings where possible. As a new joiner to GE we are pleased to be able to offer you the following as default in your benefit fund, which you then can tailor to meet your individual needs;

 

* Non-contributory Pension
* Bonus
* Car allowance
* Life Assurance
* Group income protection
* Private medical cover
* Holiday Hourly equivalent of 26 days, with flexible option to buy or sell

Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS) clearance is required and must be maintained for this role. Please note that in the event that BPSS clearance cannot be obtained, you may not be eligible for the role and/or any offer of employment may be withdrawn on grounds of national security. Please see the link below for further details regarding the requirements for BPSS clearance: BPSS

Applications from job seekers who require sponsorship to work in the UK are welcome and will be considered alongside all other applications. However, under the applicable UK immigration rules as may be in place from time to time, it may be that candidates who do not currently have the right to work in the UK may not be appointed to a post if a suitably qualified, experienced and skilled candidate who does not require sponsorship is available to take up the post. For further information please visit the UK Visas and Immigration website.

GE Aerospace offers a great work environment, professional development, challenging careers, and competitive compensation. GE Aerospace is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, national or ethnic origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, disability, protected veteran status or other characteristics protected by law.

existing_roles.title: Advisor/Sr Advisor/Director – Manufacturing Science
existing_roles.description:
At Lilly, the work is demanding because patients are waiting. We unite caring with discovery to help make life better for people around the world, knowing that every decision, every detail, and every day matters. Headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana, our over 50,000 employees around the globe take on complex challenges to discover and deliver life-changing medicines, strengthen how health is understood and managed, and support the communities we serve. This is hard, urgent, selfless work—but it’s work worth doing. If you’re driven by purpose and ready to bring your best to work that truly matters for patients, we invite you to join us.
 
 
Company Overview
 
At Lilly, we unite caring with discovery to make life better for people around the world. We are a global healthcare leader headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana. Our employees around the world work to discover and bring life-changing medicines to those who need them, improve the understanding and management of disease, and give back to our communities through philanthropy and volunteerism. We give our best effort to our work, and we put people first. We’re looking for people who are determined to make life better for people around the world.
 
 
Position Brand Description
 
How would you like a career where you get to apply your best technical and analytical skills to bring complex, high-potency biologic medicines to patients? We are seeking a scientific leader on our Parenteral Product Network Technical Services/Manufacturing Science (TS/MS) team to drive the commercialization of lyophilized drug products, with a focus on antibody drug conjugates (ADCs), and to provide technical support for commercial lyophilized product manufacturing.
 
In this role, you are critical to the success of Lilly’s oncology and biologics portfolio. As a Global Product Steward and lyophilization process expert, you will hold technical ownership of assigned lyophilized ADC and other parenteral products from late-stage development through the commercial lifecycle, serving as the technical link between Product Development and our commercial manufacturing sites. You will ensure these products are successfully launched, reliably supplied, and technically well controlled across internal and external sites.
 
 
Responsibilities
 
As an individual contributor, you will work side by side with colleagues in Product Development, Manufacturing Operations, Quality, EHS, and Supply Chain, as well as with external manufacturing organizations. You will be a visible technical presence in cross-functional teams, mentor junior technical associates, and escalate significant technical, quality, safety, and supply risks to management with clear assessments and recommended actions.
 
 
**Key responsibilities include:** 

* Serve as Global Product Steward and subject matter expert for lyophilized, ADC and parenteral products, holding end-to-end technical accountability for process performance, product quality, and supply across all manufacturing sites, and serving as the primary technical interface between Product Development and commercial manufacturing.
* Advance lyophilization technology in commercial manufacturing
* Maintain the product technical knowledge base and lifecycle strategy, including process history, critical material and supplier knowledge, a product technical risk register, and a roadmap for yield, robustness, capacity, and site-network improvements.
* Collaborate with product development and manufacturing site for technology transfer, scale-up, process performance qualification/validation, and comparability activities (including lyophilization cycle transfer between freeze-dryers of differing scale and design) to support commercial launch readiness.
* Escalate significant technical, quality, safety, compliance, and supply risks to TS/MS management in a timely manner, providing risk assessments, impact to patients and supply, and recommended mitigation plans.
* Own the commercial control strategy for lyophilization critical process parameters and critical quality attributes, and maintain process understanding through continued process verification, stability and batch trending, and global product assessment.
* Partner with Product Development to ensure manufacturability of new ADC and lyophilized products, and to provide commercial manufacturing feedback that informs formulation, cycle design, specifications, container closure selection, and site selection.
* Author and review technical sections of global regulatory submissions, post-approval changes, and responses to regulatory questions, and support inspection readiness at commercial sites.
* Lead process improvement and lifecycle management projects, including introduction of new lyophilization, filling, and containment technologies and qualification of vials, stoppers, and other critical materials.

Basic Qualifications
 
 

* A degree in a relevant area such as Pharmaceutical Science, Chemical Engineering, Biochemistry, or Chemistry with one of the following:
* PhD degree with 5 years of practical experience in parenteral, biologic, or antibody drug conjugate drug substance or drug product development and/or manufacturing, or
* Master’s degree with 10 years of practical experience in parenteral, biologic, or antibody drug conjugate drug substance or drug product development and/or manufacturing, or
* Bachelor’s degree with 15 years of practical experience in parenteral, biologic, or antibody drug conjugate drug substance or drug product development and/or manufacturing.
* Hands-on experience with lyophilization development or manufacturing (e.g., formulation and cycle development, scale-up, tech transfer, or commercial cycle support).
* Working knowledge of protein-based and ADC drug product formulation and aseptic fill/finish processes.
* Experience supporting GMP commercial manufacturing, including technology transfer, process validation, and/or deviation investigation and resolution.

Qualified candidates must be legally authorized to be employed in the United States. Lilly does not anticipate providing sponsorship for employment visa status (e.g., H-1B or TN status) for this employment position.
 
 
Additional Skills/Preferences
 
We want you to bring your lyophilization and biologics expertise, commercial manufacturing experience, and technical influence to help launch and supply ADC and other lyophilized medicines.
 
 
**Preferred experience includes:** 

* Direct ADC drug product experience, including handling of cytotoxic or highly potent payloads and the stability and process sensitivities of conjugated antibodies.
* Background in lyophilized product development, including formulation and excipient selection, freeze-drying cycle design, and thermal characterization, and cycle scale-up.
* Analytical characterization of lyophilized biologics and ADCs
* Experience with container closure and critical material qualification, including vial and stopper selection, container closure integrity, and the interaction of materials with processing equipment.
* Product stewardship experience, such as serving as technical owner or product lead for a commercial or late-stage product, authoring annual product reviews or technical risk assessments, and managing multi-site process harmonization.
* Demonstrated leadership, influence, and problem-solving skills, including the ability to interpret complex technical data, troubleshoot manufacturing issues, and clearly escalate risks and recommendations to management.
* Preparation, review, and response to global regulatory submissions (e.g., BLAs, NDAs, or equivalent), post-approval changes, and support of regulatory inspections.

**Company Description**

Table 87 Frozen LLC is a national frozen pizza manufacturer and “The Home Of The Coal Oven Slice.” Born in Brooklyn NY, founder Thomas Cucco opened his first slice shop in Brooklyn Heights in 2012. Today, Table 87 runs three authentic coal-oven pizza shops while operating its own vertically integrated frozen production facility that ships its signature frozen pizza nationwide. After national exposure on ABC’s Shark Tank, Table 87 has scaled into top retailers and distributors across the USA, bringing authentic Brooklyn NY coal-oven pizza to freezers everywhere.

**Role Description**

The Director of Operations, Frozen is a full-time, on-site role based in Brooklyn, NY. This role will own day-to-day operations of the Frozen Production Facility and drive consistent output across all frozen manufacturing. Core responsibilities include production leadership, packaging, staffing, inventory and supply-chain optimization, logistics expertise, food-safety elevation, and full facility/equipment readiness. Our mandate is clear: take a high-growth disruptor brand’s production operation and turn it into a dominant, scalable food-manufacturing engine. Success in this role is designed to evolve into COO.

**Qualifications**

* Proven track record evolving an emerging brand into advanced, large-scale manufacturing success
* Proven blend of entrepreneurial grit and disciplined management systems

As part of the Thermo Fisher Scientific team, you’ll discover meaningful work that makes a positive impact on a global scale. As a Senior Director of Operations at Thermo Fisher Scientific, you'll manage complex manufacturing operations while driving strategic growth and operational excellence. This key leadership role involves directing production of high-quality products in regulated environments while ensuring exceptional customer service and compliance.
