B. Braun Medical Inc., a leader in infusion therapy and pain management, develops, manufactures, and markets innovative medical products and services to the healthcare industry. Other key product areas include nutrition, pharmacy admixture and compounding, ostomy and wound care, and dialysis. The company is committed to eliminating preventable treatment errors and enhancing patient, clinician and environmental safety. B. Braun Medical is headquartered in Bethlehem, Pa., and is part of the B. Braun Group of Companies in the U.S., which includes B. Braun Interventional Systems, Aesculap® and CAPS®.

Globally, the B. Braun Group of Companies employs more than 64,000 employees in 64 countries. Guided by its Sharing Expertise® philosophy, B. Braun continuously exchanges knowledge with customers, partners and clinicians to address the critical issues of improving care and lowering costs. To learn more about B. Braun Medical, visit www.bbraunusa.com

Ready to lead where science, quality, and patient safety come together? Join B. Braun and shape the future of laboratory excellence while driving the strategy, compliance, and innovation behind critical healthcare products.

**Why this role matters:**

The Director, Lab Quality Control serves as the senior site authority for Quality Control Chemistry and Microbiology, providing the scientific and operational leadership needed to protect product quality and maintain regulatory compliance. This role establishes the site’s laboratory strategy, leads critical quality initiatives, and ensures that laboratory operations remain scientifically sound, inspection-ready, and aligned with business and product portfolio requirements.

**How you will make an impact:**

* Develop, maintain, and execute the site Quality Control strategy in alignment with business objectives, product portfolio requirements, and regulatory expectations.
* Provide strategic oversight for QC Chemistry and QC Microbiology operations, including release, stability, raw material, in-process, microbiological, and sterility-related testing activities.
* Establish and govern laboratory standards for testing compliance, data integrity, investigations, sample management, analytical methods, specifications, and laboratory workflows.
* Serve as the primary site subject matter expert during regulatory inspections and customer audits involving laboratory operations and quality systems.
* Partner with Quality Assurance, Manufacturing, Sterility Assurance, Engineering, Validation, Technical Services, Supply Chain, and Regulatory Affairs to support site operations and timely product release.
* Lead laboratory optimization, method modernization, automation, Lean deployment, and quality system improvement initiatives.
* Foster a culture of quality, accountability, scientific rigor, collaboration, safety, and continuous improvement.

**What sets you up for success:**

* Bachelor’s degree in a STEM discipline required; master’s degree or doctorate preferred.
* 10+ years of related experience, including significant leadership responsibility within laboratory quality control or pharmaceutical manufacturing.
* Demonstrated expertise in QC Chemistry and/or QC Microbiology operations within a sterile drug product manufacturing environment.
* Significant experience with laboratory compliance, data integrity, out-of-specification and out-of-trend investigations, analytical methods, and pharmaceutical quality systems.
* Proven experience supporting regulatory inspections, customer audits, and interactions with senior internal and external stakeholders.
* Ability to resolve complex scientific, operational, and compliance issues using sound judgment, technical expertise, and risk-based decision-making.
* Lean Six Sigma certification or demonstrated experience applying Lean and continuous-improvement methodologies preferred.

**What you will enjoy along the way:**

* The opportunity to shape the laboratory quality strategy for a regulated sterile pharmaceutical manufacturing site.
* A highly visible leadership role with influence across Quality, Manufacturing, Technical Operations, Supply Chain, and Regulatory Affairs.
* The ability to modernize analytical capabilities through automation, method lifecycle management, Lean principles, and emerging technologies.
* Responsibility for developing laboratory leaders, building organizational capability, and determining the effective allocation of people and resources.
* Meaningful work that directly supports product quality, regulatory compliance, operational reliability, and patient safety.
* A collaborative environment built on scientific rigor, accountability, diverse perspectives, and continuous improvement.

existing_roles.title: Director, Balance of Plant
existing_roles.description:
**Company Overview**

Kairos Power is a new nuclear energy technology and engineering company whose mission is to enable the world's transition to clean energy, with the ultimate goal to dramatically improve people's quality of life while protecting the environment. This goal will be accomplished through the commercialization of the fluoride-salt-cooled, high-temperature reactor (FHR) that can be deployed with robust safety, affordable costs, and flexible operation to accommodate the expansion of variable renewables.

**Job Summary**

Kairos Power is seeking an experienced senior engineering leader to serve as Director, Balance of Plant (Power Generation System & Turbine Island), to provide strategic and technical leadership for multidisciplinary engineering teams. This role is responsible for the technical leadership, organizational capability, and execution of the engineering teams responsible for design and deployment for Structures, Systems, and Components that convert thermal energy to electricity and provide auxiliary plant functions necessary to support reliable and efficient plant operation. The ideal candidate combines broad power plant and thermal-fluid systems expertise with demonstrated success building engineering teams, working with external partners, and delivering complex, hardware systems from concept through commissioning and operation.

**Responsibilities**

* Provide strategic and technical leadership for the development and integration of balance-of-plant (BOP) Systems, such as the Heat Transport Systems interfacing with high-temperature steam Rankine cycles, Power Generation System (PGS), and auxiliary systems such as service water, treated water, and compressed air systems.
* Establish department technical direction and decision boundaries consistent with company strategy and designated technical authorities.
* Lead engineering delivery from conceptual sizing through detailed design, vendor package review, and commissioning support, owning design reviews and technical risk.
* Ensures that system and discipline leads satisfy applicable requirements, codes and standards, safety functions,and align to program
* Ensure engineering deliverables—including requirements, calculations, analyses, specifications, drawings, design reports, interface documents, and test plans—are technically sound and meet established quality and schedule requirements.
* Oversee supplier technical execution, including supplier selection, bid evaluations, equipment specifications, design reviews, technical evaluations, qualification programs, factory acceptance testing, and resolution of supplier technical issues, to ensure supplier designs and deliverables meet Kairos Power requirements.
* Oversee evaluation of BOP design and supplier changes for impacts on system interfaces, plant performance, safety, and commissioning readiness, and ensure approved changes are incorporated into the controlled technical baseline.
* Build productive relationships with external organizations while maintaining clear accountability for Kairos Power technical requirements and engineering decisions.
* Translates company strategy into measurable organizational priorities and decision principles.
* Determine and communicate explicit scope, schedule, risk, and resource tradeoffs across the organization.
* Maintain accountability for organizational outcomes and the consequences of scope, schedule, risk, and resource decisions within delegated authority, including decisions delegated to others.
* Ensure execution of strategic priorities, take corrective action when results are off track, and remove systemic barriers teams cannot resolve.
* Establish organizational technical direction and decision boundaries are established, consistent with company strategy and designated technical authorities.
* Ensure material technical and safety risk, their potential consequences, and proposed mitigations are clearly documented and communicated to the appropriate authority, with risk acceptance decisions explicitly recorded.
* Personally engage in mission-critical technical or organizational decisions, crises, external reviews, or critical deliverables when judgment materially changes the outcome.
* Build the organization and leadership pipeline required for current and future strategy, including recruitment, staffing, and leadership development.
* Hold senior leaders and technical leads accountable for team capability, succession, performance, engagement, and retention.
* Ensure systemic operational or compliance weaknesses are corrected and that improvements are sustained across the organization.
* Communicate organizational direction and tradeoffs consistently to leadership, teams, and cross-functional partners.
* Establish alignment across teams, resolve cross-functional conflicts, and escalate tradeoffs that require broader leadership decisions.
* Set the organizational tone for accountability, integrity, psychological safety, and mission stewardship, and reinforce these values through visible decisions, resource choices, recognition, and corrective action.
* Other duties as assigned.

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree or higher in Mechanical Engineering, Nuclear Engineering, Chemical Engineering, or equivalent
* 15+ years of progressively responsible engineering experience involving power generation, thermal-fluid systems, process systems, nuclear systems, or other complex industrial systems.
* 7+years of progressive engineering leadership experience managing engineering teams with multiple engineering disciplines.
* Experience managing engineering managers or technical leads with accountability for outcomes across multiple teams and work sites.
* Experience working with suppliers, OEMs, engineering contractors, or other external technical organizations.
* Experience leading technical development and qualification of major equipment through external suppliers or OEMs.
* Experience supporting construction, commissioning, startup, or operation of complex power generation or industrial facilities.

existing_roles.description:
**Position Summary:**

**The Director of Contract Manufacturing** focuses activities and resources in the organization around value creation and has responsibility for the success of the value stream. Unlike Steffes’ product-line business units, Contract Manufacturing does not own a product line; it markets and sells Steffes’ engineering and manufacturing services, building to customer designs, specifications, and requirements.

The Director of Contract Manufacturing understands key system constraints, quickly identifies critical process issues and successfully maintains key customer relationships. Has management responsibility for the strategy, relationship management, pricing and margin.

This role must have excellent business, manufacturing, and technical knowledge; as well as interpersonal skills to communicate and be an influencer, both internal and external to the organization.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Maintains responsibility for assigned business unit, including profitability, business development and budgeting.

* Develops sales and promotional strategies for Steffes’ engineering and manufacturing services within the Value Stream.

* Sets vision, defines direction, influences and inspires others, aligns and leads teams to create value and grow the business.

* Responsible for increasing and tracking contract manufacturing revenue and market share.

* Responsible for advancing key customer relationships.

* Works with other department leaders to aid in allocation of resources and capacity to achieve specific business results.

* Coaches and assists team members.

* Sets clear expectations for the customer program life cycle, from quote through production and delivery, and ensures the team understands goals and expectations.

* Identifies risks and establishes suitable actions.

* Responsible for overall customer experience and customer care.

* Maintains a deep understanding of Steffes’ engineering and production processes, capabilities, and capacity.

* Ensures accurate and timely technical reviews of customer designs, drawings, and requirements.

* Establishes pricing based on cost estimates and market value such that market share and profitability goals can be met.

* Maintains a good understanding of competing contract manufacturers and engineering service providers, including their capabilities, marketing strategies, and relative costs. Be capable of effectively communicating this information with the sales department and other functional areas.

* Works with account managers to develop strategies to sell Steffes’ engineering and manufacturing services to current and prospective customers.

* Ensures Steffes’ contract manufacturing services are competitive from the standpoint of quality, reliability, cost, lead time, and on-time shipping by calling out deficiencies and seeing proper action is initiated to correct problem areas.

* Monthly maintains financial forecasting and price reviews.

* Communicates with internal staff on a regular basis to understand their business problems and help find solutions.

* Maintains a positive work atmosphere by acting and communicating in a collaborative manner with customers, suppliers, co-workers, and management.

* Helps company meet its Strategic, Quality, and Safety objectives.

* Assists with development and execution of annual sales plans.

* Establishes and maintains guidelines for pursuing and accepting new business.

* Daily monitors shipping activity, costing and pricing to ensure sales and profitability goals are being achieved.

* Assists CFO with review of Terms & Conditions and MSA’s and negotiates with the customer to resolve differences.

* Ensures prompt and satisfactory resolution to external quality issues on customer parts and assemblies.

* Other duties may be assigned

**Job Requirements/Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Engineering or equivalent experience preferred.
* 5 years of experience working in engineering, manufacturing, marketing, or sales
* Experience selling or managing engineering and/or contract manufacturing services with customers.
* Intermediate computer knowledge (Windows, email, internet, etc.)
* Written and verbal communication skills
* Overnight travel is required occasionally

-OR-

* An acceptable combination of education and experience

**Functional & Cognitive Requirements of Position**

* This position requires walking, sitting or standing to a significant degree.
* Must have the ability to lift 50 pounds from floor to waist, carry 50 pounds, and push and/or pull up to 50 pounds.
* Must have the ability to climb ladders and/or stairs.
* Stooping, crouching, kneeling and bending.
* Handling, feeling, and gripping would be required for some activities.
* Visual acuity is required to inspect work completed.
* This role may be subject to internal and external environmental conditions.
* Learn new tasks, remember processes, maintain focus, complete tasks independently, make timely decisions in the context of a workflow, ability to communicate with visitors, ability to complete tasks in situations that have a speed or productivity quota.

**Core Values:** 
**Trust:** We promote growth and long-term success by making wise decisions with trust as an essential component. 
**Respect:** We unleash creative talents of our diverse workforce by treating each other the way we would like to be treated. 
**Teamwork**: We believe people achieve much more by working together. 
**Integrity:** We follow through and keep our word while being open, honest, ethical, and fair. 
**Safety:** We view our co-workers as family members of our business and strive to ensure safety for all. • Humility: We recognize and appreciate strengths and contributions beyond one’s self. We are modest, genuine, and authentic. 
 
**Core Expectations:** 
**Customer Service** - Demonstrate excellent customer service and display a positive attitude and behavior consistent with the Steffes Code of Conduct and Core Values. 
**Environmental, Health, Safety (EHS)** – Perform work in compliance with EHS training and identified procedures/standard work. Report any EHS incident or concern to your supervisor immediately. Cooperate and contribute to the overall success of the EHS program. 
**Quality** – Participate in job-specific training. Complete work as indicated by standard work, processes, and/or procedures. If your work can’t be completed as required, notify your supervisor immediately for guidance. 
**Conduct** - Demonstrate and support the Steffes Code of Conduct. 
**Policies and Procedures** - Demonstrate and support Steffes Policies and Procedures by: 
o Using tact, sound judgement, and maintaining a professional attitude in communication and relationships with others. 
o Striving to deliver the best quality in daily work. 
o Promoting a positive image of Steffes and its products. 
o Being timely and punctual in attendance and following all policies and procedures.

*Equal Opportunity Employer*

existing_roles.title: Director of Manufacturing Engineering, Imaging
existing_roles.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century's most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril's family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

**ABOUT THE JOB** 
 
As the Director of Manufacturing Engineering, your role encompasses the strategic oversight and tactical management of manufacturing engineering and systems to support both the development of new products and the scaling of high-volume production in Waltham, MA. You are charged with ensuring rigorous manufacturing processes are in place, resulting in the consistent delivery of superior quality products to our customers. Your leadership will also guarantee the fulfillment of manufacturing's capacity commitments while driving advancements in digital tools and methodologies to improve design, analysis, and execution. This role demands an innovative and adaptable approach to solving complex manufacturing challenges in a highly dynamic environment. 
 
**WHAT YOU'LL DO:**

* **Build & Lead the Manufacturing Engineering Team:** Recruit, mentor, and develop a high-performing team of manufacturing engineers and technical staff. Foster a culture of innovation, accountability, and continuous improvement across the organization.
* **Drive Manufacturing Strategy & Technology:** Develop and implement a long-term manufacturing engineering strategy aligned with Anduril Imaging's growth objectives. Drive adoption of automation, advanced manufacturing technologies, and digital manufacturing tools to enhance efficiency and scalability across development and high-volume production.
* **Lead New Product Introduction (NPI):** Partner with R&D and product development teams to ensure seamless transition of new products from design to production. Champion Design for Manufacturability (DfM) and Design for Assembly (DfA) principles early in the development cycle to de-risk production scaling.
* **Scale Production Capability:** Evaluate, plan, and prioritize supply chain, production, and test optimizations to ensure the value stream can reliably meet production output goals. Develop business cases for vertical integration or supplier diversification where strategic partnerships will accelerate scalability.
* **Drive Continuous Improvement & Complexity Reduction:** Lead initiatives to improve yield, reduce cycle time, and lower cost across the manufacturing value chain. Drive commonality optimization, component and supplier rationalization, and process standardization to simplify production at scale.
* **Resource & Budget Management:** Manage budgets, staffing, and capital equipment planning for the manufacturing engineering organization. Forecast headcount and operational needs to support rapid scaling, including classified production environments.

#### **REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS:**

* Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, or a related technical field; Master's degree or MBA preferred.
* 12+ years of progressive experience in manufacturing engineering and operations, with at least 5 years in a leadership role managing manufacturing engineering teams.
* Demonstrated experience owning manufacturing value chains for complex electro-mechanical or imaging hardware — defense, aerospace, or adjacent industries strongly preferred.
* Strong background in make-vs-buy analysis, contract manufacturer management, and supplier development for precision hardware.
* Experience managing NPI and scaling production in high-growth environments with condensed timelines.
* Familiarity with optical system integration and test, precision assembly, or imaging hardware manufacturing.
* Knowledge of automation, advanced manufacturing technologies, and digital manufacturing tools.
* Familiarity with quality systems (ISO 9001/AS9100) and PLM, MES, and ERP systems.
* Hands-on experience physically manufacturing hardware (assembly, soldering, machining, fabrication, etc.).
* Excellent leadership, communication, and cross-functional collaboration skills.
* Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance.

The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. Additionally, Anduril offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including:

 

### **Benefits**

At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you're supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next. *For more information,* *Explore Our Benefits**.*

 

### **Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams**

Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information.

To ensure your safety and help you navigate your job search with confidence, please keep the following critical points in mind:

* **No Financial Requests:** Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates.
* **Please always verify communications:**
 + Direct from Anduril: If you receive an email from one of our recruiters, it will *only* come from an @anduril.com address.
 + Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com.
* **Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach:** If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links.
* **What to Do If You Suspect Fraud:** Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to contact@anduril.com. Your proactive caution is invaluable in protecting your personal information and upholding the security and trustworthiness of our recruitment efforts.

### **Data Privacy**

To view Anduril's candidate data privacy policy, please visit https://anduril.com/applicant-privacy-notice/.

 

By submitting your application, you consent to Anduril Industries using a third-party service provider to conduct pre-employment risk, integrity, and due diligence screening and assessing potential risks as part of your application process. This third-party service provider provides risk-intelligence services that may include analysis of sanctions and watchlists, adverse media, public-record information, and other lawful open-source or commercial data sources. This third-party service provider does not act as a consumer reporting agency. Use of this provider helps to ensure compliance with applicable laws and protect technology, intellectual property, and organizational security.

existing_roles.title: Director, Quality
existing_roles.description:
Our mission at ŌURA is to empower every person to own their inner potential. Our award-winning products help our global community gain a deeper knowledge of their readiness, activity, and sleep quality by using their Oura Ring and its connected app. We've helped millions of people understand and improve their health by providing daily insights and practical steps to inspire healthy lifestyles.

Empowering the world starts with living our values and empowering our team. As a quickly growing company focused on helping people live healthier and happier lives, we ensure that our team members have what they need to do their best work — both in and out of the office.

We’re looking for a Director, Quality to lead quality strategy and execution across Oura’s global engineering organization and supply chain.

### **What You Will Do:**

* In this role, you will ensure that quality and reliability are designed into our products, components, suppliers, and manufacturing processes from concept through development, launch, ramp, and sustaining operations. You will lead a global team of quality professionals and partner closely with Product Development, Hardware, Software, Reliability, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Customer Experience, and external suppliers.
* You will connect customer and field needs to engineering requirements, component controls, supplier capability, manufacturing performance, and product reliability. Your team will help Oura identify risks early, make evidence-based decisions, prevent defects, and resolve complex issues with durable corrective actions.
* This is a broad, highly cross-functional leadership role for an experienced quality executive who can set strategy, develop talent, influence engineering and operations leaders, and engage deeply in both product and supply chain quality when needed.
* Set the quality strategy: Define Oura’s quality vision, operating model, standards, metrics, and priorities across product development, components, suppliers, manufacturing, reliability, and the field.
* Lead and develop a global quality organization: Build, mentor, and manage a high-performing team across product quality, component quality, supplier quality, manufacturing quality, reliability, program quality, and sustaining quality.
* Embed quality across the product lifecycle: Establish effective quality gates and decision criteria from concept and architecture through EVT, DVT, PVT, launch, ramp, and sustaining.
* Partner with engineering and product leaders: Influence product architecture, design decisions, materials, specifications, interfaces, validation plans, and manufacturability to prevent quality and reliability issues.
* Strengthen component and supplier quality: Translate product requirements into component specifications, supplier quality requirements, qualification plans, control plans, inspection strategies, and process controls. Drive supplier capability and performance across the global supply chain.
* Drive manufacturing readiness and performance: Ensure production processes are validated and controlled, with appropriate PFMEA, process capability, measurement systems, yield targets, traceability, reaction plans, and continuous improvement mechanisms.
* Lead risk-based quality planning: Establish disciplined use of DFMEA, PFMEA, reliability planning, design reviews, tolerance analysis, GR&R, SPC, DOE, and risk-based verification and validation.
* Own complex problem solving: Lead containment, failure analysis, root-cause investigation, corrective action, preventive action, and verification of effectiveness for product, component, supplier, manufacturing, reliability, and field issues.
* Build strong field-quality feedback loops: Use warranty, returns, customer support, field failure, reliability, manufacturing, and supplier data to identify systemic risks and drive improvements that reduce member impact and cost of poor quality.
* Lead launch and ramp readiness: Review product and component qualification, supplier capability, manufacturing readiness, validation evidence, yield, open risks, reliability results, and corrective actions before launch and ramp decisions.
* Govern quality-related changes: Ensure design, material, component, supplier, process, software, and manufacturing changes are evaluated for quality and reliability impact and implemented consistently through ECR/ECN and change-control processes.
* Establish a data-driven quality operating system: Define leading and lagging indicators across development, suppliers, manufacturing, and the field. Improve data quality, traceability, dashboards, and escalation mechanisms.

existing_roles.title: Head of Manufacturing Engineering (US)
existing_roles.description:
**About Genesis**
=================

We are a full-stack general-purpose robot company, born across San Francisco and Paris and bound by a single mission: to make general-purpose robots a reality, unlocking infinite physical labor for the world and freeing people for creativity, exploration, and the pursuits they love for their own sake.

We are French and American by birth and global by nature. We are backed by partners who share our vision, including Eclipse, Khosla Ventures, Bpifrance, and HSG, alongside Eric Schmidt, Xavier Niel, Daniela Rus, and Vladlen Koltun. Our people work across the Bay Area and Europe, building the engine that will teach robots to do real work in the real world. We recently unveiled Eno, our wheeled, dexterous robot powered by our GENE foundation model, and we are starting to put it to work with real customers.

**The role**
------------

We build general-purpose robots, and next year we start building them in volume. You will be the manufacturing leader who takes the robot from engineering builds to production. Our CA facility is where new products are introduced: the process is designed, the first stations are built and proven, and the technicians are trained there. Volume production runs with a manufacturing partner, on their floor or on ours with their people, and you own the process in both cases. You design how the robot gets built, you lead the engineers and technicians who prove it, and you own the quality gate that decides when a unit leaves.

This is hands-on work. You design the first station, write the first work instruction, and bring the partner's team up to our standard. What exists today: an engineering build process with our design team, a production partner, a bill of materials and a plan. What does not exist yet is the production process, and that is the job.

**What you'll do**
------------------

* Design the production process: layout and cycle time, line balancing, station and fixture design, end-of-line test and calibration, material flow.
* Capacity planning: stations, equipment, people and hours by build phase, from the first units to rate, and the plan to add capacity ahead of demand.
* Specify, source and commission fixtures, tooling and test equipment: requirements, RFQ with Supply Chain, acceptance at the vendor and on the floor.
* Own process documentation under revision control: work instructions with photos and video, PFMEA, control plans, inspection plans, SOPs; keep the manufacturing BOM aligned with the engineering BOM and run engineering changes through to the floor.
* Run the transfer from engineering builds to production: pilot builds, DFM and DFA feedback with the authority to push back, build readiness reviews at each phase gate, release to volume.
* Package the process so it can be copied: one documented set of stations, fixtures, test, instructions and training that a partner's floor can run to the same yield as ours.
* Build and lead the team: manufacturing engineers, test engineers and technicians; hiring pace, training and certification, trainer capacity, shift structure as volume grows.
* Own the quality gate: first-pass yield, defect capture, root cause (8D, SPC, DOE where it earns its keep), closed-loop feedback to engineering and suppliers; nothing ships that quality has not passed.
* Partner with Supply Chain on clear-to-build so no unit starts without a complete kit, and with the manufacturing partner so their team runs our process to our standard.
* Stand up the systems as we grow: traceability by serial, MES-lite at first, then the real thing; the weekly numbers (yield, hours per unit, cost per unit, downtime, schedule adherence) and the readout to leadership.

**What we're looking for**
--------------------------

* You have taken a complex electromechanical product from prototype through pilot to volume and designed the process yourself, not inherited it. Robots, vehicles, drones, medical devices, industrial equipment all count.
* You have transferred a process to a contract manufacturer and held them to your standard.
* Strong manufacturing engineering foundation: time studies, line balancing, capacity planning, fixture and tooling design, test strategy, PFMEA and control plans, lean and continuous improvement; CAD and GD&T fluency.
* You have hired and trained technicians, written certification criteria, and know that trained people are the real constraint on throughput.
* You have run a quality gate and held it under schedule pressure.
* You are on the floor every day and rigorous in the data.
* 8 or more years in manufacturing engineering or production, with time in a mature organization so you know what good looks like at scale, and 3 or more years leading people.
* Bonus: actuators, gearboxes or precision assemblies; PLM, MES and ERP implementation; product safety certification processes.

**Working conditions**
----------------------

Production and lab environments; travel to partner sites, up to 25%.

**Why this role**
-----------------

You build the way our robots get built, from the first station to rate, and the process and the team that do it are yours.

**How we work**
---------------

We are always looking for people who are driven to work on hard problems and want to shape what the world will look like in ten years. A few of the values that guide us:

* **Limitless ambition.** We hold ourselves to the highest bar in everything we build.
* **Relentless urgency.** Iterate faster, learn faster. Time is the denominator.
* **Type-2 Fun.** Take the work seriously, not yourself. Embrace the grind and find joy in the struggle.
* **Radical transparency.** Candid communication builds trust, and direct feedback drives growth.
* **Multiculturalism.** We come from across the world. Be curious. Meet people on their terms.
* **Team over ego.** Help others, share context, and win as a team.
* **A joyful journey.** We take pride in the craft.

existing_roles.description:
Enjoy leading in an international, cross-functional setting and elevating quality in cutting-edge tech? Excellent—here’s your chance: as Director Quality Management in the Vertical Core Power Product Line, you’ll lead a global team and own product quality for modules for key Infineon AI customers.

Help shape the backbone of AI by delivering reliable, efficient power for hyperscale data centers—driving innovation in one of the most dynamic markets of our time.

Your role 
Key responsibilities in your new role

* + **Shape, manage and develop a global quality team for power modules that is equipped to define quality and reliability plans, technical problem solving and cross functional collaboration.**
 + Be responsible for Quality **Management of the power module lifecycle for products and technologies within a very dynamic product line.**
 + Define and maintain **quality targets (corporate and department targets) out of requirements from customer and market** for existing and planned future technologies, packages, products and services
 + **Define and deploy quality targets for power modules** based on customer, market and application requirements with a strong background in power module package and assembly.
 + Ensure the **fulfillment of time and cost according to agreed qualification plans** and schedules
 + **Develop strategy for product qualification that fit business needs and company quality brand**
 + **Participate in project board reviews and make decisions on project release**
 + **Lead the qualification strategy** along the whole value chain (in house, production partner, material supplier)
 + **Conduct risk assessments** and have decision competence on risk releases under time constraints
 + Initiate and drive **continuous improvement activities** and programs
 + **Act as an interface and build bridges across different functions** i.e. R&D, Marketing, Project management, and Quality Management
 + **Support customer** quality requirements and participate to discussion with key customers
 + Partner with technical teams and operations to **address quality escalations that could affect product quality or customers.**

Your profile 
Qualifications and skills to help you succeed

 

* Achieved a **technical university degree** in Electrical Engineering, Physics, Materials Science or a comparable degree
* **10+ years of professional experience** ideallywithin the semiconductor industry, power module industry and **quality management**
* **Leadership capabilities,** +5 years of experience in leading global teams, taking full ownership and steering all parties towards common goals
* Experience with PCB **power module and module manufacturing**, and ODMs
* Advanced knowledge of **quality systems, methods, procedures and tools** (e.g. risk management, QFD, FMEA, 8D, JEDEC, AEC-Q, IPC standards etc.) and customer related processes
* In-depth knowledge of **semiconductor technologies, development and production** as well as of **logistics processes**
* Basic Knowledge of **audits, certifications, standards and process management**
* Experience in **customer communication and stakeholder management**
* **Flexibility regarding functional alignments across different continents**
* **Project Management experience** as a plus
* Experience in **power module and module manufacturing** as a plus
* **Fluent in English skills** – German or the willingness to learn it would be an additional plus

**Additional information**

Infineon Technologies is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), gender identity, national origin, ancestry, citizenship, age, physical or mental disability, legally protected medical condition, family care status, military or veteran status, marital status, domestic partner status, sexual orientation, or any other basis protected by local, state, or federal laws.

Employment at Infineon is contingent upon proof of your legal right to work in the United States under applicable law, verification of satisfactory references, successful completion of a background check and drug test, and signing all your on-boarding documents.

In some instances, if applicable, U.S. export control laws require that Infineon obtain a U.S. government export license prior to releasing technologies to certain persons. This offer is contingent upon Infineon's ability to satisfy these export control laws as related to your employment and anticipated job activities. The decision whether or not to submit and/or pursue an export license to satisfy this contingency, if applicable, shall be at Infineon's sole discretion.

Infineon Technologies takes data privacy and identity theft very seriously. As such, we do not request personally-identifiable information (PII) from applicants over the internet or electronically. Please kindly refrain from disclosing your PII electronically during the application process or to unauthorized websites that may purport to be Infineon or any of our affiliates.

**Location**

San Jose, CA, United States

existing_roles.description:
**Department:** Operations **Job Status:** Full Time

**FLSA Status:** Exempt **Reports To:** President

**Job Type:** Non-Union **Amount of Travel Required:** Occasional

**Work Schedule:** Monday – Friday

Evenings, weekends, Holidays as needed. **Positions Supervised:** Production Staff

**POSITION SUMMARY**

The Director of Manufacturing executes the company operating plan within capital and operating budget parameters. The Director of Manufacturing works with the executive leadership team to develop strategies and objectives to maximize productivity and profitability. Analyzes production trends, forecasts future requirements, solve problems, motivates & develops employees.

**ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS**

**Essential Functions Statement(s)**

 

* Improve operational efficiencies to reduce total production costs while meeting specific product volume needs
* Check and verify production records, handle questions or concerns of inventory shortages or overages and address problems with inventory control.
* Coordinate production schedules to meet sales demand. Adjust production as necessary to meet seasonal demands ahead of schedule.
* Ensure consistency in collective bargaining agreement and provide support during contract negotiations
* Effect necessary communication and motivation to staff. Monitors individual performance via observation and review of various productivity measures. Counsels and disciplines as necessary.
* Provides production required safety leadership and training and is responsible for improved safety performance
* Oversees all production planning and executing against demand signals.
* Oversees facility maintenance team, including Cap-Ex planning and execution.
* Provides input on new product development.
* Ensure compliance with all appropriate health and food safety regulations and cleanliness, including audit preparation
* Manage customer complaint process.
* OSHA, Federal and State requirements are followed with the facility and equipment.
* Attends the Executive, Senior Management, and Safety Committee Meetings
* Maintain work area in a neat, orderly and sanitary manner.
* Correctly and promptly follow specified company procedures required for the appropriate handling of all.
* Emergency Responses and Safety practices.

**POSITION QUALIFICATIONS**

**Competency Statement(s)**

* Communication, Written – Ability to communicate in writing clearly and concisely.
* Collaboration - Collaborates positively to effectively build relationships with customers and co-workers to achieve company objectives and contribute to overall organizational success. Works effectively within a diverse environment. Exhibits a positive attitude and contributes to overall team success.
* Organized – Being organized or following a systematic method of performing a task.
* Communication, Oral – Ability to communicate effectively with others using the spoken word.
* Responsible – Ability to be held accountable or answerable for one’s conduct.
* Honesty / Integrity – Ability to be truthful and be seen as credible in the workplace.
* Accountability – Ability to accept responsibility and account for his/her actions.
* Reliability – The trait of being dependable and trustworthy.
* Friendly – Ability to exhibit a cheerful demeanor toward others.
* Customer Oriented – Ability to take care of the customer’s needs while following company procedures.

**Mental Demands:**

* Ability to work under stressful conditions
* Able to interact with others with courtesy and tact
* Ability to manage and prioritize multiple projects in an organized and efficient manner
* Ability to respond to crisis situations in a calm and effective manner

The position requires talking to co-workers, customers, vendors; requires written communications to and from co-workers, customers and vendors, talking on the telephone; requires responding to written or verbal requests of co-workers, customers and vendors; requires training/giving verbal and written instructions; requires receiving verbal and written instructions; requires writing/composing written language; requires reading; requires visiting/working at other work-sites; Ability to communicate via the latest technologies required for the position.

existing_roles.description:
Formica is a name people know. Our laminate was introduced in Cincinnati more than a century ago, and our products are found in homes and businesses around the world. Today we are a global leader in building products and surface materials, and part of Broadview Holding alongside sister companies Trespa, Arpa, and Westag.

Our 1-million-square-foot Evendale site is in the middle of a transformation, and we are looking for a **Director of Manufacturing** to lead it. This is not a role for someone who wants to maintain the status quo. It is for an action-driven leader who wants to roll up their sleeves, raise the bar, and build a plant that performs at a best-in-class level and stays there.

**About the Role**

Reporting to the Vice President of Operations, the Director of Manufacturing leads day-to-day operations at Evendale, with direct accountability for health, safety and environment; quality; production; maintenance; engineering; production planning; and warehousing. You will be a key member of the Operations leadership team and the person who sets the pace for change on the floor.

**What You’ll Do**

* Lead the site’s transformation: develop and carry out the strategy and operating plan that moves Evendale to best-in-class performance
* Bring urgency and energy to the floor, and build a culture of accountability, ownership, and follow-through at every level
* Drive safety, quality, and performance to clear targets, including zero recordable injuries, 98% first-pass yield, OEE above 80%, and OTIF above 96%
* Lead Lean and continuous improvement, including 5S, visual management, Gemba walks, Kaizen, 80/20, and Six Sigma
* Build a clear maintenance strategy that keeps improving equipment reliability
* Own the annual budget, including capital projects and improvement savings
* Coach and develop leaders, and build succession plans for critical roles

**What You Bring**

* 10–15 years of progressive experience leading operations in a medium- to large-sized manufacturing organization
* A demonstrated track record of change leadership: you have lifted a site or operation, identified challenges, changed the culture, and made the results last
* Hands-on leadership across safety, quality, maintenance, and production
* Deep, practical experience with Lean manufacturing and continuous improvement
* A history of staying, building, and seeing the work through
* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, or in Business with an Operations Management focus

**Strongly preferred:** experience leading an organized labor workforce, including union contract negotiations, and a background in process manufacturing or building products.

**How You Lead**

* **Transformation leader:** You have led real change and are energized by closing the gap between where things are and where they need to be.
* **Action driver:** You turn plans into action, follow through, and expect the same from your team.
* **Direct and assertive:** You bring a clear point of view and hold it, while listening to others.
* **Constructive negotiator:** You find common ground and reach agreements without creating conflict.
* **Developer of people:** You have grown successors and build leaders who bring the same energy.

**Why Formica**

Ask people at Formica why they work here and many will tell you the answer is simple: they love the brand, the company, and the products. We are a collaborative community of independent thinkers, and we back our people with real tools for growing their careers.

We offer a competitive package, including base salary and an annual incentive opportunity, plus medical, dental, and vision coverage; a 401(k) with a company match of up to 4%, immediately vested; 15 days of PTO from your start date plus 11 paid holidays; and company-paid short-term disability and life insurance.

Candidates in Ohio and the Cincinnati region are preferred. Strong candidates from other areas are welcome.

#### **Education**

Preferred

* Bachelors or better

**Company Description**

**About AbbVie**

AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. We strive to have a remarkable impact on people's lives across several key therapeutic areas including immunology, oncology and neuroscience - and products and services in our Allergan Aesthetics portfolio. For more information about AbbVie, please visit us at www.abbvie.com. Follow @abbvie on LinkedIn, Facebook, Instagram, X and YouTube.

 **Job Description**

**New to North Carolina. Known for pursuing breakthroughs in medicine.**

**Ready to join our team?**

At AbbVie, we bring together talented people and innovative science to develop medicines that help patients. Now, we’re bringing that commitment to Durham, North Carolina, with a new manufacturing campus that will expand our ability to produce medicines and create opportunities in the Research Triangle.

The campus will integrate advanced manufacturing, laboratory technologies and AI to support the production of immunology, oncology and neuroscience medicines. The first phase will include manufacturing facilities, next-generation laboratories, a warehouse, administrative offices and employee wellness facilities.

We are now recruiting our **Project Director / Manufacturing Director, Operations as part of the core start up leadership team.**

In this role, you will provide leadership and direction for a manufacturing operation of a large site (drug substance, drug product, biologics and/or aseptic sterile fill finish) delivering multiple products, technically complex products, and in support of new product introductions, readiness for launch.

**Key Responsibilities**

 

* Partnering with the leadership team, help build and establish the site - from recruiting the key talent needed for your team to establishing operational readiness
* Create operational and financial goals, budgets and objectives for the assigned manufacturing area. Manage budget of typically $60MM or more, ensure performance levels to maximize operations.
* Apply a high level of scientific analysis and decision-making to influence the design and ongoing optimization of manufacturing processes. Provide leadership to teams when troubleshooting manufacturing issues; consults and advises cross-functional teams to ensure processes and approaches result in efficient, high quality products.
* Drive and lead the assigned manufacturing area to meet the site business strategies; accountable for operating expenses, payroll and capital expenditures for manufacturing area projects and programs.
* Guide development and implementation of business strategies to achieve budget expectations as well as drive cost reduction efforts; implement actions to adapt and transform the organization in order to meet changing business needs.
* Ensure staff members are provided training and coaching to build technical knowledge and capability.
* Responsible for synthesizing action plans, timelines and budgets for project and product goals and adjusting these plans accordingly to effectively respond to changing demands of the business.
* Develop and manage staff through hiring, managing performance, developing talent and providing clear expectations.
* Ensure all labor and equipment performance measures are met. Responsible for completing established goals, prioritizing project work and controlling and coordinating all activities and improvement efforts across manufacturing areas.
* Manage the employee relations climate to ensure that our AbbVie Way is realized and an environment exists where all employees have the opportunity to develop to their maximum potential.
* Coach managers in the organization and establish clear expectations with them and all employees regarding responsibilities, goals and behaviors and champion and model exceptional AbbVie performance and talent management practices.

 
**Qualifications** 

* Bachelor’s Degree required in a related technical field such as Chemical Engineering: advanced technical degree (Master’s or Doctorate Degree) strongly preferred
* 12+ years’ experience including: work as an individual contributor building technical expertise and proved project management skills. Progressively increased responsibility and performance as supervisor, department manager and leader of diverse teams in Operations (Manufacturing, Quality, Supply Chain, Engineering, etc.)
* 8+ years expeirence in a simiilar drug substance, drug product, biologics and/or aseptic sterile fill finish environment is required
* You will have demonstrated your ability to lead successful teams in prior roles and experience in partnering cross functionally in a GMP manufacturing environment
* Business acumen coupled with functional leadership experience is required to ensure effectiveness and high performance in a complex operation
* Travel up to 50% during the initial start up phase of the project

.

**About Mayzo, Inc.**

Since 1986, Mayzo has been a trusted global supplier of specialty chemical additives and innovative material solutions that help manufacturers create safer, more efficient, and more sustainable products. Our technologies support a wide range of industries by improving product performance, enhancing manufacturing processes, reducing waste, and lowering costs.

As a privately held company, Mayzo combines the agility and entrepreneurial spirit of a growing organization with the stability, reputation, and financial strength built over nearly four decades. Our success is driven by knowledgeable, passionate employees who are committed to solving complex customer challenges through technical expertise, innovation, and exceptional service.

At Mayzo, we believe our people are our greatest advantage. We foster a collaborative, customer-focused culture where employees are empowered to make an impact, develop professionally, and contribute to meaningful work that supports customers around the world. If you're looking to build your career with a company that values innovation, teamwork, and long-term success, we'd love to hear from you.

**About the Role**

**Department**

Operations

**Reports to**

Vice President of Global Operations

**Type**

Full-Time

**Location**

Mayzo Operations Center in Walterboro, SC

**Overview**

Mayzo is seeking an experienced Plant Manager to lead the overall performance and continuous improvement of our manufacturing facility in Walterboro, South Carolina. This hands-on leadership role oversees production, safety, quality, maintenance, inventory, shipping and receiving, and employee development. The Plant Manager will ensure products are manufactured safely, efficiently, and in accordance with company standards, customer requirements, and regulatory guidelines while fostering accountability, teamwork, and operational excellence.

This is an opportunity to join a vibrant, privately held company that combines the energy and growth of an entrepreneurial organization with the stability, brand recognition, and solid financial foundation of an established business.

**Duties and Responsibilities**

* Lead day-to-day manufacturing operations to achieve production goals, quality standards, and customer delivery expectations.
* Monitor production schedules and coordinate labor, equipment, and other resources to optimize workflow and efficiency.
* Build a strong safety culture and maintain compliance with OSHA requirements, environmental regulations, company policies, and safe work practices.
* Lead investigations involving safety incidents, quality concerns, equipment failures, and operational issues, including corrective and preventive actions.
* Ensure compliance with applicable ISO standards, quality management systems, and customer specifications.
* Drive continuous improvement initiatives focused on productivity, quality, cost reduction, production yield, and operational efficiency.
* Analyze plant performance metrics, including safety, quality, productivity, labor, inventory, equipment utilization, and financial results.
* Develop, coach, and lead supervisors and plant employees through clear expectations, regular feedback, and professional development.
* Oversee preventive maintenance programs and ensure equipment and facilities support safe, reliable, and efficient operations.
* Partner with Supply Chain, Customer Service, Sales, and Procurement to support inventory availability and on-time customer shipments.
* Develop and manage the plant operating budget and identify cost-saving opportunities without compromising safety or quality.
* Support new product introductions, process improvements, capital projects, and other business objectives.

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in engineering, chemistry, or another technical discipline required; industrial engineering or logistics is preferred.
* Minimum of 15 years of business and team management experience in the chemicals industry or a related field; small- or mid-sized company experience is preferred.
* Minimum of 10 years of experience in supply chain management, operations management, and/or product management.
* Experience with ERP systems, inventory control, warehousing, logistics, and procurement.
* Demonstrated knowledge of manufacturing safety, regulatory compliance, quality systems, budgeting, maintenance, and continuous improvement.
* Proven ability to lead teams, solve complex operational problems, manage projects, and adapt to changing priorities.

**Supervisory Responsibilities**

* Directly supervises employees within the Mayzo Operations Center.
* Recruits, hires, trains, coaches, and evaluates employees; plans and assigns work; recognizes performance; addresses concerns; and takes corrective action when appropriate.
* Carries out supervisory responsibilities in accordance with Mayzo policies and applicable laws.

**Physical Demands and Work Environment**

* Continual standing and walking, with frequent climbing, balancing, bending, stooping, kneeling, or crawling.
* Ability to lift, push, or carry items up to 25 kg (approximately 55 lb.) without assistance.
* Frequent work around fumes, airborne particles, toxic chemicals, production machinery, and loud noise with required PPE.
* Use of specialized equipment or vehicles, including forklifts and scissor lifts.

**Benefits**

* Health, dental, and vision insurance
* 401(k)
* Flexible Spending Account and Health Savings Account
* Life insurance
* Short-term and long-term disability coverage
* Paid time off

**Core Competencies**

* People leadership and employee development
* Safety, quality, and regulatory focus
* Operational and financial management
* Problem solving and sound decision-making
* Project management and execution
* Adaptability and continuous improvement
* Cross-functional communication and collaboration

*The above is intended to outline the general content and requirements for this role and should not be considered an exhaustive list of duties, responsibilities, or physical demands. Nothing in this job posting limits management’s right to assign or reassign tasks as needed. Reasonable accommodations may be provided to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.*

*Mayzo is committed to a fair, merit-based hiring process. We use inclusive job postings, standardized evaluation criteria, and bias-awareness training for hiring managers. Accommodations are available throughout the recruitment process, and our practices are regularly reviewed to support equal opportunity and a respectful, harassment-free workplace.*

Welcome to the intersection of energy and home services. At NRG, we’re all about propelling the next generation of leaders forward. We are driven by our passion to create a smarter, cleaner and more connected future. We deliver innovative solutions that make our customers’ lives easier—helping them power, protect, and intelligently manage their homes and businesses. To do this, we need creative and talented people to join our company.

We offer a dynamic work environment and a unified and inclusive culture. NRG fosters a strong sense of belonging that leads to better collaboration and business performance. Our company programs are designed to help employees develop the skills they need for success now and in the future. In everything we do, we aim to champion our employees and bring value to our customers, investors and society.

More information is available at www.nrg.com. Connect with NRG on Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn and X.

**Job Summary**
---------------

Responsible for all aspects of Plant Operation and Maintenance, including P&L responsibility. Responsible for maintaining a competent, well-trained staff. Responsible for plant safety, training, environmental compliance, policy administration and has purchasing authority for required materials and services. Maintain good relationship with customers and the community. Responsible for supporting and executing Gas Plant Strategy in a dynamic financial climate. The Aurora and Rockford Generating simple cycle peaking plants are located outside of Chicago. Aurora Generation is a 1000 MW facility operating four GE 7FAs and six GE LM 6000 natural gas-fired combustion turbines. Rockford Generation is a 540MW facility operating three Siemens V84.3A2 natural gas-fired combustion turbines. The two sites are about 70 miles apart.

**Responsibilities:**
---------------------

* Supports and emphasizes importance of safety and environmental programs and ensures regulatory compliance
* Promotes productivity and teamwork with open communication, timely decision making, and use of leadership skills to set high standards of performance, while providing the direction necessary to achieve performance
* Promotes and supports the development of technical leadership and business skills of employees to carry out responsibilities in a competitive environment
* Responsible for matrix communications to NRG management
* Provides regular feedback to employees on their performance to allow them to capitalize on their strengths and focus on opportunities for improvement
* Creates and supports an organizational culture that encourages and rewards employee involvement, innovative thinking, adaptation to change, responsible risk taking, customer focus, and continuous improvement
* Formulates appropriate strategies which support the overall NRG strategy and manages development, implementation and execution of assigned area goals, objectives, and initiatives
* Manages all business aspects of assigned area to maximize competitive position of the plant including operational performance, staff development and cost management
* Reviews organizational performance with constituents and addresses opportunities for improvement on a regular basis
* Manages, as necessary, the evaluation and selection of external service providers.
* Manages work performed by external service providers in support of organizational objectives and responsibilities
* Assigns work and holds employees accountable for their performance
* Develops and maintains professional relationships with organizations external to the plant
* Ensures that appropriate technical expertise related to assigned area of responsibility is available and provided to employees in a timely manner.
* Manages development and execution of appropriate standards, guidelines, programs, and procedures within assigned area of responsibility
* Uses and maintains technical and professional knowledge, shares that knowledge with others, and recognizes/applies new technology in a cost-effective manner
* Obtains and applies knowledge of competitive business practices in daily work activities and decision making
* Seeks and understands the organizational needs and focuses on meeting and exceeding these requirements
* Anticipates, accepts and successfully implements necessary changes in the organization and adapts to meet the new requirements
* Ensure a safe and environmentally compliant workplace
* Willing to accept accountability for own decisions, performance, and behavior, as well as the performance of assigned staff
* Must be able to effectively interface with regulatory, political, business, civic and public representatives consistent with NRG corporate objectives

**Qualifications:**
-------------------

* Minimum of Bachelors degree in an Engineering or related technical discipline, and 10 years of equivalent experience in a related technical field; or a minimum of 14 years experience in a related technical field or similar position
* Demonstrated record of successfully leading/supervising employees in a related field
* Ability to split time between both sites

**Preferred:**

* Experience with GE 7FA, LM6000 and/or Siemens V84.3A2 preferred.
* Experience with remote operations a plus. Aurora responsible for the remote operation of 8 LM6000s in Texas at 4 different sites.

**Competencies:**
-----------------

* Uses and maintains technical and professional knowledge, shares that knowledge with others, and recognizes/applies new technology in a cost effective manner
* Obtains and applies knowledge of competitive business practices in daily work activities and decision making
* Seeks and understands the customer/client’s needs and focuses on meeting and exceeding their expectations
* Anticipates and accepts changes in the organization and adapts to meet the new requirements
* Committed to making the workplace safe and environmentally sound
* Willing to accept accountability for own decisions, performance, and behavior, as well as the performance of assigned employees.

**Working Conditions:**
-----------------------

* Power plant environment.
* Requires operation of a motor vehicle; active Driver’s License.
* Work overtime and non-standard working hours as required
* Requires occasional travel outside service area
* Requires wearing personal protective safety equipment (respirators, safety glasses, hard hat, appropriate footwear, ear plugs, etc.)
* Required to work around rotating and energized equipment, hazardous materials and chemicals
* Requires standing, sitting, walking, kneeling, twisting, climbing stairs and ladders, and entering plant equipment.
* Requires operation of a personal computer
* Occasionally requires lifting as appropriate to perform duties and responsibilities

**Position Summary:**

* We are conducting a confidential search for a Plant Manager with a well-established industrial manufacturer in the Tulsa area.
* This leader will oversee a concrete production operation and have direct influence over safety, quality, production performance, and the people who make it happen.
* The company is seeking an experienced, hands-on leader who can set expectations, develop teams, and produce consistent results.

**What You Will Lead:**

* Safety first, always. Establish and maintain a proactive safety culture through field presence, training, hazard recognition, and accountability.
* Lead daily plant production, scheduling, staffing, equipment readiness, output, and on-time fulfillment.
* Own quality control and product consistency, including adherence to customer specifications and internal manufacturing standards.
* Oversee concrete manufacturing processes such as batching, reinforcement, forming and molds, casting, curing, handling, and finished-product inspection.
* Coach supervisors, leads, and hourly employees; develop talent and improve workforce performance, engagement, and accountability.
* Partner with maintenance, engineering, and logistics to reduce downtime, rework, waste, and process bottlenecks.

**What We Are Looking For:**

* Demonstrated success leading manufacturing operations with direct accountability for workplace safety, quality, production, and labor.
* Strong practical experience in concrete manufacturing is highly preferred; reinforced concrete pipe, culverts, drainage structures, manholes, inlets, vaults, or related products are especially relevant.
* Knowledge of production processes, quality inspections, equipment, maintenance coordination, and continuous improvement.
* Proven ability to lead frontline teams, strengthen supervisors, and solve operational problems on the plant floor.
* Clear communication, sound judgment, and the ability to balance production goals with uncompromising safety standards.
* Bilingual English and Spanish skills are a significant plus, but not a requirement.

**Compensation and Location:**

* Tulsa, Oklahoma area; the role requires on-site plant leadership.
* Competitive compensation commensurate with substantial operating experience. Final base salary, bonus, and benefits details will be discussed during the screening process.
* Qualified candidates outside the region are welcome to inquire; relocation is open for the right person. Assistance details are subject to confirmation.

**Interested in a Confidential Conversation:**

* If you have led safety, production, quality, and people in concrete or closely related manufacturing environment, we welcome a confidential discussion.

Pay: $130,000.00 - $200,000.00 per year

Benefits:

* 401(k)

* Flexible spending account

existing_roles.title: Plant Manager
existing_roles.description:
**What you’ll do:**
-------------------

**Lead one of Eaton’s key B-Line manufacturing operations and help position it for its next stage of growth.**

Eaton’s Global Energy Infrastructure Solutions (GEIS) division is seeking a Plant Manager to lead its **approximately 400-person, non-union manufacturing facility in Sherman, Texas**. This role offers significant leadership scope, combining ownership of plant performance and financial results with the opportunity to **develop the organization, strengthen operational capability, and influence the future direction of the site.**

Reporting to the Director of Operations, you will lead the plant’s strategy and execution while developing a strong leadership team and advancing performance across **safety, quality, delivery, productivity, and employee engagement**. For a manufacturing leader who enjoys both driving results today and building an operation for the future, this is an opportunity to make a meaningful impact at the site and across the broader business.

GEIS operates within Eaton’s global Electrical Sector, supporting customers in markets being reshaped by **electrification, energy transition, digitalization, and increasing demands for safe and reliable power infrastructure**. With more than a century of industry experience, the business is focused on accelerating growth through innovation, operational excellence, and continued investment in its global manufacturing capabilities.

**What you will need:**
-----------------------

**Essential Functions:**

* Translate business goals into a clear plant strategy, annual operating plan, and measurable priorities, with accountability for achieving the annual budget, managing costs, and delivering sustained operational and financial performance.
* Champion a proactive environmental, health, and safety culture by engaging employees in hazard identification and prevention, ensuring regulatory compliance, and reinforcing personal accountability and Eaton’s standards for ethical conduct.
* Strengthen customer satisfaction by improving product quality, on-time delivery, and productivity, aligning plant execution with customer requirements, and resolving issues that affect service and responsiveness.
* Apply the Eaton Business System and Lean/Six Sigma methods to eliminate waste, address root causes, reduce costs, and improve process reliability through disciplined problem-solving and sustained, measurable improvements.
* Build organizational capability by attracting, developing, coaching, and retaining talent, setting clear expectations, and strengthening leadership capability, employee engagement, and accountability throughout the plant.
* Align manufacturing engineering, safety, quality, supply chain, continuous improvement, HR, and finance around shared priorities, using clear communication and cross-functional collaboration to remove barriers and execute plant objectives.

**Requirements & Additional Information:**
------------------------------------------

**Required Qualifications:**

* Bachelor’s degree from an accredited university
* Minimum 10 years of progressively responsible experience in manufacturing, supply chain, finance, operational excellence, or related manufacturing support functions.

**Additional Information**

* The position will be based onsite at our Sherman, TX manufacturing plant.
* This position will offer relocation within the US.
* Legally authorized to work in the US without company sponsorship. Eaton will not consider applicants for employment, immigration sponsorship or support for this position. This means that Eaton will not support any CPT, OPT, or STEM OPT plans, F-1 to H-1B, H-1B cap registration, O-1, E-3, TN status, I-485 job portability, etc.
* Up to 10% travel is required.

All positions may require participation in video and in-person interviews as part of the hiring process. All candidates will be evaluated based on job-related competencies, and all candidates’ privacy rights and data security will be protected in accordance with applicable laws.

At Eaton, we strive to provide compensation and benefits that attract, engage, and retain the best talent. This includes competitive pay and a variety of benefit programs for eligible employees. The expected annual salary range for this role is $165000 - $242000 a year. This role is also eligible for a variable incentive program. *Please note the salary information shown above is a general guideline only. Salaries are based upon candidate skills, experience, and qualifications, as well as market and business considerations.*

We are committed to ensuring equal employment opportunities for all job applicants and employees. Employment decisions are based upon job-related reasons regardless of an applicant's race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, national origin, disability, marital status, genetic information, protected veteran status, or any other status protected by law.

Eaton believes in second chance employment. Qualified applicants with arrest or conviction history will be considered regardless of their arrest or conviction history, consistent with the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance, the California Fair Chance Act and other local laws.

You do not need to disclose your conviction history or participate in a background check until a conditional job offer is made to you. After making a conditional offer and running a background check, if Eaton is concerned about conviction that is directly related to the job, you will be given the chance to explain the circumstances surrounding the conviction, provide mitigating evidence, or challenge the accuracy of the background report.

To request a disability-related reasonable accommodation to assist you in your job search, application, or interview process, please call us at 1-800-836-6345 to discuss your specific need. Only accommodation requests will be accepted by this phone number.

We know that good benefit programs are important to employees and their families. Eaton provides various Health and Welfare benefits as well as Retirement benefits, and several programs that provide for paid and unpaid time away from work. Click here for more detail: Eaton Benefits Overview. Please note that specific programs and options available to an employee may depend on eligibility factors such as geographic location, date of hire, and the applicability of collective bargaining agreements.
