protected_roles.description:
**Overview**

We are seeking an experienced, results-driven **Plant Manager** to lead all daily manufacturing and facility operations. In this role, you will oversee production performance, quality standards, equipment maintenance, and environmental health and safety (EHS/OSHA) compliance. You will manage plant-level budgets, drive improvement initiatives, and build a high-performing, accountable team.

**Responsibilities**

* Provide leadership, coordination, direction and oversight of management/supervisory personnel assigned to power generation facilities.
* Review, analyze, plan, coordinate, and lead all activities within the Operations Department.
* Ensure plant availability and execution of operating and maintenance schedules in conjunction with Plant Staff. • Enforce OSHA, NERC and Environmental permit regulations, investigating accidents, and tracking safety violations.
* Improve processes to optimize asset performance.
* Direct preventive/predictive maintenance programs and coordinate major plant overhauls or planned outages to minimize downtown.
* Establish goals to provide continual improvement in operational productivity and quality.
* Facilitate operational and process engineering changes as necessary.
* Provide oversight to foster an environment that encourages employee involvement.
* Provide guidance and support to ensure safety, environmental, and regulatory compliance.
* Coordinate fulfillment of obligations to its contract counterparties and the energy markets.
* Prepare and manage annual operating and labor budgets, vendor contracts, parts inventory and cost control initiatives.
* Hire, train, schedule and evaluate plant operators, engineers and maintenance staff.
* Ensure compliance with all company standards, practices and policies.
* Oversee the administration of all computerized databases, file systems, and reporting systems for the collection and processing of plant related data.
* Perform other duties as deemed necessary by Owner and VP of Operations.

**Skills**

* A bachelor's degree in business or engineering discipline or equivalent experience preferred.
* A minimum of 10-15 years’ experience in hydroelectric, steam and/or electric power plant operations.
* A minimum of 5 years’ management experience.
* Practical knowledge of power generation systems, boilers, gas turbines, and equipment maintenance.
* Mechanical knowledge, electrical systems familiarity, and engineering troubleshooting ability; technical proficiency with plant equipment and P&IDs.
* Understanding of water and wastewater treatment, pipelines, oil and gas operations, safety regulations, and environmental compliance.
* Readiness to follow emergency response procedures and use PPE and respiratory protection correctly.

The Director of Operations, Frozen is a full-time, on-site role based in Brooklyn, NY. Core responsibilities include production leadership, packaging, staffing, inventory and supply-chain optimization, logistics expertise, food-safety elevation, and full facility/equipment readiness. * Proven blend of entrepreneurial grit and disciplined management systems

**Job Description**

As part of the Thermo Fisher Scientific team, you’ll discover meaningful work that makes a positive impact on a global scale. Join our colleagues in bringing our Mission to life every single day to enable our customers to make the world healthier, cleaner and safer. We provide our global teams with the resources needed to achieve individual career goals while helping to take science a step beyond by developing solutions for some of the world’s toughest challenges, like protecting the environment, making sure our food is safe or helping find cures for cancer.

* Must be legally authorized to work in the United States without sponsorship.
* Must be able to pass a comprehensive background check, which includes a drug screening.

As a Senior Director of Operations at Thermo Fisher Scientific, you'll manage complex manufacturing operations while driving strategic growth and operational excellence. This key leadership role involves directing production of high-quality products in regulated environments while ensuring exceptional customer service and compliance. You'll optimize end-to-end operations, implement continuous improvement initiatives, and develop high-performing teams aligned with our mission of enabling customers to make the world healthier, cleaner, and safer.

Working closely with cross-functional partners, you'll establish and execute strategic plans, drive productivity and efficiency improvements, and support a culture focused on quality, safety and customer success. This role requires strong business acumen to manage P&L responsibilities while scaling operations to meet growing demand. You'll support our PPI (Practical Process Improvement) business system and 4i values - Integrity, Intensity, Innovation and Involvement - while developing talent and building engaged, collaborative teams.

**REQUIREMENTS**:

* Preferred Fields of Study: Engineering, Chemistry, Biology, Business or related technical/scientific field
* Advanced training in continuous improvement methodologies (Six Sigma, Lean)
* Demonstrated P&L management and operational excellence experience at scale
* Strong working knowledge of cGMP, FDA, and other relevant quality/regulatory requirements
* Experience leading and developing large, multi-functional teams
* Experience implementing continuous improvement and lean manufacturing methodologies
* Strong business acumen and analytical capabilities
* Effective communication and influence skills across all organizational levels
* Ability to implement change and deliver results in matrix environments
* Experience with ERP systems and manufacturing technologies
* Strong project management capabilities
* Strategic mindset with ability to balance short and long-term priorities
* Experience in customer/client relationship management
* Strong problem-solving and decision-making abilities
* Ability to travel 50-75% as required
* Change management and transformation experience
* Cross-functional collaboration and influence skills
* Financial planning and budget management expertise

We offer competitive remuneration, annual incentive plan bonus scheme, healthcare, company 401k, and a range of employee benefits! Thermo Fisher Scientific is an EEO/Affirmative Action Employer and does not discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, protected veteran status, disability, or any other legally protected status. protected_roles.title: Director, Quality
protected_roles.description:
Our mission at ŌURA is to empower every person to own their inner potential. Our award-winning products help our global community gain a deeper knowledge of their readiness, activity, and sleep quality by using their Oura Ring and its connected app. We've helped millions of people understand and improve their health by providing daily insights and practical steps to inspire healthy lifestyles.

Empowering the world starts with living our values and empowering our team. As a quickly growing company focused on helping people live healthier and happier lives, we ensure that our team members have what they need to do their best work — both in and out of the office.

We’re looking for a Director, Quality to lead quality strategy and execution across Oura’s global engineering organization and supply chain.

### **What You Will Do:**

* In this role, you will ensure that quality and reliability are designed into our products, components, suppliers, and manufacturing processes from concept through development, launch, ramp, and sustaining operations. You will lead a global team of quality professionals and partner closely with Product Development, Hardware, Software, Reliability, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Customer Experience, and external suppliers.
* You will connect customer and field needs to engineering requirements, component controls, supplier capability, manufacturing performance, and product reliability. Your team will help Oura identify risks early, make evidence-based decisions, prevent defects, and resolve complex issues with durable corrective actions.
* This is a broad, highly cross-functional leadership role for an experienced quality executive who can set strategy, develop talent, influence engineering and operations leaders, and engage deeply in both product and supply chain quality when needed.
* Set the quality strategy: Define Oura’s quality vision, operating model, standards, metrics, and priorities across product development, components, suppliers, manufacturing, reliability, and the field.
* Lead and develop a global quality organization: Build, mentor, and manage a high-performing team across product quality, component quality, supplier quality, manufacturing quality, reliability, program quality, and sustaining quality.
* Embed quality across the product lifecycle: Establish effective quality gates and decision criteria from concept and architecture through EVT, DVT, PVT, launch, ramp, and sustaining.
* Partner with engineering and product leaders: Influence product architecture, design decisions, materials, specifications, interfaces, validation plans, and manufacturability to prevent quality and reliability issues.
* Strengthen component and supplier quality: Translate product requirements into component specifications, supplier quality requirements, qualification plans, control plans, inspection strategies, and process controls. Drive supplier capability and performance across the global supply chain.
* Drive manufacturing readiness and performance: Ensure production processes are validated and controlled, with appropriate PFMEA, process capability, measurement systems, yield targets, traceability, reaction plans, and continuous improvement mechanisms.
* Lead risk-based quality planning: Establish disciplined use of DFMEA, PFMEA, reliability planning, design reviews, tolerance analysis, GR&R, SPC, DOE, and risk-based verification and validation.
* Own complex problem solving: Lead containment, failure analysis, root-cause investigation, corrective action, preventive action, and verification of effectiveness for product, component, supplier, manufacturing, reliability, and field issues.
* Build strong field-quality feedback loops: Use warranty, returns, customer support, field failure, reliability, manufacturing, and supplier data to identify systemic risks and drive improvements that reduce member impact and cost of poor quality.
* Lead launch and ramp readiness: Review product and component qualification, supplier capability, manufacturing readiness, validation evidence, yield, open risks, reliability results, and corrective actions before launch and ramp decisions.
* Govern quality-related changes: Ensure design, material, component, supplier, process, software, and manufacturing changes are evaluated for quality and reliability impact and implemented consistently through ECR/ECN and change-control processes.
* Establish a data-driven quality operating system: Define leading and lagging indicators across development, suppliers, manufacturing, and the field. Improve data quality, traceability, dashboards, and escalation mechanisms.
* Drive continuous improvement: Reduce defects, escapes, returns, warranty claims, rework, scrap, and other sources of cost of poor quality while improving product reliability, supplier performance, and customer experience.
* Influence cross-functional decisions: Provide clear, risk-based recommendations when quality, schedule, cost, performance, capacity, and supply continuity priorities compete.
* Communicate with senior leadership: Present concise assessments of product risk, supplier and manufacturing performance, launch readiness, field quality, and improvement priorities.
* Build a culture of prevention and accountability: Make quality a shared responsibility across engineering and operations, with clear ownership for requirements, validation, supplier controls, manufacturing execution, and sustained performance.

This is a hybrid role out of our San Francisco office.

### **What you'll bring**

* 15+ years of experience in product quality, supplier quality, manufacturing quality, reliability, operations quality, or a related engineering discipline, including significant people leadership experience.
* Demonstrated success leading quality for complex, high-volume consumer electronics, wearable, medical-adjacent, or similarly reliability-sensitive products.
* Experience leading and developing teams across one or more of the following areas: product quality, component quality, supplier quality, manufacturing quality, reliability, program quality, or sustaining quality.
* A track record of establishing quality strategy, operating mechanisms, and measurable improvements from early product development through launch and sustaining.
* Strong understanding of product development, design verification and validation, component qualification, reliability engineering, supplier quality, manufacturing processes, and production ramp.
* Strong command of quality and problem-solving methods, including FMEA, 8D, CAPA, SPC, GR&R, DOE, root-cause analysis, control plans, and process capability.
* Experience using engineering, field, warranty, customer support, supplier, and manufacturing data to identify systemic risks and drive corrective action.
* Demonstrated ability to influence engineering, operations, suppliers, and executive leadership without relying solely on direct authority.
* Experience with engineering change control, supplier changes, component qualification, process validation, manufacturing readiness, or production quality improvement.
* Strong understanding of DFM/DFA, GD&T, Lean and Six Sigma principles, measurement systems, and quality management systems.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to translate complex technical risks into concise decisions and actions.
* A self-directed, pragmatic, and resilient leadership style, with a willingness to engage deeply in details while maintaining a strategic perspective.
* Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical, Electrical, Industrial, Systems, Manufacturing, or a related engineering field required; advanced degree or quality certification is a plus.
* Preferred qualifications
* Experience with both product quality and supplier or manufacturing quality, or demonstrated ability to operate effectively across both domains.
* Experience with batteries, electronics, sensors, RF systems, precision mechanics, adhesives, miniaturized assemblies, or other demanding product technologies.
* Experience leading quality for products that combine hardware, firmware, software, and cloud-enabled member experiences.
* Experience building or scaling quality management systems during rapid company growth.
* Familiarity with product safety, regulatory, compliance, traceability, and risk-management requirements relevant to wearable technology.
* Experience with supplier development, APQP, PPAP, SCAR processes, multi-source strategies, capacity expansion, or major manufacturing transitions.
* Experience working across multiple countries, engineering sites, suppliers, and manufacturing partners.

### **Nice to have:**

* HW Experience
* Global distributor teams
* grown and org

### **Benefits**

At Ōura, we care about you and your well-being. Everyone here at Ōura has a ring of their own and we are continually looking to improve employee health.

What we offer:

protected_roles.description:
**Department:** Operations **Job Status:** Full Time

**FLSA Status:** Exempt **Reports To:** President

**Job Type:** Non-Union **Amount of Travel Required:** Occasional

**Work Schedule:** Monday – Friday

Evenings, weekends, Holidays as needed. **Positions Supervised:** Production Staff

**POSITION SUMMARY**

The Director of Manufacturing executes the company operating plan within capital and operating budget parameters. The Director of Manufacturing works with the executive leadership team to develop strategies and objectives to maximize productivity and profitability. Analyzes production trends, forecasts future requirements, solve problems, motivates & develops employees.

**ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS**

**Essential Functions Statement(s)**

 

* Improve operational efficiencies to reduce total production costs while meeting specific product volume needs
* Check and verify production records, handle questions or concerns of inventory shortages or overages and address problems with inventory control.
* Coordinate production schedules to meet sales demand. Adjust production as necessary to meet seasonal demands ahead of schedule.
* Ensure consistency in collective bargaining agreement and provide support during contract negotiations
* Effect necessary communication and motivation to staff. Monitors individual performance via observation and review of various productivity measures. Counsels and disciplines as necessary.
* Provides production required safety leadership and training and is responsible for improved safety performance
* Oversees all production planning and executing against demand signals.
* Oversees facility maintenance team, including Cap-Ex planning and execution.
* Provides input on new product development.
* Ensure compliance with all appropriate health and food safety regulations and cleanliness, including audit preparation
* Manage customer complaint process.
* OSHA, Federal and State requirements are followed with the facility and equipment.
* Attends the Executive, Senior Management, and Safety Committee Meetings
* Maintain work area in a neat, orderly and sanitary manner.
* Correctly and promptly follow specified company procedures required for the appropriate handling of all.
* Emergency Responses and Safety practices.

**POSITION QUALIFICATIONS**

**Competency Statement(s)**

* Communication, Written – Ability to communicate in writing clearly and concisely.
* Collaboration - Collaborates positively to effectively build relationships with customers and co-workers to achieve company objectives and contribute to overall organizational success. Works effectively within a diverse environment. Exhibits a positive attitude and contributes to overall team success.
* Organized – Being organized or following a systematic method of performing a task.
* Communication, Oral – Ability to communicate effectively with others using the spoken word.
* Responsible – Ability to be held accountable or answerable for one’s conduct.
* Honesty / Integrity – Ability to be truthful and be seen as credible in the workplace.
* Accountability – Ability to accept responsibility and account for his/her actions.
* Reliability – The trait of being dependable and trustworthy.
* Friendly – Ability to exhibit a cheerful demeanor toward others.
* Customer Oriented – Ability to take care of the customer’s needs while following company procedures.

**Mental Demands:**

* Ability to work under stressful conditions
* Able to interact with others with courtesy and tact
* Ability to manage and prioritize multiple projects in an organized and efficient manner
* Ability to respond to crisis situations in a calm and effective manner
* Ability to complete projects on schedule

**Communication Demands:**

The position requires talking to co-workers, customers, vendors; requires written communications to and from co-workers, customers and vendors, talking on the telephone; requires responding to written or verbal requests of co-workers, customers and vendors; requires training/giving verbal and written instructions; requires receiving verbal and written instructions; requires writing/composing written language; requires reading; requires visiting/working at other work-sites; Ability to communicate via the latest technologies required for the position.

**Reasonable Accommodations Statement**

To accomplish this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform, with or without reasonable accommodation, each essential function satisfactorily. Reasonable accommodations may be made to help enable qualified individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

**SKILLS & ABILITIES**

**Experience:** 10 years of progressive experience in managing Operations in a food production setting, ideally coffee. Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) safety rules and HACCP (Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Points) required; strong interpersonal skills with an understanding of diverse backgrounds and an emphasis on communication: training, team building, negotiation skills, interdepartmental interaction, leadership and supervision (motivation, directing) and management (planning, budgeting, projecting revenues, analyzing trends); union labor relations, compliance with federal and state regulations,

**Education:** Bachelor’s Degree preferred

**Computer Skills:** To perform this job successfully, an individual should have basic knowledge of Microsoft

Office applications and experience using a manufacturing ERP system

**Language:** Well-developed verbal and written English communication skills.

**PHYSICAL DEMANDS**

**The physical demands described her are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.**

protected_roles.description:
**Company Description**

**About AbbVie**

AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. We strive to have a remarkable impact on people's lives across several key therapeutic areas including immunology, oncology and neuroscience - and products and services in our Allergan Aesthetics portfolio. For more information about AbbVie, please visit us at www.abbvie.com. Follow @abbvie on LinkedIn, Facebook, Instagram, X and YouTube.

 **Job Description**

**New to North Carolina. Known for pursuing breakthroughs in medicine.**

**Ready to join our team?**

At AbbVie, we bring together talented people and innovative science to develop medicines that help patients. Now, we’re bringing that commitment to Durham, North Carolina, with a new manufacturing campus that will expand our ability to produce medicines and create opportunities in the Research Triangle.

The campus will integrate advanced manufacturing, laboratory technologies and AI to support the production of immunology, oncology and neuroscience medicines. The first phase will include manufacturing facilities, next-generation laboratories, a warehouse, administrative offices and employee wellness facilities.

We are now recruiting our **Project Director / Manufacturing Director, Operations as part of the core start up leadership team.**

In this role, you will provide leadership and direction for a manufacturing operation of a large site (drug substance, drug product, biologics and/or aseptic sterile fill finish) delivering multiple products, technically complex products, and in support of new product introductions, readiness for launch.

**Key Responsibilities**

 

* Partnering with the leadership team, help build and establish the site - from recruiting the key talent needed for your team to establishing operational readiness
* Create operational and financial goals, budgets and objectives for the assigned manufacturing area. Manage budget of typically $60MM or more, ensure performance levels to maximize operations.
* Apply a high level of scientific analysis and decision-making to influence the design and ongoing optimization of manufacturing processes. Provide leadership to teams when troubleshooting manufacturing issues; consults and advises cross-functional teams to ensure processes and approaches result in efficient, high quality products.
* Drive and lead the assigned manufacturing area to meet the site business strategies; accountable for operating expenses, payroll and capital expenditures for manufacturing area projects and programs.
* Guide development and implementation of business strategies to achieve budget expectations as well as drive cost reduction efforts; implement actions to adapt and transform the organization in order to meet changing business needs.
* Ensure staff members are provided training and coaching to build technical knowledge and capability.
* Responsible for synthesizing action plans, timelines and budgets for project and product goals and adjusting these plans accordingly to effectively respond to changing demands of the business.
* Develop and manage staff through hiring, managing performance, developing talent and providing clear expectations.
* Ensure all labor and equipment performance measures are met. Responsible for completing established goals, prioritizing project work and controlling and coordinating all activities and improvement efforts across manufacturing areas.
* Manage the employee relations climate to ensure that our AbbVie Way is realized and an environment exists where all employees have the opportunity to develop to their maximum potential.
* Coach managers in the organization and establish clear expectations with them and all employees regarding responsibilities, goals and behaviors and champion and model exceptional AbbVie performance and talent management practices.

 
**Qualifications** 

* Bachelor’s Degree required in a related technical field such as Chemical Engineering: advanced technical degree (Master’s or Doctorate Degree) strongly preferred
* 12+ years’ experience including: work as an individual contributor building technical expertise and proved project management skills. Progressively increased responsibility and performance as supervisor, department manager and leader of diverse teams in Operations (Manufacturing, Quality, Supply Chain, Engineering, etc.)
* 8+ years expeirence in a simiilar drug substance, drug product, biologics and/or aseptic sterile fill finish environment is required
* You will have demonstrated your ability to lead successful teams in prior roles and experience in partnering cross functionally in a GMP manufacturing environment
* Business acumen coupled with functional leadership experience is required to ensure effectiveness and high performance in a complex operation
* Travel up to 50% during the initial start up phase of the project

.

 **Additional Information**

Applicable only to applicants applying to a position in any location with pay disclosure requirements under state or local law:

* The compensation range described below is the range of possible base pay compensation that the Company believes in good faith it will pay for this role at the time of this posting based on the job grade for this position. Individual compensation paid within this range will depend on many factors including geographic location, and we may ultimately pay more or less than the posted range. This range may be modified in the future.
* We offer a comprehensive package of benefits including paid time off (vacation, holidays, sick), medical/dental/vision insurance and 401(k) to eligible employees.
* This job is eligible to participate in our long-term incentive programs.

Note: No amount of pay is considered to be wages or compensation until such amount is earned, vested, and determinable. The amount and availability of any bonus, commission, incentive, benefits, or any other form of compensation and benefits that are allocable to a particular employee remains in the Company's sole and absolute discretion unless and until paid and may be modified at the Company’s sole and absolute discretion, consistent with applicable law.

The Plant Manager is responsible for the management, planning, and coordination of all precast manufacturing operations to meet DVP business goals, while providing leadership to all plant and yard personnel.

* Track and manage the inventory levels of finished goods
* Oversee and manage all incoming materials to ensure adequate inventory levels are met
* Continually collect and review data to reduce inefficiencies and waste
* Successfully hire, supervise, train, and retain production/yard staff
* Evaluate and review employee’s performance for the purpose of determining skill level and training needs
* Coach and mentor employees to allow for increased responsibilities and career advancement. Lead by example.

**Physical Requirements:**

Plant Manager – Level 3 Water Treatment PlantNorth Greene Utilities (NGU)Baileyton, Tennessee

North Greene Utilities is seeking a certified Level 3 Water Treatment Plant Manager to lead operations at our Level 3 water treatment production plant in Baileyton Tennessee. This is a key leadership role responsible for the full management of plant functions, regulatory compliance, and a small team of operators.

Position Overview

The Plant Manager oversees all day-to-day and long-term operations of NGU’s Level 3 water treatment plant. The position ensures continuous production of safe, high-quality water that meets or exceeds all Tennessee Department of Environment and Conservation (TDEC) and U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) standards and guidance. The manager supervises, mentors, and develops a team of three subordinates while maintaining efficient, safe, and compliant plant operations.

Key Responsibilities

* Manage all plant functions and treatment processes to meet TDEC and EPA regulatory requirements and policy guidance.• Supervise, mentor, and train three subordinates. Two subordinates are expected to achieve Level 1 certification by mid-2027.• Develop, implement, and manage shift schedules to ensure continuous, reliable plant coverage.• Ensure compliance with all federal and state safety regulations and NGU safety protocols.• Conduct lifecycle and operational management of treatment infrastructure, including maintenance planning and capital needs.• Participate in daily stand-up meetings with the NGU management team.• Assist with HR requirements for subordinates, including ensuring compliance with company policies.• Monitor the health and welfare of subordinates.• Conduct biannual performance counseling for subordinates.• Demonstrate flexibility and adaptability to evolving operational requirements and tasks as directed by the Operations Supervisor and General Manager.• Maintain accurate records, reporting, and documentation required for regulatory compliance and internal management.

Qualifications

* Current Tennessee Level 3 Water Treatment Operator certification (required).• Proven experience in water treatment plant operations, preferably in a leadership or supervisory role.• Strong knowledge of TDEC and EPA drinking water regulations, treatment processes, and compliance requirements.• Ability to supervise, train, and develop staff.• Valid driver’s license and ability to meet any additional job-related certifications or requirements (e.g., safety, drug and alcohol screening).• Excellent communication, organizational, and problem-solving skills.• Commitment to safety, regulatory compliance, and continuous improvement.

Compensation and Benefits

NGU offers very competitive wages, an IRA, health insurance, and dental coverage. Additional details on pay and benefits will be discussed with qualified candidates.

How to Apply

Interested candidates should submit a resume, copy of current Level 3 certification, and contact information to .

For questions, contact the office at 423-234-3145.

Choosing where to start and grow your career has a major impact on your professional and personal life, so it’s equally important you know that the company that you choose to work at, and its leaders, will support and guide you. protected_roles.title: Sr. Manager, Flight Coordination Quality & Tr
protected_roles.description:
**Title Options:** Flight Coordination Quality & Training Manager

**Location:** Remote, US

**Reports to:** VP of Flight Coordination

**Hours:** Monday – Friday 8:30 am – 5:30 pm

**Position Summary**

The **Flight Coordination Quality & Training Manager** represents a quality-control and workforce-development function similar to those found in high-performing contact centers and service-delivery organizations. The role ensures every incoming lead, whether received by phone, web form, chat, or referral, is responded to promptly, handled consistently, accurately qualified, fully documented, and advanced through the appropriate next step. Through quality assurance, coaching, training, performance analytics, workflow oversight, and cross-functional coordination, this role strengthens Flight Coordinator performance while protecting the patient and partner experience from first contact through flight execution

This is a hands-on leadership role responsible for continuously reviewing lead interactions, identifying performance and process gaps, and translating findings into targeted coaching, training, and development initiatives. The individual reviews call recordings, chats, web submissions, referral activity, CRM records, follow-up activity, and department handoffs to identify quality risks before they affect a patient, referring facility, payer, partner, or flight outcome.

**How this role impacts our mission**

Every day, families, healthcare providers, and case managers rely on our team to help navigate complex situations and coordinate critical air medical transportation. As the nation's largest fixed-wing air ambulance operator, our mission is to make those moments easier through compassionate, expert air medical transportation, connecting patients with the care they need and getting them to that destination.

The Flight Coordination team is often the first point of contact, serving as a trusted guide through a time-sensitive and highly emotional process. As the FC Quality & Training Manager, you will strengthen team performance through coaching, training, quality oversight, and continuous improvement – helping Flight Coordinators build the skills and confidence to deliver compassionate, accurate, and professional service while advancing opportunities efficiently and supporting patients throughout their journey.

This is an opportunity to shape the experience of both our team members and the families we serve. By improving quality, readiness, and operational consistency, you will help ensure that every patient, provider, and referral partner receives the highest level of care and support throughout their journey.

**Core ownership**

Own quality control across every inbound lead channel and protect forward movement through two distinct stages: (1) incoming lead to qualified opportunity and (2) active opportunity to completed flight or a fully documented, supportable lost outcome.

**Essential Responsibilities**

**1. Intake Quality & Opportunity Readiness**

* Monitor incoming inquiry channels, queues, assignment, and response times to ensure every viable inquiry is acknowledged and actively worked within established service expectations.
* Review calls and transcripts for discovery, active listening, empathy, urgency recognition, value communication, objection handling, qualification, closing language, and clear next steps.
* Audit whether Flight Coordinators appropriately advance, nurture, close, or disqualify inquiries.

* Review inquiries marked false, invalid, duplicate, unqualified, or closed-lost. Challenge, reopen, or escalate records when the disposition is unsupported or a viable opportunity may have been missed.
* Identify conversion and process gaps by coordinator, source, payer type, referral source, service type, call scenario, shift, and funnel stage.
* Maintain a standardized intake-quality scorecard and documented expectations for what strong performance looks like.

**2. Flight Readiness & Coordination Oversight**

* Serves as a cross-departmental liaison with Clinical Operations and Revenue Cycle Management to confirm required clinical reviews, financial clearance, authorizations, documentation, and follow-through are progressing on time and that each opportunity is fully prepared to fly.
* Monitor active opportunities until they become completed flights or reach a documented and supportable lost outcome.
* Confirm each opportunity has a clear next action, responsible owner, due date, and follow-up plan.
* Audit records for required patient, clinical, financial, facility, authorization, payer, transportation, logistics, and operational information.
* Identify aging, stalled, inactive, or incomplete opportunities and intervene before the flight is delayed or lost.
* Ensure follow-up continues after an inquiry is advanced to an opportunity and that ownership does not stop at the initial commitment.
* Audit documentation and coordination steps for completeness before and after handoff.
* Strong ability to identify revenue and service leakage, determine root causes, and translate findings into corrective action.

**Quality Review, Coaching & Development**

* Establish and maintain a consistent review methodology across inbound calls, outbound follow-up, quote conversations, high-urgency inquiries, lost-flight interactions, and other priority scenarios.
* Conduct recurring one-on-one coaching using specific examples from calls, transcripts, records, and workflow activity.
* Create documented coaching plans with clear behaviors, actions, due dates, and follow-up review.
* Recognize strong performance and share repeatable best practices across the team.
* Measure whether coaching produces sustained improvement and escalate recurring quality or workflow concerns to Flight Coordination leadership.
* Partner with leaders on focused development plans when additional support or accountability is needed.

**4. Training & Team Readiness**

* Translate quality findings into targeted training, refreshers, job aids, talk tracks, checklists, and scenario-based exercises.

* Identify recurring themes that require team-wide training rather than individual coaching.
* Coordinate subject-matter input from Revenue Cycle Management, Clinical Operations, Logistics, and other operational partners.
* Maintain current process guidance and a centralized source of truth for Flight Coordination expectations.
* Support new-hire onboarding, readiness reviews, and ongoing proficiency checks.
* Track training completion, understanding, and sustained application on the job.

**5. Cross-Functional Handoff Quality**

* Serve as the primary quality liaison between Flight Coordination and departments receiving or supporting active opportunities.
* Establish clear handoff reuirements, ownership expectations, and acceptance criteria with partner departments.
* Audit documentation and coordination steps for completeness before and after handoff.
* Strong ability to identify revenue and service leakage, determine root causes, and translate findings into corrective action.

**What you’ll do.**

As the Senior Manager, Quality Improvement, you’ll help neurologists put evidence into practice by managing the processes that support clinical practice guidelines, evidence-based publications, and resources. You’ll advance the AAN’s strategic objectives by supporting the development of timely, evidence-based clinical guidelines, editorial and dissemination strategies, and meaningful resources that engage neurologists in improving their practice. Working across divisions, you’ll connect clinical practice and quality efforts to deliver value for AAN members.

**Please review the attached job description for full details. If viewing from an external site, please visit** **https://www.aan.com/about-the-aan/work-at-the-aan****.**

**Who we are.**

Join a diverse community of fun, energetic, and dedicated employees and members who are committed to supporting neurologists worldwide in providing exceptional care to their patients. The AAN's vision is to be indispensable to our members, and we continue to embrace our values of Community, Leadership, Well-being and Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion. Together, we pursue our mission to enhance member career fulfillment and promote brain health for all.

The AAN, founded in Minneapolis in 1948, supports and represents more than 44,000 neurologists and neuroscience professionals worldwide who provide crucial patient care, seek new cures and treatments for brain disease and work to ensure patient access to the right care. Our headquarters is in a stunning, energy-efficient office, located in downtown Minneapolis’s dynamic Mill District, and our public policy office is near the action on Capitol Hill in Washington, DC. Both locations offer easy access to light rail, major bus lines, parking options, walking/biking paths, and a myriad of dining and entertainment choices, making it a vibrant hub for everyone.

**What we look for.**

**Education:**

* Bachelor's degree in Public Health, Health Care Management, Health Sciences, Nursing, or related field

**Experience:**

* Minimum of 5 years of related experience in healthcare management and quality improvement
* Minimum of 3 years of supervisory experience
* Minimum of 3 years of project management experience
* Demonstrated ability to uphold the AAN’s values
* Demonstrated ability to supervise a team in a fast-paced environment and nurture individual career development and growth
* Ability to provide clear instructions and successful presentations to staff, work groups and panels
* Demonstrated skill, tact, diplomacy, confidentiality, and professionalism in interactions with teams, members, and other relevant individuals or groups
* Demonstrated proficiency using MS Office for word, spreadsheet, and presentations
* Excellent time management skills, ability to deliver results when facing multiple projects with tight deadlines
* Advanced knowledge of evidence-based medicine and clinical practice guideline development is preferred
* Knowledge of established evidence grading, and recommendation-development methods, such as GRADE or comparable frameworks is preferred
* Experience leading multidisciplinary teams and physician or subject-matter expert panels through complex evidence-based projects is preferred
* Demonstrated experience providing strategic and operational leadership for multiple concurrent, multi-year programs or projects is preferred
* Experience identifying and implementing process improvements, technology, or emerging approaches is preferred

*Relevant education and/or experience exceeding the required qualifications may be substituted on a year-for-year basis.*

**Travel Requirements:** Minimal travel required – up to 5%

**Location:** Minneapolis, MN and is identified as hybrid (required to work in the office with the ability to work remotely part of the week)

**Schedule:** Occasional evening and weekends required

**What we offer.**

 + Generous PTO & holidays
 + Comprehensive wellness programs
 + Paid parental, family, and bereavement leave
* **Benefits to Secure Your Future**
 + Competitive salary & incentive program
 + 10.5% 401(k) contribution & financial planning resources

* **Benefits to Grow With Us**
 + Tuition reimbursement
 + Professional development opportunities
 + Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion training programs

* **Feel Recognized & Connected (Culture & Community)**
 + Employee awards & peer recognition to celebrate excellence
 + Team-building events & company celebrations to foster connections
 + Diversity, Equity & Inclusion initiatives to create a culture where everyone belongs
 + Volunteer days & charitable giving programs to make an impact beyond the workplace
* **Health & Happiness (Medical, Dental, Vision & More)**
 + Comprehensive health coverage with medical, dental, and vision plans
 + Telemedicine & mental health resources for accessible care
 + Onsite workout facility, gender-neutral restroom, wellness and lactation rooms
 + Transportation subsidy

**Great Location:** Our headquarters is a beautiful, energy-efficient office in Minneapolis, MN. Our headquarters is in a stunning, energy-efficient office, located in downtown Minneapolis’s dynamic Mill District, and our public policy office is near the action on Capitol Hill in Washington, DC. Both locations offer easy access to light rail, major bus lines, parking options, walking/biking paths, and a myriad of dining and entertainment choices, making it a vibrant hub for everyone.

**Great People in Great Careers:** The AAN offers talent opportunities in the fields of Administration, Accounting, Marketing, Communications, Digital Development, Event Planning, Social Media, Research, Health Policy, Information Systems, Project Management, and more.

**ADDITIONAL RESOURCES**

View our press room, conferences, world-renowned guidelines, social media channels, patient and caregiver magazine, and most recent Annual Report.

**Since 1869, we've connected people through food they love. We’re proud to be stewards of amazing brands that people trust. Our portfolio includes the iconic Campbell’s brand, as well as Cape Cod, Chunky, Goldfish, Kettle Brand, Lance, Late July, Pacific Foods, Pepperidge Farm, Prego, Pace, Rao’s Homemade, Snack Factory, Snyder’s of Hanover. Swanson, and V8.**

**Here, you will make a difference every day. You will be supported to build a rewarding career with opportunities to grow, innovate and inspire. Make history with us.**

**Why Campbell’s…**

* Benefits begin on day one and include medical, dental, short and long-term disability, AD&D, and life insurance (for individual, families, and domestic partners).
* Employees are eligible for our matching 401(k) plan and can enroll on the first day of employment with immediate vesting.
* Campbell’s offers unlimited sick time along with paid time off and holiday pay.
* If in WHQ – free access to the fitness center. Access to on-site day care (operated by Bright Horizons) and company store.
* Giving back to the communities where our employees work and live is very important to Campbell’s. Our “Campbell’s Cares” program matches employee donations and/or volunteer activity up to $1,500 annually.
* Campbell’s has a variety of Employee Resource Groups (ERGs) to support employees.

**Sr. Director, Supply Quality and Warehouse and Distribution Quality**

The Sr. Director, Supply Quality and Warehouse and Distribution Quality is responsible for leading a comprehensive supply quality, warehouse quality, and distribution quality program across ingredients, packaging, suppliers, warehouses, distributors, and external partners. This role partners closely with Quality, Procurement, Supply Chain, R&D, Regulatory, Legal, plant operations, warehouse and distribution teams, suppliers, brokers, distributors, customers, and third parties to drive quality, compliance, supply continuity, and execution excellence. The director establishes and executes strategy, strengthens governance and systems, leverages data and digital tools to proactively manage risk, serves as a key customer interface, and owns critical customer quality relationships to build trust, resolve issues, and deliver on customer, consumer, brand, and business expectations.

 

**What you will do…**

* Strategic Leadership: Define, communicate, and execute the supply quality and warehouse and distribution quality strategy, roadmap, objectives, and programs across the supply network. Lead with a systems-thinking approach to prioritize risk, align resources, and drive measurable results.
* Category and Network Oversight: Provide leadership across ingredient, packaging, supplier, warehouse, and distributor categories, applying deep quality expertise to materials, storage, handling, processes, and network performance.
* Standards and Systems Management: Establish, interpret, communicate, and strengthen policies, standards, procedures, specifications, verification, and validation processes to ensure consistent execution of warehouse, distribution, regulatory, and quality expectations.
* Risk and Compliance Leadership: Identify, assess, and mitigate quality, regulatory, operational, and reputational risks across the supply base, warehouse network, and distribution network. Oversee risk assessments, ratings, audits, compliance, nonconformances, and business continuity actions.
* Audit and Verification Oversight: Lead audit strategy and governance, including planning, auditor capability development, execution oversight, corrective action follow-up, and continuous improvement of supplier, warehouse, and distributor verification programs.
* Performance Management and Analytics: Lead the use of metrics, data analytics, digital tools, and AI-enabled insights to monitor supplier, warehouse, and distributor performance, identify trends, accelerate decision-making, and improve accountability, transparency, and consistency.
* Supplier, Warehouse, and Distributor Performance: Oversee relationship management, improvement initiatives, contract and performance reviews, and resource deployment to improve quality, compliance, and service outcomes across the network.
* Regulatory and Industry Leadership: Apply deep knowledge of applicable regulations and industry expectations to guide program design, ensure compliance, and influence best-in-class execution across the supply, warehouse, and distribution network.
* Customer Interface and Relationship Ownership: Serve as a key customer interface for quality-related matters and own strategic customer relationships. Build credibility and trust, lead quality discussions, respond to customer concerns, align on expectations, and drive effective resolution of quality, compliance, and service issues.
* Cross-Functional and Enterprise Collaboration: Partner across supply chain, quality, regulatory, legal, R&D, operations, and external stakeholders to align priorities, influence change, and deliver integrated solutions that protect the business and strengthen performance.
* People and Resource Leadership: Lead, coach, and develop talent while overseeing internal, supplier, and third-party resources. Build a high-performing team environment focused on accountability, capability building, and continuous improvement.
Benchmarking and Continuous Improvement: Benchmark internal and external best practices, incorporate learnings into systems and processes, and drive future-ready capabilities across supply quality and warehouse and distribution quality. 

 

**Who you will work with…**

Collaborate closely with Quality, Procurement, Supply Chain, R&D, Legal, Regulatory, plant operations, warehouse and distribution teams, suppliers, distributors, brokers, customers, and third-party partners.

 

**What you bring to the table… (Must Have)**

* Bachelor’s degree required; advanced degree in a relevant field preferred.
* 10+ years of progressive quality, supply quality, warehouse quality, or distribution quality management experience in food manufacturing, consumer products, logistics, or a related industry.
* Demonstrated leadership in supplier quality, warehouse and distribution quality systems, regulatory compliance, and cross-functional program management.
* Strong capability in risk assessment, strategic planning, stakeholder influence, data-driven decision-making, and leading through complexity.
* Experience leading teams, developing talent, and managing external partners and third-party resources.
Ability to travel up to 50% depending on business, audit, and project needs.

**POSITION Description**

**Manager/Director of Quality**

**Title:** Manager/Director of Quality

**Location:** Rochester, NY

**Company:** EvolvOptic is a leading supplier of precision machined optical blanks. We are shaping the future together with our collaborators and customers. We are growing our capacity and capabilities for blank manufacturing. The same experienced team that made our company a respected leader in our field remains on the frontlines, keeping production humming and delivering an array of high-quality components. We are proud and honored to be a partner to our customers for their optical component needs providing best-value solutions to meet their priorities, including cost, schedule, and assured quality.

The forecast for the future is bright. We are expanding into large, complex optical components by pulling together the right team, the right technology, and the right methods to provide best-value solutions to ground-based and space-based imaging, semiconductor industry, and high energy optics, such as laser fusion and directed energy.

**Position Summary**

The Manager/ Director of Quality is a senior leadership position responsible for developing and executing EvolvOptic's quality strategy and ensuring the highest standards of product quality, measurement integrity, and operational excellence across the organization. Reporting directly to the President, this role provides strategic and technical leadership for quality assurance and compliance.

**Leadership Expectations**

Serve as a member of the executive leadership team, driving a culture of quality, accountability, continuous improvement, and customer satisfaction while enabling EvolvOptic's growth in commercial space, aerospace, defense, semiconductor, and scientific optics markets.

**Primary Responsibilities**

* Develop and execute the company's quality strategy aligned with business objectives.
* Provide executive leadership for Quality, Inspection, Calibration and Compliance functions.
* Lead and continuously improve the QMS and all audit activities.
* Establish quality KPIs and drive CAPA, root cause analysis, and operational excellence.
* Lead supplier quality and serve as the senior customer quality interface.
* Support proposals, NPI, program execution, and manufacturing readiness reviews.
* Build and mentor a high-performing Quality organization.

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in a relevant engineering or scientific discipline; advanced degree preferred.
* 10+ years of progressive quality, metrology, or manufacturing leadership experience.
* 5+ years in a management or director-level leadership role.
* Experience in precision optics, aerospace, defense, semiconductor, or scientific instrumentation preferred.
* Strong knowledge of optical manufacturing, advanced metrology, ISO 9001, AS9100, SPC, MSA, FMEA, and GD&T.

**Key Competencies**

* Technical credibility with engineers and manufacturing teams
* Strong organizational and prioritization skills
* Clear, concise written and verbal communication
* Risk-driven decision making
* Adaptability and comfort with ambiguity

This position is subject to US export control laws, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) and the Export Administration Regulations (EAR), which require US person status. A “US person” is defined by these regulations as a US citizen, US lawful permanent resident (i.e., “green card holder”), political asylee, or refugee.

All employees must also be legally authorized to work in the United States. Verification of employment eligibility will be required consistent with federal law (Form I-9). Export control assessments are conducted separately to ensure compliance with ITAR/EAR.

EvolvOptic is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of any legally protected status or characteristic protected by state or federal law.

* 401(k)
* 401(k) matching
* Dental insurance
* Health insurance
* Health savings account
* Life insurance
* Paid time off
* Vision insurance

protected_roles.title: Director, Commercial Operations and Asset Management
protected_roles.description:
**SUMMARY:** The Director, Commercial Operations & Asset Management provides leadership over the operational execution and ongoing asset management of Rhyze’s Commercial lending platform. This role is accountable for establishing scalable, controlled processes across transaction closing, funding, participation, servicing and portfolio administration, while actively overseeing the performance, credit quality and risk profile of the commercial real estate loan portfolio.

The Director leads portfolio surveillance, borrower and property performance monitoring, covenant compliance, annual review coordination, delinquency management and the operational execution of workout and loss mitigation strategies. The position works closely with the Managing Director, Commercial; Capital Markets; and Legal, and coordinates with lead lenders, borrowers, servicing partners and participating credit unions as appropriate.

The successful candidate combines commercial real estate credit and asset management expertise with operational discipline, sound judgment, strong communication skills and a focus on scalable execution.

**DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:**

**Commercial Portfolio & Asset Management**

· Lead portfolio surveillance and risk-based monitoring of commercial real estate loans, including payment performance, DSCR, net operating income, occupancy, rent rolls, leasing, borrower liquidity, maturities and concentration exposure.

· Oversee borrower and property financial reporting, covenant testing and compliance calendars; identify reporting deficiencies, covenant breaches, emerging risks and required follow-up.

· Coordinate annual and interim credit reviews, risk-rating assessments, watchlist management and action plans, with documented findings, ownership, deadlines and management escalation.

· Oversee collateral protection requirements, including insurance, property taxes, escrows, reserves, liens, property inspections, appraisals and other third-party assessments, in coordination with Servicing and Legal.

**Special Assets & Loss Mitigation**

· Identify and escalate delinquencies, maturity or covenant defaults and deteriorating credits; coordinate borrower outreach, collection strategies and remediation plans for criticized or classified assets.

· Evaluate requests for waivers, modifications, extensions, forbearances and other accommodations; develop supporting analysis and recommendations for authorized decision-makers.

· Coordinate workout and loss mitigation activities with Commercial leadership, Legal and external counsel, including enforcement, bankruptcy or foreclosure matters when applicable.

· Prepare required participant notices and approval packages; document borrower communications, decisions, conditions and deadlines, and monitor execution and performance under approved resolution plans.

**Commercial Operations & Servicing Oversight**

· Lead day-to-day Commercial operations with clear accountability, service standards, quality controls and escalation procedures across the loan lifecycle.

· Oversee transaction closing, funding, loan boarding and post-closing administration, including conditions, documentation, milestone tracking, data transfers and outstanding exceptions.

· Coordinate with internal teams, servicing partners and Capital Markets on participation administration, payment processing, reconciliations, escrows, reserves, borrower notices, payoffs, releases and related servicing matters.

· Ensure accurate implementation and recording of approved modifications, extensions and other post-closing actions, consistent with loan documents, participation agreements, delegated authority and applicable requirements.

**Operational Excellence, Reporting & Scalability**

· Provide timely loan-level and portfolio reporting to management and participating investors, including delinquencies, covenant exceptions, watchlist activity, material credit events and remediation progress.

· Serve as a central coordinator across Commercial, Capital Markets, Finance, Legal, servicing partners, lead lenders and participating credit unions on operational and portfolio matters.

· Develop and standardize procedures, controls, checklists, templates and reporting; identify opportunities for automation, integration and improved data quality to support scalable growth.

· Establish and monitor key performance indicators, including reporting compliance, review completion, exception aging, delinquency trends, watchlist resolution and transaction cycle times.

**Other**· Responsible for effective self/workload management. Demonstrates clear written and verbal communication skills. Promotes collaboration and a positive, professional work environment. Attends all position related meetings to ensure proper communication/planning occurs.

· Performs other related duties as assigned by the Managing Director

· Complies with all company policies, procedures, and regulatory requirements.

· Care for non-public information (NPI) and ensuring that confidentiality of company, borrowers, and partner information is maintained.

· Responsible for contributing to a positive work environment and culture that represents the company values.

**QUALIFICATIONS:**

· Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Business Administration, or a related field preferred; equivalent professional experience considered.

· Minimum of 10 years of progressive experience in commercial real estate lending, commercial credit administration, loan servicing, asset management, or a related field, with demonstrated experience managing commercial loan portfolios.

· Strong understanding of the end-to-end commercial lending lifecycle, including loan documentation, closing, funding, servicing, portfolio administration, and loan participations.

· Demonstrated expertise in commercial real estate asset management, including financial statement analysis, property performance monitoring, debt service coverage, covenant compliance, collateral valuation, and credit risk assessment.

· Experience identifying and managing problem loans, including delinquencies, covenant defaults, borrower accommodations, forbearances, modifications, workouts, and loss mitigation strategies.

· Strong knowledge of commercial loan servicing practices, including payment administration, escrow and reserve management, collateral protection, and post-closing compliance.

· Demonstrated ability to evaluate portfolio performance, identify emerging credit risks, develop actionable recommendations, and effectively communicate findings to management and other stakeholders.

· Experience establishing and improving operational processes, internal controls, reporting practices, and technology-enabled workflows to support efficiency, accuracy, and scalability.

· Strong understanding of commercial lending regulatory requirements, credit policies, risk management practices, and financial institution governance.

· Proven ability to manage multiple priorities, coordinate cross-functional activities, and lead complex initiatives with a high degree of accountability and attention to detail.

· Excellent analytical, problem-solving, organizational, and communication skills, with the ability to effectively engage borrowers, lending partners, credit union executives, and internal stakeholders.

· Self-motivated, adaptable, and comfortable operating independently in an entrepreneurial, growth-oriented environment.

Pay: $165,000.00 - $185,000.00 per year

Benefits:

* 401(k)
* Dental insurance
* Flexible spending account
* Health insurance
* Health savings account
* Life insurance
* Paid time off
* Retirement plan
* Vision insurance

Work Location: Remote

protected_roles.title: NPI Director North America - Solutions
protected_roles.description:
*Join the worldwide leader in playing cards and in “play” solutions. Play is what keeps us going, and it always has been our greatest motivation. That's why we* ***live different****,* ***play different****.*

We are seeking an experienced **NPI Director North America - Solutions** to provide regional leadership for New Product Introduction across North America, covering the relevant manufacturing sites and Design Center capabilities. The role translates business and customer priorities into a coherent NPI strategy, governance model and project portfolio, ensuring that new products move from concept to stable commercialization with the required quality, cost, timing, compliance and manufacturability. The role aligns Commercial, Global Design Center, NPI, Engineering, R&D, Quality, Procurement and Manufacturing and develops the capabilities required for consistent execution across sites..

**Key Responsibilities:**

**NPI strategy and governance**

* Translate the global NPI strategy into the North American operating model, stage-gate governance, priorities and decision routines, aligned with the Global Accounts and Global Design Center Director.
* Own the North American NPI portfolio and facilitate prioritization, resource allocation, escalation and trade-off decisions across customer programs and manufacturing sites in the region.
* Implement and continuously improve common global standards, templates, performance measures and management routines for product development, prototyping, design transfer, validation and industrialization.
* Ensure early NPI and Design Center involvement in strategic customer opportunities and new product concepts.

**Portfolio delivery and industrialization**

* Oversee major and complex NPI programs from concept through commercialization and stable production handover.
* Ensure projects have clear business cases, requirements, milestones, risks, accountabilities and readiness criteria.
* Drive design-for-manufacturing, cost engineering, value engineering and manufacturability reviews before production commitment.
* Ensure product concepts are technically feasible, compliant, financially viable and transferable across the relevant North American manufacturing network, while ensuring effective transfer to or from other regions when required.
* Lead executive-level reviews of portfolio status, critical risks, capacity constraints and recovery plans.

**Cross-functional and customer leadership**

* Act as the senior NPI interface for strategic customer programs and align customer expectations with operational capabilities.
* Build strong collaboration across Commercial, Business Development, Design, Engineering, R&D, Quality, Procurement, Supply Chain and Manufacturing.
* Coordinate North American and global resources to resolve cross-functional issues and accelerate decision making.
* Promote disciplined change control and transparent communication throughout the development and industrialization process.

**Capability and team leadership**

* Lead, coach and develop the North American NPI organization with teams in Seattle, Dallas and East-Longmeadow, including regional managers, project leaders and specialist resources.
* Build project management, product industrialization, risk management and technical problem-solving capabilities.
* Contribute to global communities of practice and promote best-practice sharing across North American sites and with other regions.
* Foster a culture of customer focus, innovation, accountability, collaboration and continuous improvement.

**Qualifications and Requirements:**

* Master’s degree in engineering, manufacturing, product development, business or a related field, or equivalent experience.
* Significant leadership experience in NPI, product development, engineering, industrialization or complex program management within a multi-site manufacturing environment.
* Demonstrated experience establishing governance, managing portfolios and leading major cross-functional product introductions.
* Strong commercial awareness and ability to balance customer value, technical feasibility, operational risk and financial performance.
* Excellent communication, influencing and decision-making skills in an international and multicultural environment.
* Fluent professional English; additional languages are an advantage. Ability to travel across North America and internationally when required.

Benefits an **NPI Director North America – Solutions** can expect from Cartamundi:

* Competitive pay
* Climate controlled facility
* 401(k) with company match
* Health, dental, and vision insurance starting day one
* HSA (Health Savings Account) and FSA (Flexible Savings Account)
* Life insurance
* Short-Term and Long-Term Disability
* Paid time off
* Tuition reimbursement
* Employee discounts on daycare, gym memberships, travel, and much more

**Apply today and discover the magic of making a difference at Cartamundi!**

*Cartamundi does not discriminate based on race, sex, color, religion, age, national origin, marital status, disability, veteran status, genetic information, sexual orientation, gender identity or any other reason prohibited by law in provision of employment opportunities.* *This employer participates in E-Verify and will provide the federal government with your Form I-9 information to confirm that you are authorized to work in the U.S. For more information on E-Verify, or if you believe that your employer has violated its E-Verify responsibilities, please contact DHS* *dhs.gov/e-verify**.*

*Candidates must be 18 years old to work for Cartamundi.*

*No agencies please. No sponsorship available.*

**About Cartamundi:**

At Cartamundi, we're all united by our common belief that world is better with play. Play is what keeps us going, and it always has been our greatest motivation. That's why we live different and play different. To us, it is not just an activity. It is a guiding mindset that reminds us to have fun, to be fair, to connect with people – across cultures and generations – and to embrace shared experiences.

We are a worldwide leader in playing cards and in “play” solutions.

Our owned brand portfolio includes a suite of heritage brands which go back as far as 1848, including global brands like Bicycle®, HRO®, Bee®, Copag®, Shuffle® and many locally loved brands. These brands combine craftsmanship with innovation as the basis for their continued relevance and positive contribution to the local communities that love and use these brands.

At Cartamundi, we have significant expertise in printing; our presses have been running since 1765. Today, our company has become the largest playing cards and board game manufacturer in the world and the trusted partner of leading toy companies. We make well-known brands such as Monopoly®, Uno®, Magic: The Gathering®, Guess Who ®, Pokémon®, Trivial Pursuit® every day.

As we look into the future and how entertainment evolves, we are bringing the digital world to the physical world and vice versa. We have a dedicated team of experts that is looking into future technologies, products, and applications that can get our consumers and communities to truly live different and play different.

We are still a family-owned company with headquarters in Belgium and have a global network of 16 manufacturing facilities, 6 design centers, 1 digital studio and 1 global R&D center

protected_roles.description:
Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit www.shield.ai. Follow Shield AI on LinkedIn, X, Instagram, and YouTube.

**Job Description**

The Head of Operational Excellence will lead operational excellence across Shield AI’s Group 3 UAV manufacturing in Frisco, TX (V-BAT) and Group 5 UAV manufacturing in Seattle, WA (X-BAT). Based in Frisco, this leader will create, deploy, and actively manage manufacturing KPIs and performance systems across both sites, embedding operating rhythms that improve accountability, visibility, and results. 
 
You will be responsible for instilling a culture of execution excellence, embedding structured problem-solving practices, and delivering measurable improvements in cost, quality, delivery, and productivity. This includes leading the development and governance of operational standards—such as visual management, 5S, and root cause analysis—while owning the manufacturing budget cycle, business rhythm, and executive reporting interface across both locations. This role partners with engineering, production, quality, and business functions to execute high-priority improvement initiatives, support V-BAT production, and establish operational excellence as X-BAT progresses through prototype and into rate production.

**Do you have the expertise and leadership to embed excellence into the fabric of autonomous defense manufacturing?**

### **What You'll Do:**
